## Docker Fundamentals

### 1. Multi-Stage Dockerfile Examples

#### Node.js Application
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile.nodejs
# Build stage
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Build application
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:18-alpine

# Add security: create non-root user
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodejs && \
    adduser -S nodejs -u 1001

WORKDIR /app

# Copy built artifacts from builder
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodejs:nodejs /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodejs:nodejs /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodejs:nodejs /app/package*.json ./

# Switch to non-root user
USER nodejs

# Expose port
EXPOSE 3000

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000/health', (r) => {process.exit(r.statusCode === 200 ? 0 : 1)})"

# Start application
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

#### Go Application
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile.go
# Build stage
FROM golang:1.21-alpine AS builder

# Install build dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache git ca-certificates tzdata

WORKDIR /build

# Copy go mod files
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Build binary with optimizations
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 \
    go build -ldflags="-w -s" -o app ./cmd/server

# Production stage - minimal image
FROM scratch

# Copy necessary files from builder
COPY --from=builder /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /etc/ssl/certs/
COPY --from=builder /usr/share/zoneinfo /usr/share/zoneinfo
COPY --from=builder /build/app /app

# Expose port
EXPOSE 8080

# Run as non-root (using numeric ID since scratch has no /etc/passwd)
USER 65534:65534

ENTRYPOINT ["/app"]
```

#### Python Application
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile.python
FROM python:3.11-slim AS builder

# Install build dependencies
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gcc && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Copy requirements
COPY requirements.txt .

# Install dependencies
RUN pip install --user --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Production stage
FROM python:3.11-slim

# Create non-root user
RUN useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash app

WORKDIR /app

# Copy dependencies from builder
COPY --from=builder /root/.local /home/app/.local

# Copy application code
COPY --chown=app:app . .

# Update PATH
ENV PATH=/home/app/.local/bin:$PATH

# Switch to non-root user
USER app

EXPOSE 8000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s \
    CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health')"

CMD ["python", "-m", "uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

### 2. Docker Compose for Local Development

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  # Frontend service
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      target: development
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - /app/node_modules
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=development
      - API_URL=http://backend:8080
    networks:
      - app-network
    depends_on:
      - backend

  # Backend service
  backend:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/app
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@postgres:5432/appdb
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
      - JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET}
    networks:
      - app-network
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 40s

  # PostgreSQL database
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=user
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=password
      - POSTGRES_DB=appdb
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./scripts/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql
    networks:
      - app-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U user -d appdb"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  # Redis cache
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    networks:
      - app-network
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes

  # Nginx reverse proxy
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/ssl:/etc/nginx/ssl:ro
    networks:
      - app-network
    depends_on:
      - frontend
      - backend

networks:
  app-network:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  postgres-data:
  redis-data:
```

## Kubernetes Objects

### 1. Namespace
```yaml
# namespace.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: production
  labels:
    name: production
    environment: prod
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: compute-quota
  namespace: production
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "100"
    requests.memory: 200Gi
    limits.cpu: "200"
    limits.memory: 400Gi
    persistentvolumeclaims: "10"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: resource-limits
  namespace: production
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "4"
      memory: 8Gi
    min:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
    type: Container
```

### 3. Deployment with Best Practices
```yaml
# deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: backend-api
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app: backend-api
    version: v1.0.0
    component: api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: backend-api
        version: v1.0.0
        component: api
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "8080"
        prometheus.io/path: "/metrics"
    spec:
      # Security context for pod
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
        fsGroup: 1000
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      
      # Service account
      serviceAccountName: backend-api-sa
      
      # Image pull secret
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: registry-credentials
      
      # Init container for migrations
      initContainers:
      - name: db-migration
        image: myapp/migrations:v1.0.0
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'migrate -path=/migrations -database=$DATABASE_URL up']
        env:
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: app-secrets
              key: DATABASE_URL
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
      
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: myapp/backend-api:v1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        
        ports:
        - name: http
          containerPort: 8080
          protocol: TCP
        - name: metrics
          containerPort: 9090
          protocol: TCP
        
        # Environment variables
        env:
        - name: PORT
          value: "8080"
        - name: LOG_LEVEL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: app-config
              key: LOG_LEVEL
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: app-secrets
              key: DATABASE_URL
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: app-secrets
              key: JWT_SECRET
        - name: POD_NAME
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.name
        - name: POD_NAMESPACE
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.namespace
        - name: POD_IP
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: status.podIP
        
        # Resource limits
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 256Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 1000m
            memory: 512Mi
        
        # Liveness probe
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/live
            port: http
            scheme: HTTP
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
          successThreshold: 1
          failureThreshold: 3
        
        # Readiness probe
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/ready
            port: http
            scheme: HTTP
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
          timeoutSeconds: 3
          successThreshold: 1
          failureThreshold: 3
        
        # Startup probe (for slow-starting applications)
        startupProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/startup
            port: http
          initialDelaySeconds: 0
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 3
          successThreshold: 1
          failureThreshold: 30
        
        # Volume mounts
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/app
          readOnly: true
        - name: cache
          mountPath: /tmp/cache
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log/app
        
        # Security context
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
      
      # Volumes
      volumes:
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: app-config
      - name: cache
        emptyDir:
          sizeLimit: 500Mi
      - name: logs
        emptyDir:
          sizeLimit: 1Gi
      
      # Affinity rules
      affinity:
        # Pod anti-affinity - spread pods across nodes
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 100
            podAffinityTerm:
              labelSelector:
                matchExpressions:
                - key: app
                  operator: In
                  values:
                  - backend-api
              topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        
        # Node affinity - prefer certain nodes
        nodeAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 1
            preference:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: node-type
                operator: In
                values:
                - application
      
      # Tolerations
      tolerations:
      - key: "app-workload"
        operator: "Equal"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      
      # Topology spread constraints
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: backend-api
```

### 4. StatefulSet for Stateful Applications
```yaml
# statefulset.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: postgres
  namespace: production
spec:
  serviceName: postgres-headless
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: postgres
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: postgres
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 999
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:15-alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 5432
          name: postgres
        env:
        - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: postgres-secret
              key: password
        - name: PGDATA
          value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/postgresql
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 1Gi
          limits:
            cpu: 2000m
            memory: 2Gi
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - pg_isready -U postgres
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - pg_isready -U postgres
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
      volumes:
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: postgres-config
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      storageClassName: fast-ssd
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi
```

### 5. Service Definitions
```yaml
# services.yaml
# ClusterIP Service (internal only)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: backend-api
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app: backend-api
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: backend-api
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
    protocol: TCP
  - name: metrics
    port: 9090
    targetPort: 9090
    protocol: TCP
  sessionAffinity: ClientIP
  sessionAffinityConfig:
    clientIP:
      timeoutSeconds: 10800
---

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres-headless
  namespace: production
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: postgres
  ports:
  - port: 5432
    targetPort: 5432
    name: postgres
---
# NodePort Service (for external access)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: frontend-nodeport
  namespace: production
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: frontend
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
    nodePort: 30080
    protocol: TCP
---
# LoadBalancer Service (cloud provider)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-loadbalancer
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-cross-zone-load-balancing-enabled: "true"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: backend-api
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8080
    protocol: TCP
```

### 6. Ingress Configuration
```yaml
# ingress.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: app-ingress
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    # Nginx ingress annotations
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/force-ssl-redirect: "true"
    
    # Rate limiting
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "10"
    
    # CORS
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/enable-cors: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/cors-allow-methods: "GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/cors-allow-origin: "https://example.com"
    
    # Timeouts
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout: "300"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "300"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "300"
    
    # TLS
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-prod"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - api.example.com
    - www.example.com
    secretName: tls-secret
  rules:
  - host: api.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /api
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: backend-api
            port:
              number: 80
      - path: /health
        pathType: Exact
        backend:
          service:
            name: backend-api
            port:
              number: 80
  - host: www.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: frontend
            port:
              number: 80
```

## Networking

### 1. Network Policies
```yaml
# network-policy.yaml
# Deny all ingress traffic by default
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-ingress
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
---
# Allow frontend to backend
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: frontend-to-backend
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend-api
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: frontend
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
---
# Allow backend to database
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: backend-to-database
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: postgres
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: backend-api
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
---
# Allow ingress controller
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-ingress-controller
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: frontend
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: ingress-nginx
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 3000
---
# Allow egress to DNS and specific external services
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend-api
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  # Allow DNS
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: kube-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          k8s-app: kube-dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  # Allow external HTTPS
  - to:
    - podSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  # Allow internal services
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: postgres
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: redis
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 6379
```

## Storage

### 1. PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim
```yaml
# storage.yaml
# Storage Class
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-ssd
provisioner: kubernetes.io/aws-ebs
parameters:
  type: gp3
  iops: "3000"
  throughput: "125"
  fsType: ext4
  encrypted: "true"
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
reclaimPolicy: Retain
---
# PersistentVolume (manual provisioning)
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: manual-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data
    type: DirectoryOrCreate
---
# PersistentVolumeClaim
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: postgres-pvc
  namespace: production
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: fast-ssd
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
---
# Using PVC in a Pod
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: app-with-storage
  namespace: production
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: myapp:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /data
    - name: cache
      mountPath: /cache
    - name: config
      mountPath: /etc/config
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: postgres-pvc
  - name: cache
    emptyDir:
      medium: Memory
      sizeLimit: 1Gi
  - name: config
    configMap:
      name: app-config
      items:
      - key: app.conf
        path: app.conf
```

## Scaling

### 1. Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
```yaml
# hpa.yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: backend-api-hpa
  namespace: production
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: backend-api
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  # CPU utilization
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
  # Memory utilization
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: memory
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 80
  # Custom metrics (requires metrics server)
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: http_requests_per_second
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "1000"
  # External metrics (e.g., from Prometheus)
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: queue_depth
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            queue: main
      target:
        type: Value
        value: "100"
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
```

# Database Transactions: Complete Guide

## 1. ACID Properties

**Atomicity**: All operations succeed or all fail (no partial completion)
```sql
BEGIN;
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1;
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2;
COMMIT; -- Both happen or neither happens
```

**Consistency**: Database moves from one valid state to another
```sql
-- Constraint ensures consistency
ALTER TABLE accounts ADD CONSTRAINT positive_balance 
  CHECK (balance >= 0);
-- Transaction fails if it would violate constraint
```

**Isolation**: Concurrent transactions don't interfere
```sql
-- Transaction 1 doesn't see uncommitted changes from Transaction 2
```

**Durability**: Committed data survives crashes
```sql
COMMIT; -- Data is written to disk (WAL), survives power loss
```

---

## 2. Isolation Levels & Anomalies

### Isolation Levels (weakest to strongest)

| Level | Dirty Read | Non-Repeatable Read | Phantom Read |
|-------|-----------|---------------------|--------------|
| READ UNCOMMITTED | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| READ COMMITTED | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| REPEATABLE READ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| SERIALIZABLE | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

### Anomalies Explained

**Dirty Read**: Reading uncommitted data
```sql
-- Transaction 1
UPDATE products SET price = 50 WHERE id = 1;
-- Not committed yet

-- Transaction 2 (READ UNCOMMITTED)
SELECT price FROM products WHERE id = 1; -- Sees 50
-- T1 rolls back, T2 read invalid data
```

**Non-Repeatable Read**: Same query returns different results
```sql
-- Transaction 1
SELECT price FROM products WHERE id = 1; -- Returns 100

-- Transaction 2
UPDATE products SET price = 150 WHERE id = 1;
COMMIT;

-- Transaction 1 (still open)
SELECT price FROM products WHERE id = 1; -- Returns 150 (different!)
```

**Phantom Read**: New rows appear in range queries
```sql
-- Transaction 1
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE user_id = 5; -- Returns 10

-- Transaction 2
INSERT INTO orders (user_id, ...) VALUES (5, ...);
COMMIT;

-- Transaction 1
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE user_id = 5; -- Returns 11 (phantom!)
```

### Practical Isolation Level Choice

```sql
-- READ COMMITTED (PostgreSQL default) - good for most apps
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;

-- REPEATABLE READ - for financial transactions
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
  SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = 1;
  -- Balance won't change during transaction
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1;
COMMIT;

-- SERIALIZABLE - for critical operations
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;
  -- Transaction will fail if conflicts detected
COMMIT;
```

---

## 3. MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control)

MVCC allows readers to access old versions while writers create new versions—no blocking between readers and writers.

```sql
-- PostgreSQL MVCC example
-- Each row has hidden columns: xmin (created by transaction X) 
--                              xmax (deleted by transaction Y)

-- T1 (txid=100)
BEGIN;
SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1; -- Sees version with xmin < 100

-- T2 (txid=101)
UPDATE users SET name = 'Alice' WHERE id = 1; 
-- Creates new version (xmin=101), marks old version (xmax=101)
COMMIT;

-- T1 still sees old version (REPEATABLE READ)
SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1; -- Still sees pre-T2 data
COMMIT;
```

**Benefits**: High concurrency, no read locks
**Tradeoff**: Increased storage, vacuum/cleanup needed

---

## 4. Lock Tuning

### Lock Types

```sql
-- Shared lock (read lock) - multiple readers allowed
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = 1 FOR SHARE;

-- Exclusive lock (write lock) - no other access
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = 1 FOR UPDATE;

-- Row-level vs Table-level
LOCK TABLE orders IN EXCLUSIVE MODE; -- Blocks all access (avoid!)
```

### Lock Tuning Strategies

```sql
-- 1. SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (queue processing)
BEGIN;
SELECT * FROM jobs 
  WHERE status = 'pending' 
  LIMIT 1
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; -- Skip locked rows, process next job
UPDATE jobs SET status = 'processing' WHERE id = ...;
COMMIT;

-- 2. SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT (fail fast)
BEGIN;
SELECT * FROM inventory WHERE product_id = 1
  FOR UPDATE NOWAIT; -- Error immediately if locked
COMMIT;

-- 3. Lock ordering (prevent deadlocks)
-- Always lock resources in same order: alphabetically, by ID, etc.
```

---

## 5. Deadlocks

**Deadlock**: Two transactions wait for each other's locks

```sql
-- Transaction 1
BEGIN;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1; -- Locks row 1
-- ... waiting ...
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2; -- Waits for row 2

-- Transaction 2 (concurrent)
BEGIN;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 50 WHERE id = 2;  -- Locks row 2
-- ... waiting ...
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 50 WHERE id = 1;  -- Waits for row 1 (DEADLOCK!)
```

### Deadlock Prevention

```sql
-- 1. Lock ordering (always lock lower IDs first)
BEGIN;
  SELECT * FROM accounts 
    WHERE id IN (1, 2) 
    ORDER BY id  -- Always same order
    FOR UPDATE;
  -- Perform updates
COMMIT;

-- 2. Timeout detection
SET lock_timeout = '5s'; -- PostgreSQL auto-aborts

-- 3. Reduce transaction scope
BEGIN;
  -- Do calculation OUTSIDE transaction
COMMIT; -- Keep transaction short
```

---

## 6. Idempotency Keys

Ensure operations execute exactly once, even if retried.

```sql
-- Schema
CREATE TABLE payments (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  idempotency_key VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  amount DECIMAL,
  status VARCHAR(20),
  created_at TIMESTAMP
);

-- Application code (pseudo-code)
function processPayment(amount, idempotencyKey) {
  BEGIN;
    -- Try to insert with idempotency key
    INSERT INTO payments (id, idempotency_key, amount, status)
    VALUES (gen_uuid(), idempotencyKey, amount, 'pending')
    ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id;
    
    if (no rows returned) {
      -- Already processed, return existing result
      SELECT * FROM payments WHERE idempotency_key = idempotencyKey;
      COMMIT;
      return result;
    }
    
    -- Process payment...
    UPDATE payments SET status = 'completed' WHERE id = ...;
  COMMIT;
}
```

**Stripe-style API:**
```http
POST /v1/charges
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: a7b8c9d0-1234-5678-90ab-cdef12345678

{"amount": 1000, "currency": "usd"}
```

---

## 7. Sagas & Outbox Pattern for Distributed Workflows

### Saga Pattern

Coordinates multi-service transactions using compensating actions.

**Choreography-based Saga:**
```javascript
// Order Service
async function createOrder(orderData) {
  const order = await db.insert('orders', {...orderData, status: 'PENDING'});
  
  // Publish event
  await eventBus.publish('OrderCreated', {orderId: order.id});
  return order;
}

// Payment Service - listens to OrderCreated
async function handleOrderCreated(event) {
  try {
    await processPayment(event.orderId);
    await eventBus.publish('PaymentSucceeded', {orderId: event.orderId});
  } catch (error) {
    await eventBus.publish('PaymentFailed', {orderId: event.orderId});
  }
}

// Order Service - listens to PaymentFailed (COMPENSATING ACTION)
async function handlePaymentFailed(event) {
  await db.update('orders', {
    id: event.orderId, 
    status: 'CANCELLED'
  });
}
```

**Orchestration-based Saga:**
```javascript
// Saga Orchestrator
async function orderSaga(orderData) {
  const sagaId = generateId();
  
  try {
    // Step 1: Create order
    const order = await orderService.create(orderData);
    
    // Step 2: Reserve inventory
    await inventoryService.reserve(order.items, sagaId);
    
    // Step 3: Process payment
    await paymentService.charge(order.total, sagaId);
    
    // Step 4: Confirm order
    await orderService.confirm(order.id);
    
  } catch (error) {
    // COMPENSATING TRANSACTIONS (reverse order)
    await paymentService.refund(sagaId);
    await inventoryService.release(sagaId);
    await orderService.cancel(order.id);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

### Outbox Pattern

Ensures reliable event publishing using local transaction.

```sql
-- Schema
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id UUID,
  total DECIMAL,
  status VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE outbox (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  aggregate_type VARCHAR(50),
  aggregate_id UUID,
  event_type VARCHAR(100),
  payload JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMP,
  processed_at TIMESTAMP
);
```

**Implementation:**
```javascript
// 1. Write to DB and outbox in SAME transaction
async function createOrder(orderData) {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  
  try {
    await client.query('BEGIN');
    
    // Insert order
    const order = await client.query(
      'INSERT INTO orders (id, user_id, total, status) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4) RETURNING *',
      [uuid(), orderData.userId, orderData.total, 'PENDING']
    );
    
    // Insert outbox event (SAME TRANSACTION)
    await client.query(
      'INSERT INTO outbox (id, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, event_type, payload) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)',
      [uuid(), 'Order', order.id, 'OrderCreated', JSON.stringify(order)]
    );
    
    await client.query('COMMIT');
    return order;
    
  } catch (e) {
    await client.query('ROLLBACK');
    throw e;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

// 2. Separate process polls outbox and publishes events
async function outboxProcessor() {
  while (true) {
    const events = await db.query(
      'SELECT * FROM outbox WHERE processed_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 100'
    );
    
    for (const event of events) {
      try {
        // Publish to message queue
        await messageQueue.publish(event.event_type, event.payload);
        
        // Mark as processed
        await db.query(
          'UPDATE outbox SET processed_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1',
          [event.id]
        );
      } catch (error) {
        // Retry later
        console.error('Failed to publish event', error);
      }
    }
    
    await sleep(1000);
  }
}
```

---

## Quick Decision Guide

| Scenario | Solution |
|----------|----------|
| Bank transfer | SERIALIZABLE isolation + SELECT FOR UPDATE |
| E-commerce inventory | REPEATABLE READ + optimistic locking |
| Job queue processing | SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED |
| API retry safety | Idempotency keys |
| Multi-service transaction | Saga pattern |
| Reliable event publishing | Outbox pattern |
| High-concurrency reads | MVCC (READ COMMITTED) |
| Prevent deadlocks | Lock ordering + timeouts |

**Golden Rule**: Use the weakest isolation level that maintains correctness. Stronger isolation = lower concurrency.

### Database Technology Trade-offs

```markdown
# Database Selection Trade-offs

## PostgreSQL
✅ Pros:
- ACID compliance
- Complex queries & joins
- Mature ecosystem
- JSON support (hybrid flexibility)

❌ Cons:
- Vertical scaling limitations
- Slower for massive writes
- Schema changes require migrations

Use Cases: User, Order, Inventory, Payment services

## MongoDB
✅ Pros:
- Flexible schema
- Horizontal scaling
- High write throughput
- Easy sharding

❌ Cons:
- No ACID across documents (older versions)
- Eventual consistency challenges
- Memory intensive

Use Cases: Notification, Audit logs

## Elasticsearch
✅ Pros:
- Powerful full-text search
- Real-time analytics
- Horizontal scaling

❌ Cons:
- Not a primary database
- Complex operational overhead
- Memory intensive

Use Cases: Product search, log aggregation

## Redis
✅ Pros:
- Sub-millisecond latency
- Rich data structures
- Pub/sub capabilities

❌ Cons:
- Data persistence limitations
- Memory bound
- Limited query capabilities

Use Cases: Caching, session storage, rate limiting
```

### Communication Patterns

```javascript
// communication-patterns.js

const communicationPatterns = {
  // Synchronous: REST/HTTP
  synchronous: {
    technology: "REST over HTTP/2",
    use_cases: [
      "Real-time queries (GET product details)",
      "User-facing operations",
      "Operations requiring immediate response"
    ],
    implementation: {
      client_library: "axios",
      timeout: "5 seconds",
      retry_policy: "Exponential backoff, max 3 retries",
      circuit_breaker: "Enabled"
    },
    example: `
      // Order Service calling Product Service
      const axios = require('axios');
      const CircuitBreaker = require('opossum');
      
      async function getProduct(productId) {
        const options = {
          timeout: 5000,
          errorThresholdPercentage: 50,
          resetTimeout: 30000
        };
        
        const breaker = new CircuitBreaker(async () => {
          return await axios.get(
            \`https://product-service/api/v1/products/\${productId}\`,
            { timeout: 5000 }
          );
        }, options);
        
        try {
          const response = await breaker.fire();
          return response.data;
        } catch (error) {
          // Fallback to cached data
          return await getCachedProduct(productId);
        }
      }
    `
  },
  
  // Asynchronous: Message Queue
  asynchronous_queue: {
    technology: "RabbitMQ",
    use_cases: [
      "Order processing workflow",
      "Payment processing",
      "Email notifications"
    ],
    patterns: {
      work_queue: "Task distribution across workers",
      publish_subscribe: "Fan-out events to multiple consumers",
      routing: "Selective message routing",
      topics: "Pattern-based routing"
    },
    example: `
      // Order Service publishing order created event
      const amqp = require('amqplib');
      
      class OrderEventPublisher {
        constructor() {
          this.connection = null;
          this.channel = null;
        }
        
        async connect() {
          this.connection = await amqp.connect('amqp://rabbitmq:5672');
          this.channel = await this.connection.createChannel();
          
          // Declare exchange
          await this.channel.assertExchange('orders', 'topic', {
            durable: true
          });
        }
        
        async publishOrderCreated(order) {
          const event = {
            eventType: 'order.created',
            eventId: uuidv4(),
            timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
            data: {
              orderId: order.id,
              userId: order.userId,
              items: order.items,
              total: order.total
            }
          };
          
          this.channel.publish(
            'orders',
            'order.created',
            Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(event)),
            { persistent: true }
          );
        }
      }
      
      // Inventory Service consuming order created event
      class OrderEventConsumer {
        async consume() {
          const connection = await amqp.connect('amqp://rabbitmq:5672');
          const channel = await connection.createChannel();
          
          await channel.assertExchange('orders', 'topic', { durable: true });
          await channel.assertQueue('inventory.order.created', { durable: true });
          await channel.bindQueue('inventory.order.created', 'orders', 'order.created');
          
          channel.consume('inventory.order.created', async (msg) => {
            const event = JSON.parse(msg.content.toString());
            
            try {
              await this.reserveInventory(event.data);
              channel.ack(msg);
            } catch (error) {
              // Retry logic
              if (msg.fields.redelivered) {
                // Send to DLQ after retry
                channel.nack(msg, false, false);
              } else {
                // Retry
                channel.nack(msg, false, true);
              }
            }
          });
        }
      }
    `
  },
  
  // Asynchronous: Event Stream
  asynchronous_stream: {
    technology: "Apache Kafka",
    use_cases: [
      "Event sourcing",
      "Audit logs",
      "Real-time analytics",
      "CDC (Change Data Capture)"
    ],
    characteristics: {
      durability: "Persistent, replicated logs",
      ordering: "Guaranteed within partition",
      scalability: "Horizontal via partitions",
      retention: "Configurable (e.g., 7 days)"
    },
    example: `
      // Product Service publishing to Kafka
      const { Kafka } = require('kafkajs');
      
      class ProductEventProducer {
        constructor() {
          this.kafka = new Kafka({
            clientId: 'product-service',
            brokers: ['kafka1:9092', 'kafka2:9092', 'kafka3:9092']
          });
          this.producer = this.kafka.producer();
        }
        
        async connect() {
          await this.producer.connect();
        }
        
        async publishProductUpdated(product) {
          await this.producer.send({
            topic: 'product.events',
            messages: [{
              key: product.id,
              value: JSON.stringify({
                eventType: 'product.updated',
                eventId: uuidv4(),
                timestamp: Date.now(),
                data: product
              }),
              headers: {
                'event-type': 'product.updated',
                'correlation-id': getCorrelationId()
              }
            }]
          });
        }
      }
      
      // Search Service consuming from Kafka
      class ProductEventConsumer {
        constructor() {
          this.kafka = new Kafka({
            clientId: 'search-service',
            brokers: ['kafka1:9092', 'kafka2:9092', 'kafka3:9092']
          });
          this.consumer = this.kafka.consumer({
            groupId: 'search-service-group'
          });
        }
        
        async subscribe() {
          await this.consumer.connect();
          await this.consumer.subscribe({
            topic: 'product.events',
            fromBeginning: false
          });
          
          await this.consumer.run({
            eachMessage: async ({ topic, partition, message }) => {
              const event = JSON.parse(message.value.toString());
              
              switch (event.eventType) {
                case 'product.updated':
                  await this.updateSearchIndex(event.data);
                  break;
                case 'product.deleted':
                  await this.removeFromSearchIndex(event.data.id);
                  break;
              }
            }
          });
        }
      }
    `
  },
  
  // gRPC for internal service-to-service
  grpc: {
    technology: "gRPC with Protocol Buffers",
    use_cases: [
      "High-performance internal APIs",
      "Streaming data",
      "Polyglot environments"
    ],
    advantages: [
      "Binary protocol (faster than JSON)",
      "Strong typing",
      "Bi-directional streaming",
      "HTTP/2 multiplexing"
    ],
    example: `
      // product.proto
      syntax = "proto3";
      
      package product;
      
      service ProductService {
        rpc GetProduct (GetProductRequest) returns (Product);
        rpc ListProducts (ListProductsRequest) returns (stream Product);
        rpc UpdateProduct (UpdateProductRequest) returns (Product);
      }
      
      message Product {
        string id = 1;
        string name = 2;
        string description = 3;
        double price = 4;
        string currency = 5;
      }
      
      message GetProductRequest {
        string id = 1;
      }
      
      message ListProductsRequest {
        int32 page = 1;
        int32 page_size = 2;
      }
      
      message UpdateProductRequest {
        string id = 1;
        Product product = 2;
      }
      
      // Server implementation (Node.js)
      const grpc = require('@grpc/grpc-js');
      const protoLoader = require('@grpc/proto-loader');
      
      const packageDefinition = protoLoader.loadSync('product.proto');
      const productProto = grpc.loadPackageDefinition(packageDefinition).product;
      
      function getProduct(call, callback) {
        const productId = call.request.id;
        // Fetch from database
        const product = await db.products.findById(productId);
        callback(null, product);
      }
      
      const server = new grpc.Server();
      server.addService(productProto.ProductService.service, {
        getProduct: getProduct,
        // ... other methods
      });
      
      server.bindAsync(
        '0.0.0.0:50051',
        grpc.ServerCredentials.createInsecure(),
        () => server.start()
      );
    `
  }
};

// Communication Pattern Decision Tree
```

## 4. Service Discovery

```javascript
// service-discovery-config.js

const serviceDiscoveryConfig = {
  // Option 1: Client-Side Discovery with Consul
  consul: {
    technology: "HashiCorp Consul",
    pattern: "Client-side discovery",
    
    setup: `
      // Docker Compose
      consul:
        image: consul:latest
        ports:
          - "8500:8500"
          - "8600:8600/udp"
        command: agent -server -ui -bootstrap-expect=3 -client=0.0.0.0
    `,
    
    service_registration: `
      // Service registers itself on startup
      const Consul = require('consul');
      
      class ServiceRegistry {
        constructor(serviceName, port) {
          this.consul = new Consul({
            host: process.env.CONSUL_HOST || 'consul',
            port: process.env.CONSUL_PORT || 8500
          });
          this.serviceName = serviceName;
          this.serviceId = \`\${serviceName}-\${process.env.HOSTNAME}\`;
          this.port = port;
        }
        
        async register() {
          const registration = {
            id: this.serviceId,
            name: this.serviceName,
            address: process.env.SERVICE_IP,
            port: this.port,
            check: {
              http: \`http://\${process.env.SERVICE_IP}:\${this.port}/health\`,
              interval: '10s',
              timeout: '5s',
              deregistercriticalserviceafter: '1m'
            },
            tags: [
              'v1',
              process.env.NODE_ENV,
              \`region:\${process.env.REGION}\`
            ]
          };
          
          await this.consul.agent.service.register(registration);
          console.log(\`Service \${this.serviceId} registered with Consul\`);
          
          // Deregister on shutdown
          process.on('SIGTERM', () => this.deregister());
        }
        
        async deregister() {
          await this.consul.agent.service.deregister(this.serviceId);
          console.log(\`Service \${this.serviceId} deregistered\`);
        }
      }
      
      // Usage in service
      const registry = new ServiceRegistry('product-service', 3000);
      registry.register();
    `,
    
    service_discovery: `
      // Client discovers services
      class ServiceDiscovery {
        constructor() {
          this.consul = new Consul({
            host: process.env.CONSUL_HOST || 'consul',
            port: process.env.CONSUL_PORT || 8500
          });
          this.cache = new Map();
        }
        
        async discoverService(serviceName) {
          // Check cache first
          if (this.cache.has(serviceName)) {
            const cached = this.cache.get(serviceName);
            if (Date.now() - cached.timestamp < 30000) { // 30s TTL
              return cached.instances;
            }
          }
          
          // Query Consul
          const result = await this.consul.health.service({
            service: serviceName,
            passing: true
          });
          
          const instances = result.map(entry => ({
            id: entry.Service.ID,
            address: entry.Service.Address,
            port: entry.Service.Port,
            tags: entry.Service.Tags
```

```typescript
// flag-naming.ts
export enum FlagCategory {
  RELEASE = 'release',      // Gradual feature rollout
  EXPERIMENT = 'exp',       // A/B tests
  OPS = 'ops',             // Operational toggles
  PERMISSION = 'perm',     // Entitlement flags
  KILL_SWITCH = 'kill'     // Emergency controls
}

export enum FlagScope {
  GLOBAL = 'global',
  SERVICE = 'svc',
  TEAM = 'team'
}

export interface FlagNamingConfig {
  category: FlagCategory;
  scope: FlagScope;
  service?: string;
  feature: string;
  variant?: string;
}

export class FlagNamingService {
  /**
   * Generate compliant flag name
   * Format: {category}_{scope}_{service?}_{feature}_{variant?}
   * Example: release_svc_payments_newcheckout_v2
   */
  generateFlagName(config: FlagNamingConfig): string {
    const parts = [
      config.category,
      config.scope,
      config.service,
      config.feature,
      config.variant
    ].filter(Boolean);

    const flagName = parts.join('_').toLowerCase();
    
    this.validateFlagName(flagName);
    return flagName;
  }

  validateFlagName(name: string): void {
    const rules = [
      {
        pattern: /^[a-z]+_[a-z]+_/,
        error: 'Must start with category_scope_'
      },
      {
        pattern: /^[a-z0-9_]+$/,
        error: 'Only lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores allowed'
      },
      {
        pattern: /^.{5,80}$/,
        error: 'Length must be between 5 and 80 characters'
      },
      {
        pattern: /^(?!.*__)/,
        error: 'No consecutive underscores allowed'
      }
    ];

    for (const rule of rules) {
      if (!rule.pattern.test(name)) {
        throw new Error(`Invalid flag name: ${rule.error}`);
      }
    }
  }

  parseFlagName(name: string): Partial<FlagNamingConfig> {
    const parts = name.split('_');
    return {
      category: parts[0] as FlagCategory,
      scope: parts[1] as FlagScope,
      service: parts[2],
      feature: parts.slice(3).join('_')
    };
  }
}
```

```typescript
// rollout-analytics.ts
export interface RolloutPlan {
  strategy: 'percentage' | 'targeted' | 'canary' | 'ring';
  stages: RolloutStage[];
  autoProgress: boolean;
  successCriteria: SuccessCriteria;
  monitoringPeriod: number; // minutes
}

export interface RolloutStage {
  stage: number;
  percentage?: number;
  targetUsers?: string[];
  targetRings?: string[];
  duration: number; // minutes
  requiredMetrics: MetricThreshold[];
}

export interface SuccessCriteria {
  errorRateThreshold: number;
  latencyP99Threshold: number;
  minimumSampleSize: number;
  customMetrics?: CustomMetric[];
}

export interface MetricThreshold {
  metricName: string;
  operator: 'lt' | 'lte' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'eq';
  threshold: number;
  comparisonType: 'absolute' | 'relative_to_control' | 'relative_to_baseline';
}

export interface RolloutMetrics {
  flagName: string;
  stage: number;
  timestamp: Date;
  exposures: number;
  errorRate: number;
  latencyP50: number;
  latencyP99: number;
  conversionRate?: number;
  customMetrics: Record<string, number>;
  controlGroupMetrics?: Partial<RolloutMetrics>;
}

export class RolloutAnalytics {
  private metricsStore: MetricsStore;
  private alertingService: AlertingService;

  constructor(metricsStore: MetricsStore, alertingService: AlertingService) {
    this.metricsStore = metricsStore;
    this.alertingService = alertingService;
  }

  async analyzeRollout(
    flagName: string,
    stage: RolloutStage
  ): Promise<RolloutAnalysisResult> {
    const metrics = await this.metricsStore.getMetrics(flagName, stage.stage);
    const violations: MetricViolation[] = [];

    // Check each required metric
    for (const threshold of stage.requiredMetrics) {
      const violation = this.checkThreshold(metrics, threshold);
      if (violation) {
        violations.push(violation);
      }
    }

    // Statistical significance check
    const hasEnoughData = metrics.exposures >= 1000; // Minimum sample
    const isStatisticallySignificant = 
      await this.checkStatisticalSignificance(metrics);

    const result: RolloutAnalysisResult = {
      flagName,
      stage: stage.stage,
      status: this.determineStatus(violations, hasEnoughData),
      violations,
      recommendation: this.generateRecommendation(violations, hasEnoughData),
      metrics,
      confidence: isStatisticallySignificant ? 'high' : 'low'
    };

    // Alert if issues detected
    if (result.status === 'failing') {
      await this.alertingService.sendAlert({
        severity: 'high',
        title: `Feature flag ${flagName} failing rollout criteria`,
        details: result
      });
    }

    return result;
  }

  private checkThreshold(
    metrics: RolloutMetrics,
    threshold: MetricThreshold
  ): MetricViolation | null {
    const actualValue = this.getMetricValue(metrics, threshold.metricName);
    const thresholdValue = this.calculateThreshold(
      metrics,
      threshold
    );

    const violated = this.compareMetric(
      actualValue,
      thresholdValue,
      threshold.operator
    );

    if (violated) {
      return {
        metricName: threshold.metricName,
        expected: thresholdValue,
        actual: actualValue,
        severity: this.calculateSeverity(actualValue, thresholdValue)
      };
    }

    return null;
  }

  private calculateThreshold(
    metrics: RolloutMetrics,
    threshold: MetricThreshold
  ): number {
    switch (threshold.comparisonType) {
      case 'absolute':
        return threshold.threshold;
      
      case 'relative_to_control':
        if (!metrics.controlGroupMetrics) {
          throw new Error('Control group metrics required for relative comparison');
        }
        const controlValue = this.getMetricValue(
          metrics.controlGroupMetrics as RolloutMetrics,
          threshold.metricName
        );
        return controlValue * (1 + threshold.threshold / 100);
      
      case 'relative_to_baseline':
        // Fetch baseline from historical data
        const baseline = this.getBaselineMetric(
          metrics.flagName,
          threshold.metricName
        );
        return baseline * (1 + threshold.threshold / 100);
      
      default:
        return threshold.threshold;
    }
  }

  private async checkStatisticalSignificance(
    metrics: RolloutMetrics
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!metrics.controlGroupMetrics) {
      return false;
    }

    // Simple z-test for proportions (e.g., conversion rate)
    const p1 = metrics.conversionRate || 0;
    const p2 = metrics.controlGroupMetrics.conversionRate || 0;
    const n1 = metrics.exposures;
    const n2 = metrics.controlGroupMetrics.exposures || 0;

    if (n1 < 100 || n2 < 100) {
      return false; // Insufficient sample size
    }

    const pooledP = (p1 * n1 + p2 * n2) / (n1 + n2);
    const se = Math.sqrt(pooledP * (1 - pooledP) * (1/n1 + 1/n2));
    const z = Math.abs((p1 - p2) / se);

    return z > 1.96; // 95% confidence level
  }

  private determineStatus(
    violations: MetricViolation[],
    hasEnoughData: boolean
  ): 'passing' | 'failing' | 'insufficient_data' {
    if (!hasEnoughData) {
      return 'insufficient_data';
    }

    const criticalViolations = violations.filter(v => v.severity === 'critical');
    return criticalViolations.length > 0 ? 'failing' : 'passing';
  }

  private generateRecommendation(
    violations: MetricViolation[],
    hasEnoughData: boolean
  ): string {
    if (!hasEnoughData) {
      return 'Continue monitoring. Insufficient data for decision.';
    }

    if (violations.length === 0) {
      return 'Metrics healthy. Safe to proceed to next stage.';
    }

    const critical = violations.filter(v => v.severity === 'critical');
    if (critical.length > 0) {
      return `HALT ROLLOUT. Critical metrics violated: ${
        critical.map(v => v.metricName).join(', ')
      }. Consider rollback.`;
    }

    return `Minor issues detected: ${
      violations.map(v => v.metricName).join(', ')
    }. Monitor closely before proceeding.`;
  }

  // Helper methods
  private getMetricValue(metrics: RolloutMetrics, name: string): number {
    const mapping: Record<string, keyof RolloutMetrics> = {
      'error_rate': 'errorRate',
      'latency_p99': 'latencyP99',
      'latency_p50': 'latencyP50',
      'conversion_rate': 'conversionRate'
    };

    const key = mapping[name];
    return (metrics[key] as number) || 0;
  }

  private compareMetric(
    actual: number,
    threshold: number,
    operator: string
  ): boolean {
    switch (operator) {
      case 'lt': return actual >= threshold;
      case 'lte': return actual > threshold;
      case 'gt': return actual <= threshold;
      case 'gte': return actual < threshold;
      case 'eq': return actual !== threshold;
      default: return false;
    }
  }

  private calculateSeverity(actual: number, threshold: number): 'critical' | 'warning' {
    const deviation = Math.abs((actual - threshold) / threshold);
    return deviation > 0.5 ? 'critical' : 'warning';
  }

  private getBaselineMetric(flagName: string, metricName: string): number {
    // Stub: fetch from historical data
    return 0;
  }
}
```

```typescript
export enum KillSwitchReason {
  HIGH_ERROR_RATE = 'high_error_rate',
  PERFORMANCE_DEGRADATION = 'performance_degradation',
  DATA_INTEGRITY = 'data_integrity',

  enabled: boolean;
  autoTriggerRules: AutoTriggerRule[];
  notificationChannels: string[];
  rollbackStrategy: RollbackStrategy;
  gracePeriod?: number; // seconds before kill
}

export interface AutoTriggerRule {
  condition: string; // Expression: "error_rate > 5 AND duration > 60"
  severity: 'high' | 'critical';
  cooldown: number; // seconds before can trigger again
}

export interface RollbackStrategy {
  type: 'immediate' | 'gradual' | 'targeted';
  gradualPercentagePerMinute?: number;
  targetedRings?: string[];
  preserveControlGroup?: boolean;
}

export class KillSwitchOrchestrator {
  private flagService: FeatureFlagService;
  private metricsStore: MetricsStore;
  private alerting: AlertingService;
  private auditLog: AuditLogService;
  private activeTriggers: Map<string, Date> = new Map();

  async monitorFlags(): Promise<void> {
    const configs = await this.loadKillSwitchConfigs();

    for (const config of configs) {
      if (!config.enabled) continue;

      const shouldTrigger = await this.evaluateKillSwitch(config);

      if (shouldTrigger) {
        await this.triggerKillSwitch(config, {
          flagName: config.flagName,
          reason: KillSwitchReason.HIGH_ERROR_RATE, // Determined by evaluation
          triggeredBy: 'automatic',
          severity: 'critical',
          affectedServices: await this.getAffectedServices(config.flagName),
          timestamp: new Date(),
          metadata: {}
        });
      }
    }
  }

  private async evaluateKillSwitch(
    config: KillSwitchConfig
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    // Check cooldown
    const lastTrigger = this.activeTriggers.get(config.flagName);
    if (lastTrigger) {
      const cooldown = 300; // 5 minutes default
      if (Date.now() - lastTrigger.getTime() < cooldown * 1000) {
        return false;
      }
    }

    // Evaluate each auto-trigger rule
    for (const rule of config.autoTriggerRules) {
      const metrics = await this.metricsStore.getMetrics(config.flagName, 0);
      
      if (this.evaluateCondition(rule.condition, metrics)) {
        return true;
      }
    }

    return false;
  }

  async triggerKillSwitch(
    config: KillSwitchConfig,
    event: KillSwitchEvent
  ): Promise<void> {
    console.log(`🚨 KILL SWITCH TRIGGERED: ${event.flagName}`);
    
    // Mark as triggered to prevent re-trigger during cooldown
    this.activeTriggers.set(config.flagName, new Date());

    try {
      // Execute rollback strategy
      await this.executeRollback(config, event);

      // Send notifications
      await this.notifyStakeholders(config, event);

      // Audit log
      await this.auditLog.log({
        action: 'KILL_SWITCH_TRIGGERED',
        flagName: event.flagName,
        event,
        timestamp: new Date()
      });

      // Create incident if critical
      if (event.severity === 'critical') {
        await this.createIncident(event);
      }

    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Kill switch execution failed:', error);
      // Escalate to on-call
      await this.alerting.sendAlert({
        severity: 'critical',
        title: `Kill switch execution failed for ${event.flagName}`,
        details: { event, error }
      });
    }
  }

  private async executeRollback(
    config: KillSwitchConfig,
    event: KillSwitchEvent
  ): Promise<void> {
    const strategy = config.rollbackStrategy;

    switch (strategy.type) {
      case 'immediate':
        // Turn off flag completely
        await this.flagService.setFlagState(config.flagName, {
          enabled: false,
          percentage: 0,
          reason: `Kill switch: ${event.reason}`
        });
        break;

      case 'gradual':
        // Gradually reduce exposure
        await this.gradualRollback(
          config.flagName,
          strategy.gradualPercentagePerMinute || 10
        );
        break;

      case 'targeted':
        // Disable only for specific rings/segments
        if (strategy.targetedRings) {
          for (const ring of strategy.targetedRings) {
            await this.flagService.setFlagStateForRing(
              config.flagName,
              ring,
              false
            );
          }
        }
        break;
    }
  }

  private async gradualRollback(
    flagName: string,
    percentagePerMinute: number
  ): Promise<void> {
    const currentState = await this.flagService.getFlagState(flagName);
    let percentage = currentState.percentage;

    while (percentage > 0) {
      percentage = Math.max(0, percentage - percentagePerMinute);
      await this.flagService.setFlagState(flagName, {
        enabled: percentage > 0,
        percentage,
        reason: 'Gradual rollback in progress'
      });
      
      // Wait 1 minute
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 60000));
    }
  }

  private async notifyStakeholders(
    config: KillSwitchConfig,
    event: KillSwitchEvent
  ): Promise<void> {
    const message = `
🚨 KILL SWITCH ACTIVATED 🚨

Flag: ${event.flagName}
Reason: ${event.reason}
Triggered: ${event.triggeredBy}
Severity: ${event.severity}
Services: ${event.affectedServices.join(', ')}

A rollback has been initiated automatically.
View details: https://flags.company.com/kill-switch/${event.flagName}
    `.trim();

    for (const channel of config.notificationChannels) {
      await this.alerting.sendAlert({
        severity: event.severity,
        channel,
        title: `Kill Switch: ${event.flagName}`,
        message
      });
    }

    // Page on-call for critical
    if (event.severity === 'critical') {
      await this.alerting.pageOnCall({
        title: `Critical Kill Switch: ${event.flagName}`,
        message
      });
    }
  }

  private evaluateCondition(condition: string, metrics: any): boolean {
    // Simple expression evaluator
    // In production, use a proper expression library
    try {
      const fn = new Function('metrics', `
        with (metrics) {
          return ${condition};
        }
      `);
      return fn(metrics);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Failed to evaluate condition:', error);
      return false;
    }
  }

  // Manual kill switch trigger
  async manualKillSwitch(
    flagName: string,
    userId: string,
    reason: string
  ): Promise<void> {
    const config = await this.loadKillSwitchConfig(flagName);
    
    await this.triggerKillSwitch(config, {
      flagName,
      reason: KillSwitchReason.MANUAL,
      triggeredBy: 'manual',
      triggeredByUser: userId,
      severity: 'high',
      affectedServices: await this.getAffectedServices(flagName),
      timestamp: new Date(),
      metadata: { manualReason: reason }
    });
  }

  // Stub implementations
  private async loadKillSwitchConfigs(): Promise<KillSwitchConfig[]> { return []; }
  private async loadKillSwitchConfig(flagName: string): Promise<KillSwitchConfig> {
    return {} as KillSwitchConfig;
  }
  private async getAffectedServices(flagName: string): Promise<string[]> { return []; }
  private async createIncident(event: KillSwitchEvent): Promise<void> {}
}

// Stub interfaces
interface FeatureFlagService {

  getFlagState(name: string): Promise<any>;
  setFlagStateForRing(name: string, ring: string, enabled: boolean): Promise<void>;
}
```
