```python
# iac_review_system.py
import os
import json
import hashlib
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from enum import Enum
import yaml
import re
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager

# ============================================================================
# Core Data Models
# ============================================================================

class ReviewStatus(Enum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    APPROVED = "approved"
    REJECTED = "rejected"
    CHANGES_REQUESTED = "changes_requested"

class DeploymentStatus(Enum):
    PLANNED = "planned"
    IN_PROGRESS = "in_progress"
    SUCCESS = "success"
    FAILED = "failed"
    ROLLED_BACK = "rolled_back"

class PolicySeverity(Enum):
    INFO = "info"
    WARNING = "warning"
    ERROR = "error"
    CRITICAL = "critical"

@dataclass
class ModuleVersion:
    """Represents a versioned IaC module"""
    module_name: str
    version: str
    path: str
    checksum: str
    author: str
    timestamp: datetime
    dependencies: List[Dict[str, str]]
    changelog: str
    
@dataclass
class PolicyViolation:
    """Policy check violation"""
    policy_name: str
    severity: PolicySeverity
    message: str
    resource: str
    line: Optional[int] = None
    remediation: Optional[str] = None

@dataclass
class DriftResult:
    """Drift detection result"""
    resource_type: str
    resource_name: str
    property: str
    expected_value: Any
    actual_value: Any
    drift_detected: bool
    timestamp: datetime

@dataclass
class Review:
    """Code review record"""
    review_id: str
    module_version: str
    reviewer: str
    status: ReviewStatus
    comments: str
    timestamp: datetime
    approved_by: Optional[List[str]] = None

@dataclass
class Deployment:
    """Deployment record"""
    deployment_id: str
    module_version: str
    environment: str
    status: DeploymentStatus
    started_at: datetime
    completed_at: Optional[datetime]
    deployed_by: str
    rollback_version: Optional[str] = None
    changes: Optional[List[Dict]] = None

# ============================================================================
# Module Version Manager
# ============================================================================

class ModuleVersionManager:
    """Manages versioning of IaC modules"""
    
    def __init__(self, repo_path: str, db_path: str):
        self.repo_path = Path(repo_path)
        self.db_path = db_path
        self._init_db()
    
    def _init_db(self):
        """Initialize database for module versions"""
        with self._get_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS module_versions (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    module_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                    version TEXT NOT NULL,
                    path TEXT NOT NULL,
                    checksum TEXT NOT NULL,
                    author TEXT NOT NULL,
                    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
                    dependencies TEXT,
                    changelog TEXT,
                    UNIQUE(module_name, version)
                )
            """)
    
    @contextmanager
    def _get_db(self):
        """Database connection context manager"""
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        try:
            yield conn
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()
    
    def calculate_checksum(self, module_path: Path) -> str:
        """Calculate checksum for module files"""
        hasher = hashlib.sha256()
        
        for file_path in sorted(module_path.rglob("*")):
            if file_path.is_file() and not str(file_path).startswith('.git'):
                with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
                    hasher.update(f.read())
        
        return hasher.hexdigest()
    
    def create_version(
        self,
        module_name: str,
        version: str,
        author: str,
        dependencies: List[Dict[str, str]],
        changelog: str
    ) -> ModuleVersion:
        """Create a new module version"""
        module_path = self.repo_path / module_name
        
        if not module_path.exists():
            raise ValueError(f"Module path does not exist: {module_path}")
        
        # Validate semantic versioning
        if not re.match(r'^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$', version):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid version format: {version}. Use semantic versioning (x.y.z)")
        
        checksum = self.calculate_checksum(module_path)
        timestamp = datetime.now()
        
        module_version = ModuleVersion(
            module_name=module_name,
            version=version,
            path=str(module_path),
            checksum=checksum,
            author=author,
            timestamp=timestamp,
            dependencies=dependencies,
            changelog=changelog
        )
        
        # Store in database
        with self._get_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                INSERT INTO module_versions 
                (module_name, version, path, checksum, author, timestamp, dependencies, changelog)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """, (
                module_name,
                version,
                str(module_path),
                checksum,
                author,
                timestamp.isoformat(),
                json.dumps(dependencies),
                changelog
            ))
        
        # Tag in Git
        self._create_git_tag(module_name, version)
        
        print(f"✓ Created module version: {module_name} v{version}")
        return module_version
    
    def _create_git_tag(self, module_name: str, version: str):
        """Create Git tag for module version"""
        tag = f"{module_name}-v{version}"
        try:
            subprocess.run(
                ["git", "tag", "-a", tag, "-m", f"Version {version} of {module_name}"],
                cwd=self.repo_path,
                check=True
            )
            print(f"  Created Git tag: {tag}")
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
            print(f"  Warning: Could not create Git tag: {e}")
    
    def get_version(self, module_name: str, version: str) -> Optional[ModuleVersion]:
        """Retrieve a specific module version"""
        with self._get_db() as conn:
            row = conn.execute("""
                SELECT * FROM module_versions 
                WHERE module_name = ? AND version = ?
            """, (module_name, version)).fetchone()
            
            if row:
                return ModuleVersion(
                    module_name=row['module_name'],
                    version=row['version'],
                    path=row['path'],
                    checksum=row['checksum'],
                    author=row['author'],
                    timestamp=datetime.fromisoformat(row['timestamp']),
                    dependencies=json.loads(row['dependencies']),
                    changelog=row['changelog']
                )
        return None
    
    def list_versions(self, module_name: str) -> List[ModuleVersion]:
        """List all versions of a module"""
        with self._get_db() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute("""
                SELECT * FROM module_versions 
                WHERE module_name = ?
                ORDER BY timestamp DESC
            """, (module_name,)).fetchall()
            
            return [
                ModuleVersion(
                    module_name=row['module_name'],
                    version=row['version'],
                    path=row['path'],
                    checksum=row['checksum'],
                    author=row['author'],
                    timestamp=datetime.fromisoformat(row['timestamp']),
                    dependencies=json.loads(row['dependencies']),
                    changelog=row['changelog']
                )
                for row in rows
            ]

# ============================================================================
# Policy Engine
# ============================================================================

class PolicyEngine:
    """Automated policy checking for IaC"""
    
    def __init__(self, policy_dir: str):
        self.policy_dir = Path(policy_dir)
        self.policies = self._load_policies()
    
    def _load_policies(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Load policy definitions"""
        policies = []
        
        if not self.policy_dir.exists():
            return policies
        
        for policy_file in self.policy_dir.glob("*.yaml"):
            with open(policy_file) as f:
                policy = yaml.safe_load(f)
                policies.append(policy)
        
        return policies
    
    def check_terraform(self, tf_path: Path) -> List[PolicyViolation]:
        """Check Terraform files against policies"""
        violations = []
        
        # Parse Terraform files
        tf_config = self._parse_terraform(tf_path)
        
        # Run policy checks
        for policy in self.policies:
            if policy.get('target') == 'terraform':
                violations.extend(self._check_policy(policy, tf_config))
        
        return violations
    
    def _parse_terraform(self, tf_path: Path) -> Dict:
        """Parse Terraform configuration"""
        # This is simplified - in production, use proper HCL parser
        config = {
            'resources': [],
            'variables': [],
            'outputs': []
        }
        
        for tf_file in tf_path.glob("*.tf"):
            with open(tf_file) as f:
                content = f.read()
                # Simple regex-based parsing (use proper parser in production)
                resources = re.findall(
                    r'resource\s+"([^"]+)"\s+"([^"]+)"\s+{([^}]+)}',
                    content,
                    re.DOTALL
                )
                
                for resource_type, resource_name, resource_body in resources:
                    config['resources'].append({
                        'type': resource_type,
                        'name': resource_name,
                        'body': resource_body,
                        'file': str(tf_file)
                    })
        
        return config
    
    def _check_policy(self, policy: Dict, config: Dict) -> List[PolicyViolation]:
        """Check a single policy against configuration"""
        violations = []
        
        for rule in policy.get('rules', []):
            rule_violations = self._check_rule(rule, config, policy['name'])
            violations.extend(rule_violations)
        
        return violations
    
    def _check_rule(
        self,
        rule: Dict,
        config: Dict,
        policy_name: str
    ) -> List[PolicyViolation]:
        """Check a single rule"""
        violations = []
        rule_type = rule.get('type')
        
        if rule_type == 'require_tags':
            violations.extend(self._check_tags(rule, config, policy_name))
        elif rule_type == 'restrict_regions':
            violations.extend(self._check_regions(rule, config, policy_name))
        elif rule_type == 'encryption_required':
            violations.extend(self._check_encryption(rule, config, policy_name))
        elif rule_type == 'naming_convention':
            violations.extend(self._check_naming(rule, config, policy_name))
        
        return violations
    
    def _check_tags(
        self,
        rule: Dict,
        config: Dict,
        policy_name: str
    ) -> List[PolicyViolation]:
        """Check required tags"""
        violations = []
        required_tags = rule.get('required_tags', [])
        
        for resource in config.get('resources', []):
            if 'tags' not in resource['body']:
                violations.append(PolicyViolation(
                    policy_name=policy_name,
                    severity=PolicySeverity(rule.get('severity', 'warning')),
                    message=f"Resource missing required tags: {', '.join(required_tags)}",
                    resource=f"{resource['type']}.{resource['name']}",
                    remediation=f"Add tags: {required_tags}"
                ))
        
        return violations
    
    def _check_regions(
        self,
        rule: Dict,
        config: Dict,
        policy_name: str
    ) -> List[PolicyViolation]:
        """Check allowed regions"""
        violations = []
        allowed_regions = rule.get('allowed_regions', [])
        
        for resource in config.get('resources', []):
            region_match = re.search(r'region\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', resource['body'])
            if region_match:
                region = region_match.group(1)
                if region not in allowed_regions:
                    violations.append(PolicyViolation(
                        policy_name=policy_name,
                        severity=PolicySeverity(rule.get('severity', 'error')),
                        message=f"Region '{region}' not in allowed list: {allowed_regions}",
                        resource=f"{resource['type']}.{resource['name']}",
                        remediation=f"Use one of: {', '.join(allowed_regions)}"
                    ))
        
        return violations
    
    def _check_encryption(
        self,
        rule: Dict,
        config: Dict,
        policy_name: str
    ) -> List[PolicyViolation]:
        """Check encryption requirements"""
        violations = []
        resource_types = rule.get('resource_types', [])
        
        for resource in config.get('resources', []):
            if resource['type'] in resource_types:
                if 'encrypted' not in resource['body'] or 'encryption' not in resource['body']:
                    violations.append(PolicyViolation(
                        policy_name=policy_name,
                        severity=PolicySeverity(rule.get('severity', 'critical')),
                        message="Encryption not enabled",
                        resource=f"{resource['type']}.{resource['name']}",
                        remediation="Enable encryption for this resource"
                    ))
        
        return violations
    
    def _check_naming(
        self,
        rule: Dict,
        config: Dict,
        policy_name: str
    ) -> List[PolicyViolation]:
        """Check naming conventions"""
        violations = []
        pattern = rule.get('pattern', '')
        
        for resource in config.get('resources', []):
            if not re.match(pattern, resource['name']):
                violations.append(PolicyViolation(
                    policy_name=policy_name,
                    severity=PolicySeverity(rule.get('severity', 'warning')),
                    message=f"Resource name doesn't match pattern: {pattern}",
                    resource=f"{resource['type']}.{resource['name']}",
                    remediation=f"Rename to match pattern: {pattern}"
                ))
        
        return violations

# ============================================================================
# Drift Detection
# ============================================================================

class DriftDetector:
    """Detect configuration drift"""
    
    def __init__(self, state_backend: str):
        self.state_backend = state_backend
    
    def detect_drift(self, module_path: Path) -> List[DriftResult]:
        """Detect drift for a module"""
        print(f"\n🔍 Detecting drift for: {module_path}")
        
        # Get current state
        current_state = self._get_current_state(module_path)
        
        # Get actual state from cloud provider
        actual_state = self._get_actual_state(module_path)
        
        # Compare states
        drift_results = self._compare_states(current_state, actual_state)
        
        return drift_results
    
    def _get_current_state(self, module_path: Path) -> Dict:
        """Get current state from state backend"""
        # Simplified - in production, integrate with actual state backend
        state_file = module_path / "terraform.tfstate"
        
        if state_file.exists():
            with open(state_file) as f:
                return json.load(f)
        
        return {'resources': []}
    
    def _get_actual_state(self, module_path: Path) -> Dict:
        """Get actual state from provider (run terraform refresh)"""
        try:
            # Run terraform refresh to get actual state
            result = subprocess.run(
                ["terraform", "refresh", "-json"],
                cwd=module_path,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True
            )
            
            # Parse output (simplified)
            return {'resources': []}
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return {'resources': []}
    
    def _compare_states(
        self,
        current_state: Dict,
        actual_state: Dict
    ) -> List[DriftResult]:
        """Compare current and actual states"""
        drift_results = []
        timestamp = datetime.now()
        
        current_resources = {
            r.get('name'): r 
            for r in current_state.get('resources', [])
        }
        
        actual_resources = {
            r.get('name'): r 
            for r in actual_state.get('resources', [])
        }
        
        # Check for differences
        for name, current in current_resources.items():
            actual = actual_resources.get(name)
            
            if not actual:
                drift_results.append(DriftResult(
                    resource_type=current.get('type', ''),
                    resource_name=name,
                    property='existence',
                    expected_value='exists',
                    actual_value='missing',
                    drift_detected=True,
                    timestamp=timestamp
                ))
            else:
                # Compare properties
                for prop, expected_val in current.get('values', {}).items():
                    actual_val = actual.get('values', {}).get(prop)
                    
                    if expected_val != actual_val:
                        drift_results.append(DriftResult(
                            resource_type=current.get('type', ''),
                            resource_name=name,
                            property=prop,
                            expected_value=expected_val,
                            actual_value=actual_val,
                            drift_detected=True,
                            timestamp=timestamp
                        ))
        
        return drift_results

# ============================================================================
# Review System
# ============================================================================

class ReviewSystem:
    """Peer review workflow"""
    
    def __init__(self, db_path: str):
        self.db_path = db_path
        self._init_db()
    
    def _init_db(self):
        """Initialize review database"""
        with self._get_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reviews (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    review_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                    module_version TEXT NOT NULL,
                    reviewer TEXT NOT NULL,
                    status TEXT NOT NULL,
                    comments TEXT,
                    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,

            if not row:

            approved_by = json.loads(row['approved_by'] if row['approved_by'] else '[]')
            
            if status == ReviewStatus.APPROVED and reviewer not in approved_by:
                approved_by.append(reviewer)
            
            conn.execute("""
                UPDATE reviews 
                SET status = ?, comments = ?, approved_by = ?
                WHERE review_id = ?

    ) -> Deployment:

        ).hexdigest()[:12]
        
        print(f"\n🚀 Starting deployment: {deployment_id}")
        print(f"   Module: {module_version}")
        print(f"   Environment: {environment}")
        
        # Get current version for rollback
        current_version = self._get_current_version(environment)
        
        deployment = Deployment(
            deployment_id=deployment_id,
            module_version=module_version,
            environment=environment,
            status=DeploymentStatus.IN_PROGRESS,
            started_at=datetime.now(),
            completed_at=None,
            deployed_by=deployed_by,
            rollback_version=current_version
        )
        
        # Save deployment record
        with self._get_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                INSERT INTO deployments 
                (deployment_id, module_version, environment, status, started_at, deployed_by, rollback_version)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """, (
                deployment_id,
                module_version,
                environment,
                deployment.status.value,
                deployment.started_at.isoformat(),
                deployed_by,
                current_version
            ))
        
        try:
            # Execute deployment
            changes = self._execute_deployment(module_path, environment)
            deployment.changes = changes
            deployment.status = DeploymentStatus.SUCCESS
            deployment.completed_at = datetime.now()
            
            print(f"✓ Deployment successful: {deployment_id}")
            
        except Exception as e:
            deployment.status = DeploymentStatus.FAILED
            deployment.completed_at = datetime.now()
            print(f"✗ Deployment failed: {e}")
            raise
        finally:
            # Update deployment record
            with self._get_db() as conn:
                conn.execute("""

                    SET status = ?, completed_at = ?, changes = ?
                    WHERE deployment_id = ?
                """, (

                    deployment.completed_at.isoformat() if deployment.completed_at else None,
                    json.dumps(deployment.changes) if deployment.changes else None,

            raise Exception("Pre-flight checks failed")
        
        # 2. Establish baseline
        baseline = await self.establish_baseline(
            experiment.steady_state.metrics
        )
        
        # 3. Verify steady state
        if not await self.verify_steady_state(baseline):
            raise Exception("System not in steady state")
        
        # 4. Notify stakeholders
        await self.notify("Experiment starting", experiment)
        
        try:
            # 5. Inject fault
            fault_id = await self.fault_injector.inject(
                experiment.method.fault
            )
            
            # 6. Monitor steady-state metrics
            monitoring_task = asyncio.create_task(
                self.monitor_steady_state(
                    baseline,
                    experiment.steady_state.validation_duration
                )
            )
            
            # 7. Wait for experiment duration
            await asyncio.sleep(experiment.method.fault.duration)
            
            # 8. Check if steady state maintained
            steady_state_ok = await monitoring_task
            
        finally:
            # 9. Rollback (always executed)
            await self.fault_injector.rollback(fault_id)
            
        # 10. Collect results
        result = await self.analyze_results(
            experiment, baseline, steady_state_ok
        )
        
        # 11. Generate report
        await self.generate_report(result)
        
        return result
    
    async def preflight_checks(self, experiment) -> bool:
        """Verify system is ready for chaos"""
        checks = [
            self.check_no_active_incidents(),
            self.check_deployment_freeze(),
            self.check_on_call_available(),
            self.check_blast_radius_valid(experiment),
            self.check_rollback_capability(),
        ]
        results = await asyncio.gather(*checks)
        return all(results)
    
    async def monitor_steady_state(self, baseline, duration) -> bool:
        """Continuously monitor metrics during experiment"""
        start = datetime.now()
        violations = []
        
        while (datetime.now() - start).seconds < duration:
            current_metrics = await self.metrics_client.get_current()
            
            for metric_name, value in current_metrics.items():
                baseline_value = baseline[metric_name]
                threshold = baseline['thresholds'][metric_name]
                
                if not self.within_threshold(value, baseline_value, threshold):
                    violation = {
                        'metric': metric_name,
                        'expected': baseline_value,
                        'actual': value,
                        'timestamp': datetime.now()
                    }
                    violations.append(violation)
                    
                    # Immediate rollback on critical violation
                    if self.is_critical_violation(violation):
                        await self.emergency_rollback()
                        return False
            
            await asyncio.sleep(10)  # Check every 10 seconds
        
        return len(violations) == 0

# Continuous chaos pipeline
class ChaosPipeline:

    def __init__(self):

# blast_radius_controller.py
from enum import Enum
from typing import List

class BlastRadiusLevel(Enum):
    SINGLE_INSTANCE = "single_instance"
    CANARY = "canary"            # 5% of traffic
    SMALL = "small"               # 10-20%
    MEDIUM = "medium"             # 20-50%
    LARGE = "large"               # 50-100%

class BlastRadiusController:
    """Enforce and manage experiment blast radius"""
    
    LEVEL_CONSTRAINTS = {
        BlastRadiusLevel.SINGLE_INSTANCE: {
            'max_instances': 1,
            'max_traffic_percent': 0,
            'max_concurrent_experiments': 1,
            'required_approvals': 1,
            'auto_approval': True
        },
        BlastRadiusLevel.CANARY: {
            'max_instances': 2,
            'max_traffic_percent': 5,
            'max_concurrent_experiments': 2,
            'required_approvals': 1,
            'auto_approval': True,
            'requires_steady_state': True
        },
        BlastRadiusLevel.MEDIUM: {
            'max_instances': 10,
            'max_traffic_percent': 50,
            'max_concurrent_experiments': 1,
            'required_approvals': 2,
            'auto_approval': False,
            'business_hours_only': True
        }
    }
    
    def validate_blast_radius(self, experiment) -> bool:
        """Validate experiment respects blast radius limits"""
        level = experiment.blast_radius.level
        constraints = self.LEVEL_CONSTRAINTS[level]
        
        validations = [
            self.check_instance_count(experiment, constraints),
            self.check_traffic_percentage(experiment, constraints),
            self.check_concurrent_limit(constraints),
            self.check_time_restrictions(constraints),
            self.check_approval_requirements(experiment, constraints)
        ]
        
        return all(validations)
    
    def check_concurrent_limit(self, constraints) -> bool:
        """Ensure we don't exceed concurrent experiment limit"""
        active = self.get_active_experiments()
        max_concurrent = constraints['max_concurrent_experiments']
        
        if len(active) >= max_concurrent:
            self.log_rejection(
                f"Concurrent limit reached: {len(active)}/{max_concurrent}"
            )
            return False
        return True
    
    def get_recommended_level(self, experiment) -> BlastRadiusLevel:
        """Suggest appropriate blast radius for experiment"""
        
        # First-time experiment
        if experiment.execution_count == 0:
            return BlastRadiusLevel.SINGLE_INSTANCE
        
        # Progressive expansion based on success history
        success_rate = experiment.successful_runs / experiment.total_runs
        
        if success_rate >= 0.95 and experiment.execution_count >= 5:
            return BlastRadiusLevel.CANARY
        elif success_rate >= 0.98 and experiment.execution_count >= 10:
            return BlastRadiusLevel.SMALL
        else:
            return BlastRadiusLevel.SINGLE_INSTANCE

# architecture_analysis.py
import ast
import networkx as nx
from collections import defaultdict

class MonolithAnalyzer:
    """Analyze codebase structure and dependencies"""
    
    def __init__(self, codebase_path):
        self.path = codebase_path
        self.dependency_graph = nx.DiGraph()
        self.module_metrics = defaultdict(dict)
    
    def analyze_dependencies(self):
        """Build dependency graph from imports"""
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(self.path):
            for file in files:
                if file.endswith('.py'):
                    self._analyze_file(os.path.join(root, file))
        
        return self.dependency_graph
    
    def _analyze_file(self, filepath):
        with open(filepath) as f:
            tree = ast.parse(f.read())
            
        module_name = self._get_module_name(filepath)
        
        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                for alias in node.names:
                    self.dependency_graph.add_edge(module_name, alias.name)
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
                if node.module:
                    self.dependency_graph.add_edge(module_name, node.module)
    
    def identify_seams(self):
        """Find natural boundaries using clustering"""
        # Find strongly connected components
        components = list(nx.strongly_connected_components(self.dependency_graph))
        
        # Calculate modularity
        communities = nx.community.greedy_modularity_communities(
            self.dependency_graph.to_undirected()
        )
        
        # Find cut vertices (removal would disconnect graph)
        cut_vertices = list(nx.articulation_points(self.dependency_graph.to_undirected()))
        
        return {
            'components': components,
            'communities': communities,
            'seams': cut_vertices,
            'highly_coupled': self._find_hub_modules()
        }
    
    def _find_hub_modules(self, threshold=10):
        """Identify modules with high fan-in/fan-out"""
        hubs = []
        for node in self.dependency_graph.nodes():
            in_degree = self.dependency_graph.in_degree(node)
            out_degree = self.dependency_graph.out_degree(node)
            if in_degree + out_degree > threshold:
                hubs.append({
                    'module': node,
                    'in_degree': in_degree,
                    'out_degree': out_degree,
                    'centrality': nx.betweenness_centrality(self.dependency_graph)[node]
                })
        return sorted(hubs, key=lambda x: x['centrality'], reverse=True)
    
    def generate_report(self):
        """Create refactoring priority report"""
        seams = self.identify_seams()
        
        return {
            'total_modules': self.dependency_graph.number_of_nodes(),
            'total_dependencies': self.dependency_graph.number_of_edges(),
            'natural_boundaries': len(seams['communities']),
            'high_risk_modules': seams['highly_coupled'][:10],
            'recommended_extraction_order': self._prioritize_extraction(seams)
        }
    
    def _prioritize_extraction(self, seams):
        """Score modules for extraction priority"""
        priorities = []
        
        for community in seams['communities']:
            score = self._calculate_extraction_score(community)
            priorities.append({
                'modules': list(community),
                'score': score,
                'rationale': self._explain_score(community, score)
            })
        
        return sorted(priorities, key=lambda x: x['score'], reverse=True)
    
    def _calculate_extraction_score(self, modules):
        """
        Score based on:
        - Low external coupling (easier to extract)
        - High internal cohesion
        - Business value (from metadata)
        - Change frequency (benefit of independent deployment)
        - Team boundaries
        """
        subgraph = self.dependency_graph.subgraph(modules)
        
        internal_edges = subgraph.number_of_edges()
        external_edges = sum(
            1 for m in modules 
            for neighbor in self.dependency_graph.neighbors(m)
            if neighbor not in modules
        )
        
        coupling_score = internal_edges / (external_edges + 1)  # Higher is better
        
        return coupling_score

                span.set_attribute("error", True)
                span.set_attribute("error.type", type(e).__name__)

                raise
                
            finally:

# strangler_pattern.py

class StranglerFacade:
    """
    Route requests to old or new implementation
    based on feature flags and rollout percentage
    """
    
    def __init__(self, service_name):
        self.service_name = service_name
        self.old_impl = self._load_old_implementation()
        self.new_impl = self._load_new_implementation()
        self.feature_flags = FeatureFlagClient()
        self.metrics = MetricsClient()
    
    async def route_request(self, request):
        """Intelligent routing with safety controls"""
        
        # Check if new service is healthy
        if not await self._health_check_new_service():
            logger.warning(f"New {self.service_name} unhealthy, routing to old")
            return await self.old_impl.handle(request)
        
        # Get routing decision
        routing = self._get_routing_decision(request)
        
        if routing == 'new':
            try:
                result = await self._call_new_with_fallback(request)
                self.metrics.increment(f'{self.service_name}.routed_to_new')
                return result
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"New implementation failed: {e}")
                self.metrics.increment(f'{self.service_name}.fallback_to_old')
                # Automatic fallback
                return await self.old_impl.handle(request)
        
        elif routing == 'both':
            # Dark launch: call both, return old, compare results
            return await self._dark_launch(request)
        
        else:  # 'old'
            self.metrics.increment(f'{self.service_name}.routed_to_old')
            return await self.old_impl.handle(request)
    
    def _get_routing_decision(self, request):
        """
        Routing logic based on:
        - Feature flags
        - User cohorts
        - Request attributes
        - Gradual rollout percentage
        - Circuit breaker state
        """
        
        # Check circuit breaker
        if self.circuit_breaker.is_open():
            return 'old'
        
        # Check feature flag
        flag = self.feature_flags.get_flag(
            f'{self.service_name}_rollout',
            context={
                'user_id': request.user_id,
                'request_type': request.type,
                'tenant': request.tenant
            }
        )
        
        if flag.value == 'new':
            return 'new'
        elif flag.value == 'dark_launch':
            return 'both'
        elif flag.value == 'percentage_rollout':
            if self._in_rollout_cohort(request, flag.percentage):
                return 'new'
        
        return 'old'
    
    async def _dark_launch(self, request):
        """Call both implementations, compare, return old result"""
        
        old_result_future = self.old_impl.handle(request)
        new_result_future = self.new_impl.handle(request)
        
        # Wait for old (primary)
        old_result = await old_result_future
        
        # New implementation runs in background
        asyncio.create_task(
            self._compare_results(request, old_result, new_result_future)
        )
        
        return old_result
    
    async def _compare_results(self, request, old_result, new_result_future):
        """Compare implementations and log discrepancies"""
        try:
            new_result = await asyncio.wait_for(new_result_future, timeout=5.0)
            
            comparison = ResultComparator.compare(old_result, new_result)

                    f"Result mismatch in {self.service_name}",
                    extra={
                        'request_id': request.id,
                        'differences': comparison.differences,
                        'old_result': old_result,
                        'new_result': new_result
                    }
                )
                
                self.metrics.increment(f'{self.service_name}.comparison.mismatch')

            self.metrics.increment(f'{self.service_name}.comparison.timeout')
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"New {self.service_name} failed: {e}")
            self.metrics.increment(f'{self.service_name}.comparison.error')

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import Set, Optional
import hashlib
import hmac

class Permission(Enum):
    READ_TEMPLATES = "read_templates"
    CREATE_PROMPTS = "create_prompts"
    APPROVE_PROMPTS = "approve_prompts"
    MANAGE_USERS = "manage_users"
    ACCESS_AUDIT_LOGS = "access_audit_logs"
    CONFIGURE_GUARDRAILS = "configure_guardrails"

class Role(Enum):
    VIEWER = "viewer"
    DEVELOPER = "developer"
    REVIEWER = "reviewer"
    ADMIN = "admin"
    AUDITOR = "auditor"

@dataclass
class User:
    id: str
    email: str
    roles: Set[Role]
    department: str
    api_key_hash: Optional[str] = None

class AccessControlManager:
    ROLE_PERMISSIONS = {
        Role.VIEWER: {
            Permission.READ_TEMPLATES,
        },
        Role.DEVELOPER: {
            Permission.READ_TEMPLATES,
            Permission.CREATE_PROMPTS,
        },
        Role.REVIEWER: {
            Permission.READ_TEMPLATES,
            Permission.CREATE_PROMPTS,
            Permission.APPROVE_PROMPTS,
        },
        Role.ADMIN: set(Permission),  # All permissions
        Role.AUDITOR: {
            Permission.READ_TEMPLATES,
            Permission.ACCESS_AUDIT_LOGS,
        }
    }
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.users = {}
        
    def has_permission(self, user: User, permission: Permission) -> bool:
        """Check if user has specific permission"""
        for role in user.roles:
            if permission in self.ROLE_PERMISSIONS.get(role, set()):
                return True
        return False
    
    def generate_api_key(self, user: User, secret: str) -> str:
        """Generate secure API key for user"""
        data = f"{user.id}:{user.email}:{secret}"
        return hmac.new(
            secret.encode(),
            data.encode(),
            hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest()
    
    def validate_api_key(self, api_key: str, user_id: str) -> bool:
        """Validate API key for user"""
        user = self.users.get(user_id)
        if not user or not user.api_key_hash:
            return False
        return hmac.compare_digest(user.api_key_hash, api_key)

# Usage

            SELECT * FROM audit_events
            WHERE event_type IN ('guardrail_triggered', 'permission_changed')
            AND timestamp > ?
            ORDER BY timestamp DESC
        """, (start_time.isoformat(),))
        
        return [dict(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
    
    def generate_compliance_report(
        self,
        start_date: datetime,
        end_date: datetime
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Generate compliance report"""
        cursor = self.conn.execute("""
            SELECT 
                event_type,
                COUNT(*) as count,
                SUM(CASE WHEN success = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as success_count,
                SUM(CASE WHEN success = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failure_count
            FROM audit_events
            WHERE timestamp BETWEEN ? AND ?
            GROUP BY event_type
        """, (start_date.isoformat(), end_date.isoformat()))
        
        return {
            "period": {
                "start": start_date.isoformat(),
                "end": end_date.isoformat()
            },
            "events": [dict(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
        }

```python
from typing import List, Tuple, Optional
import re
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

class GuardrailResult:
    def __init__(
        self,
        passed: bool,
        guardrail_name: str,
        severity: str = "info",
        message: str = "",
        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    ):
        self.passed = passed
        self.guardrail_name = guardrail_name
        self.severity = severity
        self.message = message
        self.metadata = metadata or {}

class Guardrail(ABC):
    def __init__(self, name: str, enabled: bool = True):
        self.name = name
        self.enabled = enabled
    
    @abstractmethod
    def check(self, prompt: str, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> GuardrailResult:
        pass

class PIIDetectionGuardrail(Guardrail):
    """Detect and block personally identifiable information"""
    
    PII_PATTERNS = {
        'email': r'\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b',
        'ssn': r'\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b',
        'phone': r'\b\d{3}[-.]?\d{3}[-.]?\d{4}\b',
        'credit_card': r'\b\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}\b'
    }
    
    def check(self, prompt: str, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> GuardrailResult:
        detected_pii = []
        
        for pii_type, pattern in self.PII_PATTERNS.items():
            if re.search(pattern, prompt):
                detected_pii.append(pii_type)
        
        if detected_pii:
            return GuardrailResult(
                passed=False,
                guardrail_name=self.name,
                severity="high",
                message=f"PII detected: {', '.join(detected_pii)}",
                metadata={"pii_types": detected_pii}
            )
        
        return GuardrailResult(
            passed=True,
            guardrail_name=self.name,
            message="No PII detected"
        )

class ToxicityGuardrail(Guardrail):
    """Detect toxic, harmful, or inappropriate content"""
    
    TOXIC_KEYWORDS = [
        # Add your toxic keyword list
    ]
    
    def check(self, prompt: str, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> GuardrailResult:
        prompt_lower = prompt.lower()
        detected = [kw for kw in self.TOXIC_KEYWORDS if kw in prompt_lower]
        
        if detected:
            return GuardrailResult(
                passed=False,
                guardrail_name=self.name,
                severity="high",
                message="Toxic content detected",
                metadata={"matched_keywords": detected}
            )
        
        return GuardrailResult(
            passed=True,
            guardrail_name=self.name
        )

class PromptInjectionGuardrail(Guardrail):
    """Detect prompt injection attempts"""
    
    INJECTION_PATTERNS = [
        r'ignore\s+(previous|above|all)\s+instructions',
        r'disregard\s+',
        r'new\s+instructions',
        r'system\s*:',
        r'<\|.*?\|>',  # Special tokens
    ]
    
    def check(self, prompt: str, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> GuardrailResult:
        prompt_lower = prompt.lower()
        
        for pattern in self.INJECTION_PATTERNS:
            if re.search(pattern, prompt_lower, re.IGNORECASE):
                return GuardrailResult(
                    passed=False,
                    guardrail_name=self.name,
                    severity="critical",
                    message="Potential prompt injection detected",
                    metadata={"pattern": pattern}
                )
        
        return GuardrailResult(
            passed=True,
            guardrail_name=self.name
        )

class TokenLimitGuardrail(Guardrail):
    """Enforce token limits"""
    
    def __init__(self, name: str, max_tokens: int = 4000):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
    
    def check(self, prompt: str, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> GuardrailResult:
        # Rough estimation: 1 token ≈ 4 characters
        estimated_tokens = len(prompt) // 4
        
        if estimated_tokens > self.max_tokens:
            return GuardrailResult(
                passed=False,
                guardrail_name=self.name,
                severity="medium",
                message=f"Token limit exceeded: {estimated_tokens}/{self.max_tokens}",
                metadata={"estimated_tokens": estimated_tokens}
            )
        
        return GuardrailResult(
            passed=True,
            guardrail_name=self.name,
            metadata={"estimated_tokens": estimated_tokens}
        )

class CostLimitGuardrail(Guardrail):
    """Enforce cost limits per execution"""
    
    def __init__(self, name: str, max_cost_usd: float = 0.50):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.max_cost_usd = max_cost_usd
    
    def check(self, prompt: str, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> GuardrailResult:
        estimated_cost = context.get('estimated_cost', 0)
        
        if estimated_cost > self.max_cost_usd:
            return GuardrailResult(
                passed=False,
                guardrail_name=self.name,
                severity="medium",
                message=f"Cost limit exceeded: ${estimated_cost:.4f}/${self.max_cost_usd}",
                metadata={"estimated_cost": estimated_cost}
            )
        
        return GuardrailResult(
            passed=True,
            guardrail_name=self.name,
            metadata={"estimated_cost": estimated_cost}
        )

class GuardrailEngine:
    def __init__(self, audit_logger: AuditLogger):
        self.guardrails: List[Guardrail] = []
        self.audit_logger = audit_logger
    
    def add_guardrail(self, guardrail: Guardrail):
        """Add guardrail to engine"""
        self.guardrails.append(guardrail)
    
    def check_all(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        context: Dict[str, Any],
        user_id: str,
        prompt_id: str
    ) -> Tuple[bool, List[GuardrailResult]]:
        """Run all enabled guardrails"""
        results = []
        all_passed = True
        
        for guardrail in self.guardrails:
            if not guardrail.enabled:
                continue
            
            result = guardrail.check(prompt, context)
            results.append(result)
            
            if not result.passed:
                all_passed = False
                
                # Log violation
                self.audit_logger.log_guardrail_violation(
                    user_id=user_id,
                    prompt_id=prompt_id,
                    guardrail_name=guardrail.name,
                    violation_type=result.message,
                    severity=result.severity,
                    blocked=True
                )
        
        return all_passed, results

# Initialize guardrail engine
guardrail_engine = GuardrailEngine(audit_logger)
guardrail_engine.add_guardrail(PIIDetectionGuardrail("pii_detection"))
guardrail_engine.add_guardrail(ToxicityGuardrail("toxicity_check"))
guardrail_engine.add_guardrail(PromptInjectionGuardrail("injection_detection"))

guardrail_engine.add_guardrail(CostLimitGuardrail("cost_limit", max_cost_usd=0.50))

# region_selector.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Dict
import boto3
import requests

@dataclass
class RegionMetrics:
    region: str
    avg_latency: float
    availability: float
    cost_index: float
    compliance_score: int

class RegionSelector:
    def __init__(self, requirements: Dict):
        self.requirements = requirements
        self.cloudwatch = boto3.client('cloudwatch')
        
    def evaluate_regions(self, candidate_regions: List[str]) -> List[RegionMetrics]:
        """Evaluate regions based on latency, availability, cost, and compliance"""
        metrics = []
        
        for region in candidate_regions:
            latency = self._measure_latency(region)
            availability = self._get_availability_stats(region)
            cost = self._get_cost_index(region)
            compliance = self._check_compliance(region)
            
            metrics.append(RegionMetrics(
                region=region,
                avg_latency=latency,
                availability=availability,
                cost_index=cost,
                compliance_score=compliance
            ))
        
        return sorted(metrics, key=lambda x: self._calculate_score(x), reverse=True)
    
    def _measure_latency(self, region: str) -> float:
        """Measure latency from user locations to region"""
        test_endpoints = {
            'us-east-1': 'dynamodb.us-east-1.amazonaws.com',
            'eu-west-1': 'dynamodb.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com',
            'ap-southeast-1': 'dynamodb.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com'
        }
        
        latencies = []
        for _ in range(10):
            try:
                response = requests.get(
                    f"https://{test_endpoints[region]}",
                    timeout=5
                )
                latencies.append(response.elapsed.total_seconds() * 1000)
            except:
                latencies.append(5000)  # Timeout penalty
        
        return sum(latencies) / len(latencies)
    
    def _get_availability_stats(self, region: str) -> float:
        """Get historical availability from CloudWatch"""
        response = self.cloudwatch.get_metric_statistics(
            Namespace='AWS/EC2',
            MetricName='StatusCheckFailed',
            Dimensions=[{'Name': 'Region', 'Value': region}],
            StartTime='2024-01-01',
            EndTime='2024-12-31',
            Period=86400,
            Statistics=['Average']
        )
        
        if response['Datapoints']:
            failures = sum(dp['Average'] for dp in response['Datapoints'])
            return (1 - failures / len(response['Datapoints'])) * 100
        return 99.9  # Default
    
    def _calculate_score(self, metrics: RegionMetrics) -> float:
        """Calculate weighted score for region selection"""
        weights = {
            'latency': 0.35,
            'availability': 0.30,
            'cost': 0.20,
            'compliance': 0.15
        }
        
        # Normalize and invert where necessary
        latency_score = max(0, 100 - metrics.avg_latency / 10)
        availability_score = metrics.availability
        cost_score = max(0, 100 - metrics.cost_index)
        compliance_score = metrics.compliance_score
        
        return (
            latency_score * weights['latency'] +
            availability_score * weights['availability'] +
            cost_score * weights['cost'] +
            compliance_score * weights['compliance']
        )

        self.pools = {}
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    
    async def initialize_pools(self):
        """Create connection pools for all regions"""
        for region, db_config in self.config['regions'].items():
            self.pools[region] = await asyncpg.create_pool(
                host=db_config['host'],
                port=db_config['port'],
                database=db_config['database'],
                user=db_config['user'],
                password=db_config['password'],
                min_size=10,
                max_size=100,
                command_timeout=60
            )
            self.logger.info(f"Initialized pool for region: {region}")
    
    async def write_with_replication(
        self, 
        query: str, 
        params: tuple,
        consistency: str = 'eventual'
    ) -> Dict:
        """Write to primary and replicate to secondaries"""
        primary_region = self.config['primary']
        
        # Write to primary
        async with self.pools[primary_region].acquire() as conn:
            async with conn.transaction():
                result = await conn.execute(query, *params)
                write_lsn = await conn.fetchval(
                    "SELECT pg_current_wal_lsn()"
                )
        
        # Handle replication based on consistency requirement
        if consistency == 'strong':
            await self._wait_for_replication(write_lsn)
        elif consistency == 'eventual':
            asyncio.create_task(self._verify_replication(write_lsn))
        
        return {
            'status': 'success',
            'lsn': write_lsn,
            'consistency': consistency
        }
    
    async def _wait_for_replication(self, target_lsn: str):
        """Wait for all replicas to catch up (strong consistency)"""
        tasks = []
        for region, pool in self.pools.items():
            if region != self.config['primary']:
                tasks.append(self._check_replica_lag(pool, target_lsn))
        
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
    
    async def _check_replica_lag(
        self, 
        pool: asyncpg.Pool, 
        target_lsn: str,
        timeout: int = 10
    ):
        """Check if replica has caught up to target LSN"""
        start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
        
        while asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - start_time < timeout:
            async with pool.acquire() as conn:
                current_lsn = await conn.fetchval(
                    "SELECT pg_last_wal_replay_lsn()"
                )
                
                if current_lsn >= target_lsn:
                    return True
            
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        
        raise TimeoutError(f"Replica did not catch up within {timeout}s")
    
    async def read_from_nearest(
        self, 
        query: str, 
        params: tuple,
        user_region: str
    ) -> List[Dict]:
        """Read from geographically nearest replica"""
        region = self._select_read_region(user_region)
        
        async with self.pools[region].acquire() as conn:
            rows = await conn.fetch(query, *params)
            return [dict(row) for row in rows]
    
    def _select_read_region(self, user_region: str) -> str:
        """Select best region for read based on user location"""
        region_mapping = {
            'us': 'us-east-1',
            'eu': 'eu-west-1',
            'asia': 'ap-southeast-1'
        }
        return region_mapping.get(user_region, self.config['primary'])

### Intelligent Traffic Routing Service

```go
// traffic_router.go
package router

import (
    "context"
    "time"
    "sync"
    "math"
)

type Region struct {
    ID           string
    Endpoint     string
    Latency      time.Duration
    ErrorRate    float64
    Capacity     int
    CurrentLoad  int
    HealthStatus string
}

type TrafficRouter struct {
    regions      map[string]*Region
    metrics      *MetricsCollector
    mu           sync.RWMutex
    updateTicker *time.Ticker
}

func NewTrafficRouter(regions []Region) *TrafficRouter {
    tr := &TrafficRouter{
        regions:      make(map[string]*Region),
        metrics:      NewMetricsCollector(),
        updateTicker: time.NewTicker(10 * time.Second),
    }
    
    for _, r := range regions {
        region := r
        tr.regions[r.ID] = &region
    }
    
    go tr.updateMetrics()
    
    return tr
}

func (tr *TrafficRouter) SelectRegion(
    ctx context.Context,
    userLocation string,
    requirements *RoutingRequirements,
) (*Region, error) {
    tr.mu.RLock()
    defer tr.mu.RUnlock()
    
    candidates := tr.filterHealthyRegions()
    
    if len(candidates) == 0 {
        return nil, ErrNoHealthyRegions
    }
    
    // Apply routing strategy
    switch requirements.Strategy {
    case "latency":
        return tr.selectByLatency(candidates, userLocation), nil
    case "cost":
        return tr.selectByCost(candidates), nil
    case "load":
        return tr.selectByLoad(candidates), nil
    default:
        return tr.selectWeighted(candidates, userLocation), nil
    }
}

func (tr *TrafficRouter) selectWeighted(
    regions []*Region,
    userLocation string,
) *Region {
    type scoredRegion struct {
        region *Region
        score  float64
    }
    
    scored := make([]scoredRegion, 0, len(regions))
    
    for _, r := range regions {
        score := tr.calculateScore(r, userLocation)
        scored = append(scored, scoredRegion{region: r, score: score})
    }
    
    // Sort by score
    sort.Slice(scored, func(i, j int) bool {
        return scored[i].score > scored[j].score
    })
    
    return scored[0].region
}

func (tr *TrafficRouter) calculateScore(
    region *Region,
    userLocation string,
) float64 {
    weights := struct {
        latency   float64
        errorRate float64
        load      float64
    }{
        latency:   0.40,
        errorRate: 0.35,
        load:      0.25,
    }
    
    // Normalize metrics (0-100 scale)
    latencyScore := math.Max(0, 100 - float64(region.Latency.Milliseconds()))
    errorRateScore := (1 - region.ErrorRate) * 100
    loadScore := (1 - float64(region.CurrentLoad)/float64(region.Capacity)) * 100
    
    totalScore := (
        latencyScore * weights.latency +
        errorRateScore * weights.errorRate +
        loadScore * weights.load
    )
    
    return totalScore
}

func (tr *TrafficRouter) updateMetrics() {
    for range tr.updateTicker.C {
        tr.mu.Lock()
        
        for _, region := range tr.regions {
            // Update latency
            latency, err := tr.metrics.MeasureLatency(region.Endpoint)
            if err == nil {
                region.Latency = latency
            }
            
            // Update error rate
            errorRate := tr.metrics.GetErrorRate(region.ID)
            region.ErrorRate = errorRate
            
            // Update load
            load := tr.metrics.GetCurrentLoad(region.ID)
            region.CurrentLoad = load
            
            // Update health status
            health := tr.metrics.CheckHealth(region.Endpoint)
            region.HealthStatus = health
        }
        
        tr.mu.Unlock()
    }
}

func (tr *TrafficRouter) filterHealthyRegions() []*Region {
    healthy := make([]*Region, 0)
    
    for _, r := range tr.regions {
        if r.HealthStatus == "healthy" && r.ErrorRate < 0.05 {
            healthy = append(healthy, r)
        }
    }
    
    return healthy
}

### Circuit Breaker Implementation

```python
# circuit_breaker.py
from enum import Enum
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Callable, Any
import asyncio
import logging

class CircuitState(Enum):
    CLOSED = "closed"  # Normal operation
    OPEN = "open"      # Failing, reject requests
    HALF_OPEN = "half_open"  # Testing recovery

class CircuitBreaker:
    def __init__(
        self,
        failure_threshold: int = 5,
        success_threshold: int = 2,
        timeout: int = 60,
        expected_exception: type = Exception
    ):
        self.failure_threshold = failure_threshold
        self.success_threshold = success_threshold
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.expected_exception = expected_exception
        
        self.failure_count = 0
        self.success_count = 0
        self.last_failure_time = None
        self.state = CircuitState.CLOSED
        
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    
    async def call(self, func: Callable, *args, **kwargs) -> Any:
        """Execute function with circuit breaker protection"""
        if self.state == CircuitState.OPEN:
            if self._should_attempt_reset():
                self.state = CircuitState.HALF_OPEN
                self.logger.info("Circuit breaker entering HALF_OPEN state")
            else:
                raise CircuitBreakerOpenError(
                    f"Circuit breaker is OPEN. Last failure: {self.last_failure_time}"
                )
        
        try:
            result = await func(*args, **kwargs)
            self._on_success()
            return result
        
        except self.expected_exception as e:
            self._on_failure()
            raise
    
    def _on_success(self):
        """Handle successful execution"""
        if self.state == CircuitState.HALF_OPEN:
            self.success_count += 1
            
            if self.success_count >= self.success_threshold:
                self._reset()
                self.logger.info("Circuit breaker CLOSED after recovery")
        else:
            self.failure_count = 0
    
    def _on_failure(self):
        """Handle failed execution"""
        self.failure_count += 1
        self.last_failure_time = datetime.now()
        self.success_count = 0
        
        if self.failure_count >= self.failure_threshold:
            self.state = CircuitState.OPEN
            self.logger.error(
                f"Circuit breaker OPENED after {self.failure_count} failures"
            )
    
    def _should_attempt_reset(self) -> bool:
        """Check if enough time has passed to attempt reset"""
        return (
            self.last_failure_time is not None and
            datetime.now() - self.last_failure_time >= timedelta(seconds=self.timeout)
        )
    
    def _reset(self):
        """Reset circuit breaker to closed state"""
        self.state = CircuitState.CLOSED
        self.failure_count = 0
        self.success_count = 0
        self.last_failure_time = None

# Multi-region circuit breaker manager
class RegionCircuitBreakerManager:
    def __init__(self, regions: list):
        self.circuit_breakers = {
            region: CircuitBreaker(
                failure_threshold=5,
                success_threshold=2,
                timeout=60
            )
            for region in regions
        }
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    
    async def call_with_failover(
        self,
        func: Callable,
        regions: list,
        *args,
        **kwargs
    ) -> Any:
        """Try regions in order until success"""
        last_exception = None
        
        for region in regions:
            cb = self.circuit_breakers[region]
            
            try:
                result = await cb.call(func, region, *args, **kwargs)
                return result
            
            except CircuitBreakerOpenError:
                self.logger.warning(f"Circuit breaker open for region: {region}")
                continue
            
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.error(f"Error calling region {region}: {str(e)}")
                last_exception = e
                continue
        
        raise AllRegionsFailedError(
            "All regions failed or have open circuit breakers",
            last_exception
        )

class CircuitBreakerOpenError(Exception):
    pass

class AllRegionsFailedError(Exception):
    pass

### Flag Types & Usage

```typescript
// Feature flag implementation
interface FeatureFlag {
  name: string;
  type: 'release' | 'experiment' | 'operational' | 'permission';
  scope: 'global' | 'tenant' | 'user';
  dependencies?: string[];
  killSwitch: boolean;
}

class FeatureFlagService {
  // Progressive rollout
  async evaluateFlag(
    flagName: string, 
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): Promise<FlagVariation> {
    const flag = await this.getFlag(flagName);
    
    // Check kill switch first
    if (flag.killSwitch && await this.isKillSwitchActive(flagName)) {
      return flag.defaultVariation;
    }
    
    // Evaluate targeting rules
    const segment = await this.identifySegment(context.tenantId);
    const rule = this.matchTargetingRule(flag, segment);
    
    // Check rollout percentage
    if (rule.rolloutPercentage) {
      const bucket = this.calculateBucket(context.tenantId);
      if (bucket > rule.rolloutPercentage) {
        return flag.defaultVariation;
      }
    }
    
    return rule.variation;
  }
  
  // Consistent bucketing for gradual rollouts
  private calculateBucket(tenantId: string): number {
    const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256')
      .update(tenantId)
      .digest('hex');
    return (parseInt(hash.substring(0, 8), 16) % 100);
  }
}
```

### Segmentation Model

```python
from enum import Enum
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Dict

class TenantTier(Enum):
    INTERNAL = "internal"
    BETA = "beta"
    STARTUP = "startup"
    GROWTH = "growth"
    ENTERPRISE = "enterprise"

class RiskProfile(Enum):
    LOW = "low"           # Can tolerate issues
    MEDIUM = "medium"     # Standard SLA
    HIGH = "high"         # Premium SLA
    CRITICAL = "critical" # Mission-critical, 24/7

@dataclass
class TenantSegment:
    id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    tier: TenantTier
    risk_profile: RiskProfile
    size_category: str  # small, medium, large
    usage_pattern: str  # light, moderate, heavy
    rollout_wave: int
    
class TenantSegmentationService:
    def segment_tenants(self) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
        """Segment tenants for staged rollout"""
        
        segments = {
            "wave_0_internal": self.get_tenants(
                tier=TenantTier.INTERNAL,
                rollout_wave=0
            ),
            
            "wave_1_beta_low_risk": self.get_tenants(
                tier=TenantTier.BETA,
                risk_profile=RiskProfile.LOW,
                rollout_wave=1
            ),
            
            "wave_2_startup_medium_usage": self.get_tenants(
                tier=TenantTier.STARTUP,
                usage_pattern="moderate",
                rollout_wave=2
            ),
            
            "wave_3_growth_standard": self.get_tenants(
                tier=TenantTier.GROWTH,
                risk_profile=[RiskProfile.LOW, RiskProfile.MEDIUM],
                rollout_wave=3
            ),
            
            "wave_4_enterprise_low_risk": self.get_tenants(
                tier=TenantTier.ENTERPRISE,
                risk_profile=RiskProfile.LOW,
                size_category="small",
                rollout_wave=4
            ),
            
            "wave_5_remaining": self.get_tenants(
                rollout_wave=5
            )
        }
        
        return segments
    
    def calculate_rollout_risk(self, tenant_id: str) -> float:
        """Calculate risk score for tenant"""
        tenant = self.get_tenant(tenant_id)
        
        risk_factors = {
            'contract_value': self.normalize_contract_value(tenant),
            'usage_volume': self.normalize_usage(tenant),
            'support_history': self.analyze_support_tickets(tenant),
            'customizations': self.count_customizations(tenant),
            'integration_complexity': self.assess_integrations(tenant),
            'churn_risk': self.get_churn_score(tenant)
        }
        
        weights = {
            'contract_value': 0.25,
            'usage_volume': 0.15,
            'support_history': 0.20,
            'customizations': 0.15,
            'integration_complexity': 0.15,
            'churn_risk': 0.10
        }
        
        risk_score = sum(
            risk_factors[k] * weights[k] 
            for k in risk_factors
        )
        
        return risk_score

describe('API Version Compatibility', () => {

        });
        
        it('should handle feature toggles gracefully', async () => {
          const client = createClient(clientVersion);

          await setFeatureFlag('new_feature', true);

          // Test with feature off

          const responseOff = await client.useFeature(apiVersion);
          
          // Both should succeed, just different behavior

class MigrationCompatibilityTest {
  async testBackwardCompatibility(tenantId: string) {
    // Ensure old code can read new data format
    const newData = await this.fetchDataWithNewAPI(tenantId);
    const oldAPI = new LegacyAPIClient();
    
    try {
      const readResult = await oldAPI.readData(newData);
      return {
        compatible: true,
        data: readResult
      };
    } catch (error) {
      return {
        compatible: false,
        error: error.message
      };
    }

class DeploymentStrategy(Enum):

class DeploymentOrchestrator:
    def __init__(self, metrics_service, notification_service):
        self.metrics = metrics_service
        self.notifications = notification_service
        self.active_deployments = {}
    
    async def deploy_to_segment(
        self,
        version: str,
        segment: str,
        strategy: DeploymentStrategy,
        config: Dict
    ) -> DeploymentResult:
        """Deploy new version to a tenant segment"""
        
        deployment_id = f"{version}-{segment}-{timestamp()}"
        
        try:
            # Pre-deployment validation
            await self.validate_deployment(version, segment)
            
            # Create deployment
            deployment = Deployment(
                id=deployment_id,
                version=version,
                segment=segment,
                strategy=strategy,
                config=config
            )
            
            self.active_deployments[deployment_id] = deployment
            
            # Execute deployment strategy
            if strategy == DeploymentStrategy.BLUE_GREEN:
                result = await self.blue_green_deploy(deployment)
            elif strategy == DeploymentStrategy.ROLLING:
                result = await self.rolling_deploy(deployment)
            elif strategy == DeploymentStrategy.CANARY:
                result = await self.canary_deploy(deployment)
            elif strategy == DeploymentStrategy.GRADUAL_ROLLOUT:
                result = await self.gradual_rollout_deploy(deployment)
            
            # Post-deployment validation
            await self.validate_deployment_health(deployment_id)
            
            # Notify stakeholders
            await self.notifications.send_deployment_success(
                deployment_id, 
                segment
            )
            
            return result
            
        except DeploymentException as e:
            await self.handle_deployment_failure(deployment_id, e)
            raise
    
    async def gradual_rollout_deploy(
        self,
        deployment: Deployment
    ) -> DeploymentResult:
        """Gradually roll out to increasing percentages"""
        
        percentages = deployment.config.get('percentages', [10, 25, 50, 100])
        pause_duration = deployment.config.get('pause_between_steps', 24 * 3600)
        
        tenants = await self.get_segment_tenants(deployment.segment)
        
        for percentage in percentages:
            # Calculate tenant subset
            target_count = int(len(tenants) * percentage / 100)
            target_tenants = tenants[:target_count]
            
            print(f"Deploying to {percentage}% ({target_count} tenants)")
            
            # Deploy to subset
            await self.deploy_to_tenants(
                deployment.version,
                target_tenants
            )
            
            # Monitor deployment health
            health_check = await self.monitor_deployment_health(
                deployment.id,
                duration=pause_duration
            )
            
            if not health_check.passed:
                # Rollback if health check fails
                await self.rollback_deployment(deployment.id)
                raise DeploymentException(
                    f"Health check failed at {percentage}%: {health_check.reason}"
                )
            
            # Pause before next step (unless final step)
            if percentage < 100:
                print(f"Pausing for {pause_duration}s before next step")
                await asyncio.sleep(pause_duration)
        
        return DeploymentResult(
            deployment_id=deployment.id,
            status="success",
            tenants_upgraded=len(tenants)
        )
    
    async def canary_deploy(self, deployment: Deployment) -> DeploymentResult:
        """Canary deployment with traffic splitting"""
        
        canary_percentage = deployment.config.get('canary_percentage', 10)
        canary_duration = deployment.config.get('canary_duration', 3600)
        
        # Deploy canary version
        await self.deploy_canary_version(
            deployment.version,
            canary_percentage
        )
        
        # Monitor canary metrics
        canary_metrics = await self.monitor_canary(
            deployment.id,
            duration=canary_duration
        )
        
        # Compare canary vs baseline
        comparison = self.compare_metrics(
            canary_metrics,
            await self.get_baseline_metrics()
        )
        
        if comparison.is_acceptable:
            # Promote canary to full rollout
            await self.promote_canary(deployment.id)
            return DeploymentResult(status="success")
        else:
            # Terminate canary
            await self.terminate_canary(deployment.id)
            raise DeploymentException(
                f"Canary metrics unacceptable: {comparison.reason}"

class TrafficRouter {

  private tenantRegistry: TenantRegistry;
  
  async routeRequest(request: Request): Promise<Route> {
    const tenantId = this.extractTenantId(request);
    const tenant = await this.tenantRegistry.getTenant(tenantId);

    const useNewVersion = await this.featureFlags.evaluateFlag(

      return {
        version: 'v2',
        backend: this.getV2Backend(),
        headers: { 'X-App-Version': '2.0' }
      };
    } else {
      return {
        version: 'v1',
        backend: this.getV1Backend(),
        headers: { 'X-App-Version': '1.0' }
      };
    }
  }
  
  // Shadow traffic for testing
  async shadowRequest(request: Request): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = this.extractTenantId(request);

    const shadowEnabled = await this.featureFlags.evaluateFlag(
      'shadow_traffic_v2',
      { tenantId }
    );
    
    if (shadowEnabled) {
      // Send copy of request to new version (don't await)
      this.sendShadowRequest(request).catch(error => {
        // Log shadow errors but don't impact primary request
        this.logShadowError(tenantId, error);

    }
  }

// src/commands/command-handler.ts
import { DomainEvent } from '../core/events/base-event';

export interface Command {
  commandId: string;
  commandType: string;
  aggregateId: string;
  userId: string;
  timestamp: string;
  data: any;
}

export interface CommandResult {
  success: boolean;
  aggregateId: string;
  version: number;
  events?: DomainEvent[];
  error?: string;
}

export abstract class CommandHandler<T extends Command> {
  abstract handle(command: T): Promise<CommandResult>;
  abstract validate(command: T): Promise<boolean>;
}

// src/commands/validators/command-validator.ts
export class CommandValidator {
  private rules: Map<string, ValidationRule[]> = new Map();

  registerRule(commandType: string, rule: ValidationRule): void {
    if (!this.rules.has(commandType)) {
      this.rules.set(commandType, []);
    }
    this.rules.get(commandType)!.push(rule);
  }

  async validate(command: Command): Promise<ValidationResult> {
    const rules = this.rules.get(command.commandType) || [];
    const errors: string[] = [];

    for (const rule of rules) {
      const result = await rule.validate(command);
      if (!result.valid) {
        errors.push(result.error!);
      }
    }

    return {
      valid: errors.length === 0,
      errors,
    };
  }
}

export interface ValidationRule {
  validate(command: Command): Promise<ValidationResult>;
}

export interface ValidationResult {
  valid: boolean;
  error?: string;
  errors?: string[];
}

    public readonly accountData: {
      accountNumber: string;
      initialBalance: number;
      currency: string;
      ownerName: string;
    },
    correlationId?: string,
    userId?: string
  ) {
    super(accountNumber, 'Account', 1, 'AccountCreated', correlationId, undefined, userId);
  }

// src/domains/account/handlers/create-account.handler.ts
export class CreateAccountHandler extends CommandHandler<CreateAccountCommand> {
  constructor(
    private eventStore: EventStore,
    private validator: CommandValidator
  ) {
    super();
  }

  async validate(command: CreateAccountCommand): Promise<boolean> {
    // Check if account already exists
    const events = await this.eventStore.getEvents(command.data.accountNumber);
    if (events.length > 0) {
      throw new Error('Account already exists');
    }

    // Validate command data
    const result = await this.validator.validate(command);
    if (!result.valid) {
      throw new Error(`Validation failed: ${result.errors?.join(', ')}`);
    }

    return true;
  }

  async handle(command: CreateAccountCommand): Promise<CommandResult> {
    try {
      await this.validate(command);

      const event = new AccountCreatedEvent(
        command.data.accountNumber,
        command.data,
        command.commandId,
        command.userId
      );

      await this.eventStore.appendEvent(event);

      return {
        success: true,
        aggregateId: command.aggregateId,
        version: 1,
        events: [event],
      };
    } catch (error) {
      return {
        success: false,
        aggregateId: command.aggregateId,
        version: 0,
        error: (error as Error).message,
      };
    }
  }
}
