# GraphQL Federation Rollout Guide

## 1. Schema Composition & Design

### Entity-Based Architecture

```graphql
# Users Service (owns User entity)
type User @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  email: String!
  name: String!
  # Reference to Reviews (owned by another service)
  reviews: [Review!]!
}

# Products Service (owns Product entity)
type Product @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  sku: String!
  name: String!
  price: Money!
}

# Reviews Service (extends both User and Product)
extend type User @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID! @external
  reviews: [Review!]!
}

extend type Product @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID! @external
  reviews: [Review!]!
  averageRating: Float
}

type Review @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  rating: Int!
  content: String!
  author: User!
  product: Product!
}
```

```typescript
    reviews: (product: { id: string }) => {
```

### Connection Pooling & Batching

```typescript
// Subgraph with DataLoader for batching
import DataLoader from 'dataloader';

interface Context {
  loaders: {
    users: DataLoader<string, User>;
    products: DataLoader<string, Product>;
  };
}

  return {

        return ids.map(id => users.find(u => u.id === id));
      }),
```

### Entity Caching

```typescript
// Subgraph with entity caching
import { CacheHint } from '@apollo/cache-control-types';

export const resolvers = {
  Query: {
    product: (_, { id }, __, info) => {
      // Cache this entity for 5 minutes
      info.cacheControl.setCacheHint({ maxAge: 300 });
      return productService.findById(id);
    },
  },
  
  Product: {
    __resolveReference(ref, { cache }) {
      const cacheKey = `product:${ref.id}`;
      
      return cache.get(cacheKey).then(cached => {
        if (cached) return cached;
        
        return productService.findById(ref.id).then(product => {
          cache.set(cacheKey, product, { ttl: 300 });
          return product;
        });
      });
    },
  },
};
```

```graphql
  products: [Product!]! @cacheControl(maxAge: 3600)

}

  # More volatile field
```

### Invalidation Strategy

```typescript
// Cache invalidation service
class CacheInvalidator {
  constructor(private redis: Redis) {}
  
  async invalidateEntity(typename: string, id: string) {
    const pattern = `${typename}:${id}*`;
    const keys = await this.redis.keys(pattern);
    
    if (keys.length > 0) {
      await this.redis.del(...keys);
    }
    
    // Publish to other instances
    await this.redis.publish('cache:invalidate', 
      JSON.stringify({ typename, id })
    );
  }
  
  async handleProductUpdate(productId: string) {
    await Promise.all([
      this.invalidateEntity('Product', productId),
      // Invalidate related entities
      this.invalidateEntity('Review', `product:${productId}`),
    ]);
  }
}

// In mutation resolver
const resolvers = {
  Mutation: {
    updateProduct: async (_, { id, input }, { cacheInvalidator }) => {
      const product = await productService.update(id, input);
      await cacheInvalidator.handleProductUpdate(id);
      return product;
    },
  },
};
```

```typescript
      try {
        return await reviewService.findByUserId(user.id);
      } catch (error) {

        logger.error('Failed to fetch reviews', { userId: user.id, error });
        return null;
      }

};
```

### Circuit Breaker Pattern

```typescript
import CircuitBreaker from 'opossum';

class SubgraphClient {
  private breaker: CircuitBreaker;
  
  constructor(private url: string) {
    this.breaker = new CircuitBreaker(this.fetch.bind(this), {
      timeout: 3000,
      errorThresholdPercentage: 50,
      resetTimeout: 30000,
    });
    
    this.breaker.on('open', () => {
      logger.error(`Circuit breaker opened for ${this.url}`);
    });
  }
  
  async query(query: string, variables?: any) {
    try {
      return await this.breaker.fire(query, variables);
    } catch (error) {
      // Circuit is open, return degraded response
      throw new Error('Service temporarily unavailable');
    }
  }
  
  private async fetch(query: string, variables?: any) {
    const response = await fetch(this.url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
    });
    
    return response.json();
  }
}
```

### Error Extensions & Classification

```typescript
import { GraphQLError } from 'graphql';

// Custom error classes
export class UserFacingError extends GraphQLError {
  constructor(message: string, code: string, extensions?: Record<string, any>) {
    super(message, {
      extensions: {
        code,
        ...extensions,
      },
    });
  }
}

export const resolvers = {
  Mutation: {
    createOrder: async (_, { input }, context) => {
      // Validate permissions
      if (!context.user) {
        throw new UserFacingError(
          'You must be logged in',
          'UNAUTHENTICATED'
        );
      }
      
      // Validate input
      const errors = validateOrderInput(input);
      if (errors.length > 0) {
        throw new UserFacingError(
          'Invalid order data',
          'BAD_USER_INPUT',
          { validationErrors: errors }
        );
      }
      
      try {
        return await orderService.create(input);
      } catch (error) {
        // Don't expose internal errors
        logger.error('Order creation failed', { error, input });
        throw new UserFacingError(
          'Failed to create order',
          'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR'
        );
      }
    },
  },
};
```

### Gateway Error Handling

```yaml
    all:

      include_messages: true
      errors:
        - subgraph_request_error

  redact:
```

### Timeout & Fallback

```typescript

export const resolvers = {
```

```typescript
const monitoringPlugin: ApolloServerPlugin = {
```

# Zero-Trust TLS Everywhere: Comprehensive Guide

## Overview of Zero-Trust Architecture

Zero-trust assumes **no implicit trust** based on network location. Every service-to-service connection must be authenticated, authorized, and encrypted.

## 1. mTLS Issuance

### Architecture Components

```yaml
# SPIRE Server Configuration
server {
  bind_address = "0.0.0.0"
  bind_port = "8081"
  trust_domain = "production.company.com"
  data_dir = "/opt/spire/data/server"
  
  ca_subject = {
    country = ["US"]
    organization = ["Company Inc"]
    common_name = "Production CA"
  }
  
  ca_ttl = "24h"
  default_svid_ttl = "1h"
}
```

### Certificate Issuance Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Workload
    participant A as SPIRE Agent
    participant S as SPIRE Server
    participant CA as Certificate Authority
    
    W->>A: Request SVID
    A->>A: Attest workload identity
    A->>S: Node attestation + workload info
    S->>S: Verify attestation
    S->>CA: Generate certificate
    CA->>S: Return signed cert
    S->>A: SVID (cert + key)
    A->>W: Deliver SVID
```

### Workload Attestation Methods


## 2. SPIFFE IDs

### SPIFFE ID Structure

### SPIFFE Workload API Client

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"
    "github.com/spiffe/go-spiffe/v2/workloadapi"
    "github.com/spiffe/go-spiffe/v2/spiffetls/tlsconfig"
    "crypto/tls"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    
    // Get X.509 source from Workload API
    source, err := workloadapi.NewX509Source(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Unable to create X509Source: %v", err)
    }
    defer source.Close()
    
    // Create TLS config for server
    serverTLSConfig := tlsconfig.MTLSServerConfig(source, source, tlsconfig.AuthorizeAny())
    
    // Create TLS config for client
    clientTLSConfig := tlsconfig.MTLSClientConfig(source, source, tlsconfig.AuthorizeAny())
    
    // Use in your application
    _ = serverTLSConfig
    _ = clientTLSConfig
}
```

### Automated Rotation with SPIRE

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# cert-rotation-monitor.sh

SPIRE_SOCKET="/run/spire/sockets/agent.sock"
ALERT_THRESHOLD=300  # 5 minutes
METRICS_PORT=9090

check_cert_expiry() {
    local spiffe_id=$1
    
    # Get certificate from Workload API
    cert_info=$(spire-agent api fetch x509 \
        -socketPath "$SPIRE_SOCKET" \
        -write /tmp/certs/)
    
    # Extract expiry time
    expiry=$(openssl x509 -in /tmp/certs/svid.0.pem -noout -enddate | cut -d= -f2)
    expiry_epoch=$(date -d "$expiry" +%s)
    current_epoch=$(date +%s)
    
    time_until_expiry=$((expiry_epoch - current_epoch))
    
    if [ $time_until_expiry -lt $ALERT_THRESHOLD ]; then
        echo "WARNING: Certificate expires in ${time_until_expiry}s"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo "Certificate valid for ${time_until_expiry}s"
    return 0
}

# Prometheus metrics export
cat <<EOF > /var/lib/node_exporter/textfile_collector/spire_certs.prom
# HELP spire_cert_expiry_seconds Seconds until SPIRE certificate expiry
# TYPE spire_cert_expiry_seconds gauge
spire_cert_expiry_seconds{spiffe_id="$SPIFFE_ID"} $time_until_expiry
EOF
```

### Certificate Rotation Strategies

```go
// Proactive certificate rotation
package rotation

import (
    "context"
    "crypto/tls"
    "time"
    "github.com/spiffe/go-spiffe/v2/workloadapi"
)

type CertRotator struct {
    source        *workloadapi.X509Source
    rotationPoint float64  // Rotate at 50% of cert lifetime
    checkInterval time.Duration
}

func NewCertRotator(source *workloadapi.X509Source) *CertRotator {
    return &CertRotator{
        source:        source,
        rotationPoint: 0.5,
        checkInterval: 10 * time.Second,
    }
}

func (r *CertRotator) Start(ctx context.Context) {
    ticker := time.NewTicker(r.checkInterval)
    defer ticker.Stop()
    
    for {
        select {
        case <-ctx.Done():
            return
        case <-ticker.C:
            r.checkAndRotate()
        }
    }
}

func (r *CertRotator) checkAndRotate() {
    svid, err := r.source.GetX509SVID()
    if err != nil {
        log.Printf("Failed to get SVID: %v", err)
        return
    }
    
    cert := svid.Certificates[0]
    now := time.Now()
    lifetime := cert.NotAfter.Sub(cert.NotBefore)
    elapsed := now.Sub(cert.NotBefore)
    
    if elapsed.Seconds() > lifetime.Seconds()*r.rotationPoint {
        log.Printf("Certificate reached rotation point, triggering rotation")
        // SPIRE automatically provides new certs via Workload API
        // Application just needs to reload the TLS config
        r.reloadTLSConfig()
    }
}

func (r *CertRotator) reloadTLSConfig() {
    // Implementation depends on your server framework
    // Most servers support config reload without downtime
}
```

### Graceful Rotation Implementation

```python
# Python example with automatic cert reload
import grpc
from spiffe import WorkloadApiClient
import threading
import time

class MTLSServer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.workload_api = WorkloadApiClient()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.credentials = None
        self.update_credentials()
        
    def update_credentials(self):
        """Update server credentials from SPIRE"""
        with self.lock:
            x509_context = self.workload_api.fetch_x509_context()
            
            self.credentials = grpc.ssl_server_credentials(
                private_key_certificate_chain_pairs=[(
                    x509_context.default_svid.private_key_bytes,
                    x509_context.default_svid.cert_chain_bytes
                )],
                root_certificates=x509_context.x509_bundle_set.get_bundle_bytes(),
                require_client_auth=True
            )
    
    def rotation_watcher(self):
        """Watch for certificate updates"""
        def callback(x509_context):
            print("Certificate updated, reloading credentials")
            self.update_credentials()
        
        self.workload_api.watch_x509_context(callback)
    
    def start(self, port):
        """Start gRPC server with auto-rotating certs"""
        server = grpc.server(
            futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10)
        )
        
        # Add services
        add_YourServiceServicer_to_server(YourService(), server)
        
        # Start rotation watcher
        threading.Thread(
            target=self.rotation_watcher,
            daemon=True
        ).start()
        
        server.add_secure_port(
            f'[::]:{port}',
            self.credentials
        )
        
        server.start()
        server.wait_for_termination()
```

## Best Practices Summary

### 1. **Certificate Lifetime**
- Short-lived certificates (1-24 hours)
- Automatic rotation at 50-66% of lifetime
- CA certificates longer-lived (months to years)

### 2. **Attestation**
- Multi-factor attestation when possible
- Platform-specific attestors (K8s, AWS, GCP)
- Regular re-attestation

### 3. **Policy Enforcement**
- Default-deny policies
- Fine-grained authorization based on SPIFFE IDs
- Regular policy audits

### 4. **Monitoring**
- Track certificate expiry times
- Alert on rotation failures
- Monitor mTLS connection success rates
- Log all authorization decisions

This architecture ensures zero-trust security with automatic certificate management, minimal operational overhead, and strong authentication/authorization between all services.

### 2. Bottleneck Heatmap Engine

```python
# services/bottleneck_detector.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Dict
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

@dataclass
class Bottleneck:
    id: str
    category: str
    severity: float
    affected_teams: List[str]
    time_periods: List[str]
    symptoms: List[str]
    estimated_cost_hours: float
    recommendation: str

class BottleneckHeatmapEngine:
    """
    Detects and visualizes developer bottlenecks across dimensions:
    - Time (hourly, daily, weekly patterns)
    - Team/Organization
    - Workflow stage (build, test, deploy, review)
    - Tool/Service
    """
    
    def __init__(self, clickhouse_client, ml_model_registry):
        self.db = clickhouse_client
        self.models = ml_model_registry
        
    def detect_bottlenecks(self, lookback_days=7) -> List[Bottleneck]:
        """Multi-modal bottleneck detection"""
        
        # 1. Statistical anomalies (z-score > 3)
        anomalies = self._detect_duration_anomalies(lookback_days)
        
        # 2. Pattern-based (recurring delays)
        patterns = self._detect_recurring_patterns(lookback_days)
        
        # 3. Comparative (team vs org average)
        comparative = self._detect_comparative_slowdowns(lookback_days)
        
        # 4. Dependency-based (blocking chains)
        dependency_blocks = self._analyze_dependency_chains(lookback_days)
        
        # Merge and prioritize
        bottlenecks = self._merge_signals(
            anomalies, patterns, comparative, dependency_blocks
        )
        
        return self._prioritize_by_impact(bottlenecks)
    
    def _detect_duration_anomalies(self, days: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        query = f"""
        WITH baseline AS (
            SELECT 
                action_type,
                tool,
                AVG(duration_ms) as mean_duration,
                STDDEV(duration_ms) as std_duration
            FROM developer_activities
            WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL {days} DAY
                AND success = true
            GROUP BY action_type, tool
        ),
        recent AS (
            SELECT 
                action_type,
                tool,
                developer_id,
                team_id,
                AVG(duration_ms) as avg_duration,
                COUNT(*) as occurrences
            FROM developer_activities
            WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY
            GROUP BY action_type, tool, developer_id, team_id
        )
        SELECT 
            r.*,
            b.mean_duration,
            b.std_duration,
            (r.avg_duration - b.mean_duration) / b.std_duration as z_score
        FROM recent r
        JOIN baseline b USING (action_type, tool)
        WHERE z_score > 3.0
        ORDER BY z_score DESC
        """
        return self.db.query_dataframe(query)
    
    def _detect_recurring_patterns(self, days: int) -> List[Dict]:
        """Identify patterns like 'every Monday morning builds are slow'"""
        query = f"""
        SELECT 
            action_type,
            tool,
            toDayOfWeek(timestamp) as day_of_week,
            toHour(timestamp) as hour_of_day,
            AVG(duration_ms) as avg_duration,
            COUNT(*) as frequency
        FROM developer_activities
        WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL {days} DAY
        GROUP BY action_type, tool, day_of_week, hour_of_day
        HAVING frequency > 10
        """
        df = self.db.query_dataframe(query)
        
        # Cluster time periods with similar slow patterns
        if len(df) > 0:
            features = df[['day_of_week', 'hour_of_day', 'avg_duration']]
            clustering = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=3).fit(features)
            df['pattern_cluster'] = clustering.labels_
            return df[df['pattern_cluster'] != -1].to_dict('records')
        return []
    
    def generate_heatmap_data(self, dimension_x: str, dimension_y: str, 
                              metric: str = 'p95_duration') -> Dict:
        """
        Generate heatmap data for visualization
        
        Examples:
        - dimension_x='hour_of_day', dimension_y='team', metric='p95_duration'
        - dimension_x='workflow_stage', dimension_y='tool', metric='failure_rate'
        """
        query = f"""
        SELECT 
            {dimension_x} as x,
            {dimension_y} as y,
            quantile(0.95)(duration_ms) as p95_duration,
            AVG(CASE WHEN success THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) as failure_rate,
            COUNT(*) as volume
        FROM developer_activities
        WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
        GROUP BY x, y
        """
        df = self.db.query_dataframe(query)
        
        # Pivot for heatmap format
        heatmap = df.pivot(index='y', columns='x', values=metric)
        
        return {
            'data': heatmap.to_dict(),
            'x_labels': heatmap.columns.tolist(),
            'y_labels': heatmap.index.tolist(),
            'metric': metric,
            'timestamp': pd.Timestamp.now().isoformat()
        }
```

```python
# services/automation_backlog.py
from enum import Enum
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Optional
import asyncio

class AutomationOpportunityType(Enum):
    TOIL_ELIMINATION = "toil_elimination"
    WORKFLOW_OPTIMIZATION = "workflow_optimization"
    TOOL_INTEGRATION = "tool_integration"
    SELF_SERVICE = "self_service"
    ALERT_TUNING = "alert_tuning"

@dataclass
class AutomationOpportunity:
    id: str
    title: str
    description: str
    opportunity_type: AutomationOpportunityType
    
    # Impact metrics
    affected_developers: int
    time_saved_per_occurrence_mins: float
    occurrences_per_week: int
    estimated_annual_savings_hours: float
    
    # Feasibility
    effort_estimate_days: float
    technical_complexity: float  # 0-1 scale
    data_quality_score: float  # 0-1 confidence
    
    # Priority score (calculated)
    priority_score: float = field(init=False)
    
    # Evidence
    example_traces: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    affected_teams: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    
    # Workflow
    status: str = "identified"  # identified, validated, in_progress, completed
    assigned_to: Optional[str] = None
    
    def __post_init__(self):
        self.priority_score = self._calculate_priority()
    
    def _calculate_priority(self) -> float:
        """RICE scoring: Reach × Impact × Confidence / Effort"""
        reach = self.affected_developers
        impact = self.estimated_annual_savings_hours
        confidence = self.data_quality_score
        effort = max(self.effort_estimate_days, 0.5)  # Avoid division by zero
        
        return (reach * impact * confidence) / effort

class AutomationBacklogManager:
    def __init__(self, bottleneck_engine, telemetry_db):
        self.bottleneck_engine = bottleneck_engine
        self.db = telemetry_db
        
    async def identify_opportunities(self) -> List[AutomationOpportunity]:
        """Scan telemetry for automation opportunities"""
        opportunities = []
        
        # 1. Repetitive manual tasks (detected via similar sequences)
        toil = await self._identify_toil()
        opportunities.extend(toil)
        
        # 2. High-frequency tool switches (integration opportunity)
        integrations = await self._identify_integration_gaps()
        opportunities.extend(integrations)
        
        # 3. Wait times (workflow optimization)
        workflows = await self._identify_workflow_optimizations()
        opportunities.extend(workflows)
        
        # 4. Frequent escalations (self-service opportunity)
        self_service = await self._identify_self_service_gaps()
        opportunities.extend(self_service)
        
        # Sort by priority
        opportunities.sort(key=lambda x: x.priority_score, reverse=True)
        
        return opportunities
    
    async def _identify_toil(self) -> List[AutomationOpportunity]:
        """Detect repetitive manual sequences"""
        query = """
        WITH action_sequences AS (
            SELECT 
                developer_id,
                groupArray(action_type) OVER (
                    PARTITION BY developer_id 
                    ORDER BY timestamp 
                    ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 5 FOLLOWING
                ) as sequence,
                timestamp
            FROM developer_activities
            WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
        ),
        sequence_frequency AS (
            SELECT 
                sequence,
                COUNT(DISTINCT developer_id) as dev_count,
                COUNT(*) as occurrence_count,
                AVG(time_to_next_action_minutes) as avg_time
            FROM action_sequences
            WHERE length(sequence) >= 3
            GROUP BY sequence
            HAVING occurrence_count > 50  -- Happened 50+ times
                AND dev_count >= 5        -- Affects 5+ developers
        )
        SELECT * FROM sequence_frequency
        ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC
        LIMIT 20
        """
        
        results = await self.db.query(query)
        opportunities = []
        
        for row in results:
            opp = AutomationOpportunity(
                id=f"toil_{hash(str(row['sequence']))}",
                title=f"Automate repeated sequence: {' → '.join(row['sequence'][:3])}...",
                description=f"This {len(row['sequence'])}-step sequence is repeated "
                           f"{row['occurrence_count']} times across {row['dev_count']} developers",
                opportunity_type=AutomationOpportunityType.TOIL_ELIMINATION,

    async def _identify_integration_gaps(self) -> List[AutomationOpportunity]:
        """Detect frequent context switches between tools"""
        query = """
        SELECT 
            tool_a,
            tool_b,

            COUNT(DISTINCT developer_id) as dev_count,
            AVG(time_between_seconds) as avg_gap_seconds
        FROM (
            SELECT 
                developer_id,
                tool as tool_a,
                neighbor(tool, 1) as tool_b,
                neighbor(timestamp, 1) - timestamp as time_between_seconds
            FROM developer_activities
            WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
        )
        WHERE tool_a != tool_b
            AND time_between_seconds < 300  -- Within 5 minutes
        GROUP BY tool_a, tool_b
        HAVING switch_count > 100
        ORDER BY switch_count DESC
        LIMIT 10
        """
        
        results = await self.db.query(query)
        opportunities = []
```

## 1. Drift Detection Implementation

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.metrics import jensen_shannon_distance
from typing import Dict, Tuple, Optional
import logging

class DriftDetector:
    """Comprehensive drift detection system"""
    
    def __init__(self, 
                 reference_data: pd.DataFrame,
                 feature_columns: list,
                 target_column: Optional[str] = None):
        self.reference_data = reference_data
        self.feature_columns = feature_columns
        self.target_column = target_column
        self.baseline_stats = self._compute_baseline_stats()
        
    def _compute_baseline_stats(self) -> Dict:
        """Compute baseline statistics from reference data"""
        stats_dict = {}
        
        for col in self.feature_columns:
            if self.reference_data[col].dtype in ['int64', 'float64']:
                stats_dict[col] = {
                    'mean': self.reference_data[col].mean(),
                    'std': self.reference_data[col].std(),
                    'q25': self.reference_data[col].quantile(0.25),
                    'q50': self.reference_data[col].quantile(0.50),
                    'q75': self.reference_data[col].quantile(0.75),
                    'min': self.reference_data[col].min(),
                    'max': self.reference_data[col].max(),
                    'distribution': self.reference_data[col].values
                }
            else:
                # Categorical
                stats_dict[col] = {
                    'value_counts': self.reference_data[col].value_counts(normalize=True).to_dict(),
                    'unique_values': set(self.reference_data[col].unique())
                }
        
        return stats_dict
    
    def detect_data_drift(self, 
                         current_data: pd.DataFrame,
                         method: str = 'ks') -> Dict:
        """
        Detect data drift using statistical tests
        
        Methods:
        - ks: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
        - js: Jensen-Shannon divergence
        - psi: Population Stability Index
        - chi2: Chi-square test (categorical)
        """
        drift_results = {}
        
        for col in self.feature_columns:
            if col not in current_data.columns:
                continue
                
            if self.reference_data[col].dtype in ['int64', 'float64']:
                if method == 'ks':
                    result = self._ks_test(col, current_data[col])
                elif method == 'js':
                    result = self._js_divergence(col, current_data[col])
                elif method == 'psi':
                    result = self._psi(col, current_data[col])
                else:
                    raise ValueError(f"Unknown method: {method}")
            else:
                result = self._chi_square_test(col, current_data[col])
            
            drift_results[col] = result
        
        return drift_results
    
    def _ks_test(self, feature: str, current_values: pd.Series) -> Dict:
        """Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for numerical features"""
        reference_values = self.baseline_stats[feature]['distribution']
        statistic, p_value = stats.ks_2samp(reference_values, current_values)
        
        return {
            'method': 'ks_test',
            'statistic': statistic,
            'p_value': p_value,
            'drift_detected': p_value < 0.05,
            'severity': self._categorize_severity(p_value)
        }
    
    def _js_divergence(self, feature: str, current_values: pd.Series) -> Dict:
        """Jensen-Shannon divergence for numerical features"""
        reference_values = self.baseline_stats[feature]['distribution']
        
        # Create histograms
        bins = np.histogram_bin_edges(
            np.concatenate([reference_values, current_values]), 
            bins=50
        )
        ref_hist, _ = np.histogram(reference_values, bins=bins, density=True)
        cur_hist, _ = np.histogram(current_values, bins=bins, density=True)
        
        # Normalize
        ref_hist = ref_hist / ref_hist.sum()
        cur_hist = cur_hist / cur_hist.sum()
        
        # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        ref_hist = ref_hist + 1e-10
        cur_hist = cur_hist + 1e-10
        
        # Calculate JS divergence
        m = 0.5 * (ref_hist + cur_hist)
        js_div = 0.5 * stats.entropy(ref_hist, m) + 0.5 * stats.entropy(cur_hist, m)
        
        return {
            'method': 'js_divergence',
            'statistic': js_div,
            'drift_detected': js_div > 0.1,
            'severity': self._categorize_js_severity(js_div)
        }
    
    def _psi(self, feature: str, current_values: pd.Series, 
             buckets: int = 10) -> Dict:
        """Population Stability Index"""
        reference_values = self.baseline_stats[feature]['distribution']
        
        # Create buckets based on reference data
        breakpoints = np.percentile(reference_values, 
                                   np.linspace(0, 100, buckets + 1))
        breakpoints = np.unique(breakpoints)
        
        # Calculate distributions
        ref_percents = np.histogram(reference_values, bins=breakpoints)[0] / len(reference_values)
        cur_percents = np.histogram(current_values, bins=breakpoints)[0] / len(current_values)
        
        # Add small epsilon
        ref_percents = ref_percents + 1e-10
        cur_percents = cur_percents + 1e-10
        
        # Calculate PSI
        psi_value = np.sum((cur_percents - ref_percents) * np.log(cur_percents / ref_percents))
        
        return {
            'method': 'psi',
            'statistic': psi_value,
            'drift_detected': psi_value > 0.1,
            'severity': self._categorize_psi_severity(psi_value)
        }
    
    def _chi_square_test(self, feature: str, current_values: pd.Series) -> Dict:
        """Chi-square test for categorical features"""
        ref_counts = self.baseline_stats[feature]['value_counts']
        
        # Get current distribution
        cur_counts = current_values.value_counts(normalize=True).to_dict()
        
        # Align categories
        all_categories = set(ref_counts.keys()) | set(cur_counts.keys())
        
        ref_freq = np.array([ref_counts.get(cat, 0) for cat in all_categories])
        cur_freq = np.array([cur_counts.get(cat, 0) for cat in all_categories])
        
        # Convert to counts
        cur_freq_counts = cur_freq * len(current_values)
        expected_counts = ref_freq * len(current_values)
        
        # Chi-square test
        statistic, p_value = stats.chisquare(cur_freq_counts, expected_counts)
        
        return {
            'method': 'chi_square',
            'statistic': statistic,
            'p_value': p_value,
            'drift_detected': p_value < 0.05,
            'severity': self._categorize_severity(p_value),
            'new_categories': set(cur_counts.keys()) - self.baseline_stats[feature]['unique_values']
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def _categorize_severity(p_value: float) -> str:
        """Categorize drift severity based on p-value"""
        if p_value >= 0.05:
            return 'none'
        elif p_value >= 0.01:
            return 'low'
        elif p_value >= 0.001:
            return 'medium'
        else:
            return 'high'
    
    @staticmethod
    def _categorize_js_severity(js_div: float) -> str:
        """Categorize drift severity based on JS divergence"""
        if js_div < 0.1:
            return 'none'
        elif js_div < 0.2:
            return 'low'
        elif js_div < 0.3:
            return 'medium'
        else:
            return 'high'
    
    @staticmethod
    def _categorize_psi_severity(psi: float) -> str:
        """Categorize drift severity based on PSI"""
        if psi < 0.1:
            return 'none'
        elif psi < 0.2:
            return 'low'
        else:
            return 'high'
```

```python
class CohortMonitor:
    """Monitor model performance across different cohorts"""
    
    def __init__(self, cohort_definitions: Dict[str, callable]):
        """
        cohort_definitions: Dict mapping cohort names to filter functions
        Example: {'high_value': lambda df: df['value'] > 1000}
        """
        self.cohort_definitions = cohort_definitions
        self.cohort_baselines = {}
        
    def compute_cohort_baselines(self, 
                                 data: pd.DataFrame,
                                 predictions: np.ndarray,
                                 actuals: np.ndarray,
                                 metrics_func: callable) -> Dict:
        """Compute baseline metrics for each cohort"""
        for cohort_name, filter_func in self.cohort_definitions.items():
            cohort_mask = filter_func(data)
            cohort_predictions = predictions[cohort_mask]
            cohort_actuals = actuals[cohort_mask]
            
            if len(cohort_predictions) > 0:
                self.cohort_baselines[cohort_name] = {
                    'metrics': metrics_func(cohort_actuals, cohort_predictions),
                    'size': len(cohort_predictions),
                    'proportion': cohort_mask.sum() / len(data)
                }
        
        return self.cohort_baselines
    
    def monitor_cohorts(self,
                       data: pd.DataFrame,
                       predictions: np.ndarray,
                       actuals: np.ndarray,
                       metrics_func: callable,
                       threshold: float = 0.1) -> Dict:
        """Monitor current cohort performance vs baseline"""
        alerts = {}
        
        for cohort_name, filter_func in self.cohort_definitions.items():
            cohort_mask = filter_func(data)
            
            if cohort_mask.sum() == 0:
                alerts[cohort_name] = {
                    'status': 'warning',
                    'message': 'Cohort has no samples'
                }
                continue
            
            current_metrics = metrics_func(
                actuals[cohort_mask],
                predictions[cohort_mask]
            )
            baseline_metrics = self.cohort_baselines[cohort_name]['metrics']
            
            # Check for degradation
            degradations = {}
            for metric_name, current_value in current_metrics.items():
                baseline_value = baseline_metrics[metric_name]
                relative_change = abs(current_value - baseline_value) / abs(baseline_value)
                
                if relative_change > threshold:
                    degradations[metric_name] = {
                        'baseline': baseline_value,
                        'current': current_value,
                        'change': relative_change
                    }
            
            if degradations:
                alerts[cohort_name] = {
                    'status': 'alert',
                    'degradations': degradations,
                    'cohort_size': cohort_mask.sum()
                }
            else:
                alerts[cohort_name] = {
                    'status': 'ok',
                    'cohort_size': cohort_mask.sum()
                }
        
        return alerts
```

## 3. Alert System

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
import json
from typing import List, Optional

class AlertSeverity(Enum):
    INFO = 1
    WARNING = 2
    CRITICAL = 3

@dataclass
class Alert:
    timestamp: datetime
    alert_type: str
    severity: AlertSeverity
    metric_name: str
    current_value: float
    baseline_value: float
    threshold: float
    message: str
    metadata: dict

class AlertManager:
    """Manage and route alerts"""
    
    def __init__(self, alert_config: Dict):
        self.config = alert_config
        self.alert_history: List[Alert] = []
        
    def check_thresholds(self,
                        metric_name: str,
                        current_value: float,
                        baseline_value: float) -> Optional[Alert]:
        """Check if metric exceeds thresholds"""
        
        if metric_name not in self.config:
            return None
        
        config = self.config[metric_name]
        relative_change = abs(current_value - baseline_value) / abs(baseline_value)
        
        alert = None
        
        if relative_change > config['critical_threshold']:
            alert = Alert(
                timestamp=datetime.now(),
                alert_type='threshold_exceeded',
                severity=AlertSeverity.CRITICAL,
                metric_name=metric_name,
                current_value=current_value,
                baseline_value=baseline_value,
                threshold=config['critical_threshold'],
                message=f"CRITICAL: {metric_name} degraded by {relative_change:.2%}",
                metadata={'relative_change': relative_change}
            )
        elif relative_change > config['warning_threshold']:
            alert = Alert(
                timestamp=datetime.now(),
                alert_type='threshold_exceeded',
                severity=AlertSeverity.WARNING,
                metric_name=metric_name,
                current_value=current_value,
                baseline_value=baseline_value,
                threshold=config['warning_threshold'],
                message=f"WARNING: {metric_name} degraded by {relative_change:.2%}",
                metadata={'relative_change': relative_change}
            )
        
        if alert:
            self.alert_history.append(alert)
            self._route_alert(alert)
        
        return alert
    
    def _route_alert(self, alert: Alert):
        """Route alert to appropriate channels"""
        if alert.severity == AlertSeverity.CRITICAL:
            self._send_pagerduty(alert)
            self._send_slack(alert)
            self._send_email(alert)
        elif alert.severity == AlertSeverity.WARNING:
            self._send_slack(alert)
        
        # Always log
        logging.warning(f"Alert: {alert.message}")
    
    def _send_slack(self, alert: Alert):
        """Send alert to Slack"""
        # Pseudo-code for Slack integration
        slack_message = {
            'text': f"🚨 {alert.message}",
            'attachments': [{
                'fields': [
                    {'title': 'Metric', 'value': alert.metric_name},
                    {'title': 'Current', 'value': f"{alert.current_value:.4f}"},
                    {'title': 'Baseline', 'value': f"{alert.baseline_value:.4f}"},
                    {'title': 'Timestamp', 'value': alert.timestamp.isoformat()}
                ]
            }]
        }
        print(f"[SLACK] {json.dumps(slack_message, indent=2)}")
    
    def _send_pagerduty(self, alert: Alert):
        """Send alert to PagerDuty"""
        print(f"[PAGERDUTY] Critical alert: {alert.message}")
    
    def _send_email(self, alert: Alert):
        """Send alert via email"""
        print(f"[EMAIL] {alert.message}")
    
    def get_recent_alerts(self, hours: int = 24) -> List[Alert]:
        """Get alerts from last N hours"""
        cutoff = datetime.now().timestamp() - (hours * 3600)
        return [a for a in self.alert_history 
                if a.timestamp.timestamp() > cutoff]


# Configure alerts
alert_config = {
    'accuracy': {
        'warning_threshold': 0.05,  # 5% degradation
        'critical_threshold': 0.10   # 10% degradation
    },
    'auc': {
        'warning_threshold': 0.03,
        'critical_threshold': 0.07
    },
    'latency_p95': {
        'warning_threshold': 0.20,
        'critical_threshold': 0.50
    }
}

alert_manager = AlertManager(alert_config)

# Check metrics
alert = alert_manager.check_thresholds(
    metric_name='accuracy',
    current_value=0.82,
    baseline_value=0.92
)
```

## 4. Retraining Triggers

```python
class RetrainingTrigger:
    """Determine when to retrain the model"""
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict):
        self.config = config
        self.trigger_history = []
        
    def should_retrain(self,
                      drift_results: Dict,
                      performance_metrics: Dict,
                      days_since_training: int,
                      data_volume: int) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """
        Determine if model should be retrained based on multiple criteria
        
        Returns: (should_retrain, reason)
        """
        reasons = []
        
        # 1. Data drift threshold
        drift_features = sum(1 for r in drift_results.values() 
                           if r.get('drift_detected', False))
        drift_ratio = drift_features / len(drift_results)
        
        if drift_ratio > self.config['max_drift_ratio']:
            reasons.append(f"data_drift:{drift_ratio:.2%}")
        
        # 2. Performance degradation
        for metric, value in performance_metrics.items():
            if metric in self.config['performance_thresholds']:
                threshold = self.config['performance_thresholds'][metric]
                if value < threshold['min_value']:
                    reasons.append(f"{metric}_degradation:{value:.3f}<{threshold['min_value']}")
        
        # 3. Time-based trigger
        if days_since_training >= self.config['max_days_without_training']:
            reasons.append(f"time_threshold:{days_since_training}days")
        
        # 4. Volume-based trigger
        if data_volume >= self.config['min_samples_for_retrain']:
            reasons.append(f"sufficient_data:{data_volume}samples")
        
        # Determine if should retrain
        should_retrain = len(reasons) >= self.config.get('min_triggers', 1)
        
        trigger_info = {
            'timestamp': datetime.now(),
            'should_retrain': should_retrain,
            'reasons': reasons,
            'drift_ratio': drift_ratio,
            'days_since_training': days_since_training,
            'data_volume': data_volume
        }
        
        self.trigger_history.append(trigger_info)
        
        return should_retrain, ';'.join(reasons) if reasons else 'no_trigger'
    
    def get_retraining_priority(self, trigger_info: Dict) -> str:
        """Determine urgency of retraining"""
        reasons count = len(trigger_info['reasons'])
        
        if trigger_info['drift_ratio'] > 0.5:
            return 'critical'
        elif reasons_count >= 3:
            return 'high'
        elif reasons_count >= 2:
            return 'medium'
        else:
            return 'low'


# Configure retraining triggers
retrain_config = {
    'max_drift_ratio': 0.3,  # 30% of features drifting
    'performance_thresholds': {
        'accuracy': {'min_value': 0.85},
        'auc': {'min_value': 0.80}
    },
    'max_days_without_training': 30,
    'min_samples_for_retrain': 10000,
    'min_triggers': 2  # Need at least 2 reasons to trigger
}

retraining_trigger = RetrainingTrigger(retrain_config)

# Check if retraining needed
should_retrain, reason = retraining_trigger.should_retrain(
    drift_results={'f1': {'drift_detected': True}, 
                  'f2': {'drift_detected': False}},
    performance_metrics={'accuracy': 0.82, 'auc': 0.79},
    days_since_training=35,
    data_volume=15000
)

print(f"Should retrain: {should_retrain}")
print(f"Reasons: {reason}")
```

## 5. Complete Monitoring Pipeline

```python
class MLMonitoringPipeline:
    """Complete ML monitoring pipeline"""
    
    def __init__(self,
                 drift_detector: DriftDetector,
                 cohort_monitor: CohortMonitor,
                 alert_manager: AlertManager,
                 retraining_trigger: RetrainingTrigger):
        self.drift_detector = drift_detector
        self.cohort_monitor = cohort_monitor
        self.alert_manager = alert_manager
        self.retraining_trigger = retraining_trigger
        self.training_date = datetime.now()
        self.sample_buffer = []
        
    def monitor_batch(self,
                     data: pd.DataFrame,
                     predictions: np.ndarray,
                     actuals: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> Dict:
        """Monitor a batch of predictions"""
        
        report = {
            'timestamp': datetime.now(),
            'batch_size': len(data),
            'drift_detected': False,
            'performance_alerts': [],
            'should_retrain': False
        }
        
        # 1. Data Drift Detection
        drift_results = self.drift_detector.detect_data_drift(data, method='psi')
        report['drift_results'] = drift_results
        report['drift_detected'] = any(r['drift_detected'] for r in drift_results.values())
        
        # 2. Cohort Monitoring (if actuals available)
        if actuals is not None:
            from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, roc_auc_score
            
            def classification_metrics(y_true, y_pred):
                return {
                    'accuracy': accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred > 0.5),
                    'auc': roc_auc_score(y_true, y_pred)
                }
            
            cohort_alerts = self.cohort_monitor.monitor_cohorts(
                data, predictions, actuals, classification_metrics
            )
            report['cohort_alerts'] = cohort_alerts
            
            # Overall performance metrics
            overall_metrics = classification_metrics(actuals, predictions)
            report['performance_metrics'] = overall_metrics
            
            # Check alert thresholds
            for metric_name, value in overall_metrics.items():
                baseline = 0.90  # Would come from baseline metrics
                self.alert_manager.check_thresholds(metric_name, value, baseline)
        
        # 3. Store samples for retraining
        self.sample_buffer.extend(data.to_dict('records'))
        
        # 4. Check retraining triggers
        days_since_training = (datetime.now() - self.training_date).days
        should_retrain, reason = self.retraining_trigger.should_retrain(
            drift_results=drift_results,
            performance_metrics=report.get('performance_metrics', {}),
            days_since_training=days_since_training,
            data_volume=len(self.sample_buffer)
        )
        
        report['should_retrain'] = should_retrain
        report['retrain_reason'] = reason
        
        if should_retrain:
            logging.critical(f"RETRAINING TRIGGERED: {reason}")
        
        return report
    
    def generate_monitoring_dashboard(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Generate summary dashboard"""
        recent_alerts = self.alert_manager.get_recent_alerts(hours=24)
        
        dashboard = pd.DataFrame({
            'metric': ['Total Alerts', 'Critical Alerts', 'Warnings'],
            'value': [
                len(recent_alerts),
                sum(1 for a in recent_alerts if a.severity == AlertSeverity.CRITICAL),
                sum(1 for a in recent_alerts if a.severity == AlertSeverity.WARNING)
            ]
        })
        
        return dashboard


# Example: Complete pipeline
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Initialize components
    reference_data = pd.DataFrame({
        'feature1': np.random.normal(0, 1, 1000),
        'feature2': np.random.normal(5, 2, 1000),
        'region': np.random.choice(['north', 'south'], 1000)
    })
    
    drift_detector = DriftDetector(
        reference_data=reference_data,
        feature_columns=['feature1', 'feature2', 'region']
    )
    
    cohort_monitor = CohortMonitor({
        'north': lambda df: df['region'] == 'north',
        'south': lambda df: df['region'] == 'south'
    })
    
    alert_manager = AlertManager(alert_config)
    retraining_trigger = RetrainingTrigger(retrain_config)
    
    pipeline = MLMonitoringPipeline(
        drift_detector, cohort_monitor, alert_manager, retraining_trigger
    )
    
    # Monitor production batch
    prod_data = pd.DataFrame({
        'feature1': np.random.normal(0.5, 1.5, 500),
        'feature2': np.random.normal(5.5, 2.5, 500),
        'region': np.random.choice(['north', 'south'], 500)
    })
    
    predictions = np.random.random(500)
    actuals = (np.random.random(500) > 0.3).astype(int)
    
    report = pipeline.monitor_batch(prod_data, predictions, actuals)
    
    print("\n=== Monitoring Report ===")
    print(f"Drift Detected: {report['drift_detected']}")
    print(f"Should Retrain: {report['should_retrain']}")
    if report['should_retrain']:
        print(f"Reason: {report['retrain_reason']}")
```

This comprehensive system provides production-ready monitoring with drift detection, cohort analysis, alerting, and automated retraining triggers.

```javascript
const pool = require('./pool');
const logger = require('../utils/logger');

const migrations = [
  `
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    username VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    role VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'user',
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  );
  
  CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);
  CREATE INDEX idx_users_username ON users(username);
  `,
  
  `
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS posts (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    slug VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    excerpt TEXT,
    author_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'draft',
    published_at TIMESTAMP,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  );
  
  CREATE INDEX idx_posts_author ON posts(author_id);
  CREATE INDEX idx_posts_slug ON posts(slug);
  CREATE INDEX idx_posts_status ON posts(status);
  `,
  
  `
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS comments (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    post_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  );
  
  CREATE INDEX idx_comments_post ON comments(post_id);
  CREATE INDEX idx_comments_user ON comments(user_id);
  `,
  
  `
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refresh_tokens (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    token VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
    expires_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  );
  
  CREATE INDEX idx_refresh_tokens_user ON refresh_tokens(user_id);
  CREATE INDEX idx_refresh_tokens_token ON refresh_tokens(token);
  `,
];

async function migrate() {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  
  try {
    await client.query('BEGIN');
    
    for (const migration of migrations) {
      await client.query(migration);
      logger.info('Migration executed successfully');
    }
    
    await client.query('COMMIT');
    logger.info('All migrations completed');
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query('ROLLBACK');
    logger.error('Migration failed:', error);
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

if (require.main === module) {
  migrate()
    .then(() => {
      logger.info('Database migration completed');
      process.exit(0);
    })
    .catch((error) => {
      logger.error('Migration error:', error);
      process.exit(1);
    });
}

module.exports = migrate;
```

```javascript
const pool = require('../database/pool');
const bcrypt = require('bcrypt');
const { v4: uuidv4 } = require('uuid');

class User {
  static async create({ email, password, username, role = 'user' }) {
    const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, 10);
    const query = `
      INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash, username, role)
      VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
      RETURNING id, email, username, role, created_at
    `;
    
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [email, passwordHash, username, role]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async findById(id) {
    const query = 'SELECT id, email, username, role, is_active, created_at FROM users WHERE id = $1';
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [id]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async findByEmail(email) {
    const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = $1';
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [email]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async findByUsername(username) {
    const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = $1';
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [username]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async verifyPassword(plainPassword, hashedPassword) {
    return bcrypt.compare(plainPassword, hashedPassword);
  }

  static async update(id, updates) {
    const allowedUpdates = ['email', 'username'];
    const fields = [];
    const values = [];
    let paramCount = 1;

    Object.keys(updates).forEach((key) => {
      if (allowedUpdates.includes(key)) {
        fields.push(`${key} = $${paramCount}`);
        values.push(updates[key]);
        paramCount++;
      }
    });

    if (fields.length === 0) {
      return null;
    }

    fields.push(`updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`);
    values.push(id);

    const query = `
      UPDATE users 
      SET ${fields.join(', ')}
      WHERE id = $${paramCount}
      RETURNING id, email, username, role, updated_at
    `;

    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, values);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async delete(id) {
    const query = 'DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1 RETURNING id';
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [id]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async list({ limit = 10, offset = 0, orderBy = 'created_at', order = 'DESC' }) {
    const query = `
      SELECT id, email, username, role, is_active, created_at
      FROM users
      ORDER BY ${orderBy} ${order}
      LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2
    `;
    
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [limit, offset]);
    
    const countQuery = 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users';
    const { rows: countRows } = await pool.query(countQuery);
    
    return {
      data: rows,
      total: parseInt(countRows[0].count, 10),
      limit,
      offset,
    };
  }
}

module.exports = User;
```

### src/models/Post.js

```javascript
const pool = require('../database/pool');
const { v4: uuidv4 } = require('uuid');

class Post {
  static async create({ title, slug, content, excerpt, authorId, status = 'draft' }) {
    const query = `
      INSERT INTO posts (title, slug, content, excerpt, author_id, status)
      VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
      RETURNING *
    `;
    
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [title, slug, content, excerpt, authorId, status]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async findById(id) {
    const query = `
      SELECT p.*, u.username as author_name, u.email as author_email
      FROM posts p
      JOIN users u ON p.author_id = u.id
      WHERE p.id = $1
    `;
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [id]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async findBySlug(slug) {
    const query = `
      SELECT p.*, u.username as author_name, u.email as author_email
      FROM posts p
      JOIN users u ON p.author_id = u.id
      WHERE p.slug = $1
    `;
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [slug]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async update(id, updates, userId) {
    const allowedUpdates = ['title', 'slug', 'content', 'excerpt', 'status'];
    const fields = [];
    const values = [];
    let paramCount = 1;

    Object.keys(updates).forEach((key) => {
      if (allowedUpdates.includes(key) && updates[key] !== undefined) {
        fields.push(`${key} = $${paramCount}`);
        values.push(updates[key]);
        paramCount++;
      }
    });

    if (fields.length === 0) {
      return null;
    }

    fields.push(`updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`);
    
    if (updates.status === 'published' && !updates.published_at) {
      fields.push(`published_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`);
    }

    values.push(id, userId);

    const query = `
      UPDATE posts 
      SET ${fields.join(', ')}
      WHERE id = $${paramCount} AND author_id = $${paramCount + 1}
      RETURNING *
    `;

    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, values);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async delete(id, userId) {
    const query = 'DELETE FROM posts WHERE id = $1 AND author_id = $2 RETURNING id';
    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, [id, userId]);
    return rows[0];
  }

  static async list({ 
    limit = 10, 
    offset = 0, 
    status = null, 
    authorId = null,
    orderBy = 'created_at',
    order = 'DESC',
    cursor = null 
  }) {
    let query = `
      SELECT p.*, u.username as author_name, u.email as author_email
      FROM posts p
      JOIN users u ON p.author_id = u.id
      WHERE 1=1
    `;
    
    const values = [];
    let paramCount = 1;

    if (status) {
      query += ` AND p.status = $${paramCount}`;
      values.push(status);
      paramCount++;
    }

    if (authorId) {
      query += ` AND p.author_id = $${paramCount}`;
      values.push(authorId);
      paramCount++;
    }

    if (cursor) {
      query += ` AND p.created_at < $${paramCount}`;
      values.push(cursor);
      paramCount++;
    }

    query += ` ORDER BY p.${orderBy} ${order} LIMIT $${paramCount} OFFSET $${paramCount + 1}`;
    values.push(limit, offset);

    const { rows } = await pool.query(query, values);
    
    let countQuery = 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE 1=1';
    const countValues = [];
    let countParamCount = 1;
    
    if (status) {
      countQuery += ` AND status = $${countParamCount}`;
      countValues.push(status);
      countParamCount++;
    }
    
    if (authorId) {
      countQuery += ` AND author_id = $${countParamCount}`;
      countValues.push(authorId);
    }
    
    const { rows: countRows } = await pool.query(countQuery, countValues);
    
    return {
      data: rows,
      total: parseInt(countRows[0].count, 10),
      limit,
      offset,
      nextCursor: rows.length > 0 ? rows[rows.length - 1].created_at : null,
    };
  }
}

module.exports = Post;
```

### src/middleware/auth.js

```javascript
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
const config = require('../config');
const logger = require('../utils/logger');
const User = require('../models/User');

async function authenticate(req, res, next) {
  try {
    const authHeader = req.headers.authorization;
    
    if (!authHeader || !authHeader.startsWith('Bearer ')) {
      return res.status(401).json({
        error: {
          code: 'UNAUTHORIZED',
          message: 'No token provided',
        },
      });
    }

    const token = authHeader.substring(7);
    
    try {
      const decoded = jwt.verify(token, config.jwt.secret);
      
      const user = await User.findById(decoded.userId);
      
      if (!user || !user.is_active) {
        return res.status(401).json({
          error: {
            code: 'UNAUTHORIZED',
            message: 'Invalid token or user not active',
          },
        });
      }

      req.user = {
        id: user.id,
        email: user.email,
        username: user.username,
        role: user.role,
      };
      
      next();
    } catch (jwtError) {
      logger.error('JWT verification failed:', jwtError);
      return res.status(401).json({
        error: {
          code: 'UNAUTHORIZED',
          message: 'Invalid or expired token',
        },
```

```python
# services/suppression_service.py
from enum import Enum
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Optional, Set
import redis
import psycopg2

class SuppressionReason(Enum):
    HARD_BOUNCE = "hard_bounce"
    SOFT_BOUNCE = "soft_bounce"
    COMPLAINT = "complaint"
    UNSUBSCRIBE = "unsubscribe"
    MANUAL = "manual"
    INVALID_EMAIL = "invalid_email"

class SuppressionListService:
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis, db_conn):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.db = db_conn
        self.cache_ttl = 3600  # 1 hour
    
    def add_to_suppression(
        self, 
        email: str, 
        reason: SuppressionReason,
        permanent: bool = True,
        duration_days: Optional[int] = None
    ):
        """Add email to suppression list"""
        email_lower = email.lower()
        
        # Add to database (source of truth)
        with self.db.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                INSERT INTO suppression_list 
                (email, reason, permanent, expires_at, created_at)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, NOW())
                ON CONFLICT (email) 
                DO UPDATE SET 
                    reason = EXCLUDED.reason,
                    permanent = EXCLUDED.permanent,
                    expires_at = EXCLUDED.expires_at,
                    updated_at = NOW()
            """, (
                email_lower,
                reason.value,
                permanent,
                None if permanent else datetime.now() + timedelta(days=duration_days)
            ))
            self.db.commit()
        
        # Add to Redis cache
        cache_key = f"suppression:{email_lower}"
        self.redis.setex(
            cache_key,
            self.cache_ttl if permanent else duration_days * 86400,
            reason.value
        )
        
        # Add to bloom filter for fast checking
        self.redis.execute_command('BF.ADD', 'suppression_bloom', email_lower)
    
    def is_suppressed(self, email: str) -> tuple[bool, Optional[str]]:
        """Check if email is suppressed (with reason)"""
        email_lower = email.lower()
        
        # Check bloom filter first (fast negative check)
        exists = self.redis.execute_command('BF.EXISTS', 'suppression_bloom', email_lower)
        if not exists:
            return False, None
        
        # Check Redis cache
        cache_key = f"suppression:{email_lower}"
        cached = self.redis.get(cache_key)
        if cached:
            return True, cached.decode()
        
        # Check database
        with self.db.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT reason FROM suppression_list
                WHERE email = %s 
                AND (permanent = TRUE OR expires_at > NOW())
            """, (email_lower,))
            result = cur.fetchone()
            
            if result:
                reason = result[0]
                # Update cache
                self.redis.setex(cache_key, self.cache_ttl, reason)
                return True, reason
        
        return False, None
    
    def remove_from_suppression(self, email: str):
        """Remove email from suppression list"""
        email_lower = email.lower()
        
        with self.db.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM suppression_list WHERE email = %s", (email_lower,))
            self.db.commit()
        
        self.redis.delete(f"suppression:{email_lower}")
        # Note: Can't remove from bloom filter, but will be handled by DB check

    def bulk_import_suppressions(self, emails: Set[str], reason: SuppressionReason):
        """Bulk import suppression list"""
        emails_lower = [e.lower() for e in emails]
        
        with self.db.cursor() as cur:
            # Use batch insert
            psycopg2.extras.execute_batch(
                cur,
                """
                INSERT INTO suppression_list (email, reason, permanent, created_at)
                VALUES (%s, %s, TRUE, NOW())
                ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING
                """,
                [(email, reason.value) for email in emails_lower],
                page_size=1000
            )
            self.db.commit()
        
        # Add to bloom filter
        for email in emails_lower:
            self.redis.execute_command('BF.ADD', 'suppression_bloom', email)
```

```python
        """Handle permanent delivery failure"""

            'mailbox_full': SuppressionReason.HARD_BOUNCE,
        }

        reason = reasons.get(subtype, SuppressionReason.HARD_BOUNCE)
```

```python
# services/reputation_service.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List

@dataclass
class ReputationMetrics:
    bounce_rate: float
    complaint_rate: float
    open_rate: float
    click_rate: float
    sender_score: int  # 0-100
    blacklist_status: List[str]

class ReputationService:
    def __init__(self, db_conn, redis_client):
        self.db = db_conn
        self.redis = redis_client
        
        # Thresholds
        self.max_bounce_rate = 0.05  # 5%
        self.max_complaint_rate = 0.001  # 0.1%
        self.min_sender_score = 80
    
    def get_current_reputation(self) -> ReputationMetrics:
        """Get current reputation metrics"""
        metrics = self._calculate_metrics(days=7)
        
        # Check blacklists
        blacklists = self._check_blacklists()
        
        return ReputationMetrics(
            bounce_rate=metrics['bounce_rate'],
            complaint_rate=metrics['complaint_rate'],
            open_rate=metrics['open_rate'],
            click_rate=metrics['click_rate'],
            sender_score=self._calculate_sender_score(metrics),
            blacklist_status=blacklists
        )
    
    def _calculate_metrics(self, days: int) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Calculate email metrics"""
        with self.db.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT 
                    COUNT(*) as total_sent,
                    SUM(CASE WHEN bounced = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as bounces,
                    SUM(CASE WHEN complained = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as complaints,
                    SUM(CASE WHEN opened = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as opens,
                    SUM(CASE WHEN clicked = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as clicks
                FROM email_events
                WHERE sent_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '%s days'
            """, (days,))
            
            result = cur.fetchone()
            total = result[0] or 1  # Avoid division by zero
            
            return {
                'bounce_rate': result[1] / total,
                'complaint_rate': result[2] / total,
                'open_rate': result[3] / total,
                'click_rate': result[4] / total,
            }
    
    def _calculate_sender_score(self, metrics: Dict) -> int:
        """Calculate sender reputation score (0-100)"""
        score = 100
        
        # Penalize for high bounce rate
        if metrics['bounce_rate'] > self.max_bounce_rate:
            score -= (metrics['bounce_rate'] - self.max_bounce_rate) * 1000
        
        # Heavy penalty for complaints
        if metrics['complaint_rate'] > self.max_complaint_rate:
            score -= (metrics['complaint_rate'] - self.max_complaint_rate) * 10000
        
        # Reward for good engagement
        score += metrics['open_rate'] * 10
        score += metrics['click_rate'] * 20
        
        return max(0, min(100, int(score)))
    
    def _check_blacklists(self) -> List[str]:
        """Check if domain/IP is on blacklists"""
        import dns.resolver
        
        blacklists = [
            'zen.spamhaus.org',
            'bl.spamcop.net',
            'b.barracudacentral.org',
        ]
        
        found_on = []
        ip = self._get_sending_ip()
        
        # Reverse IP for DNSBL lookup
        reversed_ip = '.'.join(reversed(ip.split('.')))
        
        for bl in blacklists:
            try:
               query = f"{reversed_ip}.{bl}"
                dns.resolver.resolve(query, 'A')
                found_on.append(bl)
            except dns.resolver.NXDOMAIN:
                pass  # Not listed
            except Exception as e:
                pass  # Error checking
        
        return found_on
    
    def should_throttle_sending(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        """Determine if sending should be throttled"""
        reputation = self.get_current_reputation()
        
        if reputation.blacklist_status:
            return True, f"Blacklisted on: {', '.join(reputation.blacklist_status)}"
        
        if reputation.bounce_rate > self.max_bounce_rate:
            return True, f"High bounce rate: {reputation.bounce_rate:.2%}"
        
        if reputation.complaint_rate > self.max_complaint_rate:

        if reputation.sender_score < self.min_sender_score:
            return True, f"Low sender score: {reputation.sender_score}"
        
        return False, ""
```

```typescript
export interface StorageAdapter {

  setItem(key: string, value: string): Promise<void>;
  removeItem(key: string): Promise<void>;
  getAllKeys(): Promise<string[]>;

export class IndexedDBStorage implements StorageAdapter {
  private dbName: string;
  private storeName: string;
  private db: IDBDatabase | null = null;

  constructor(dbName = 'sync-engine', storeName = 'sync-data') {
    this.dbName = dbName;
    this.storeName = storeName;
  }

  async init(): Promise<void> {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const request = indexedDB.open(this.dbName, 1);

      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        this.db = request.result;
        resolve();
      };

      request.onupgradeneeded = (event) => {
        const db = (event.target as IDBOpenDBRequest).result;
        if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(this.storeName)) {
          db.createObjectStore(this.storeName);
        }
      };
    });
  }

  async getItem(key: string): Promise<string | null> {
    if (!this.db) await this.init();
    
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const transaction = this.db!.transaction([this.storeName], 'readonly');
      const store = transaction.objectStore(this.storeName);
      const request = store.get(key);

      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result || null);
    });
  }

  async setItem(key: string, value: string): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.db) await this.init();

    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const transaction = this.db!.transaction([this.storeName], 'readwrite');
      const store = transaction.objectStore(this.storeName);
      const request = store.put(value, key);

      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => resolve();
    });
  }

  async removeItem(key: string): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.db) await this.init();

    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const transaction = this.db!.transaction([this.storeName], 'readwrite');
      const store = transaction.objectStore(this.storeName);
      const request = store.delete(key);

      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => resolve();
    });
  }

  async getAllKeys(): Promise<string[]> {
    if (!this.db) await this.init();

    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const transaction = this.db!.transaction([this.storeName], 'readonly');
      const store = transaction.objectStore(this.storeName);
      const request = store.getAllKeys();

      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result as string[]);
    });
  }

  async clear(): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.db) await this.init();

    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const transaction = this.db!.transaction([this.storeName], 'readwrite');
      const store = transaction.objectStore(this.storeName);
      const request = store.clear();

      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => resolve();
    });
  }
}
```

```typescript
// crdt.ts
export class LWWRegister<T> {
  private value: T;
  private timestamp: number;
  private nodeId: string;

  constructor(value: T, nodeId: string, timestamp = Date.now()) {
    this.value = value;
    this.nodeId = nodeId;
    this.timestamp = timestamp;
  }

  set(value: T, timestamp = Date.now()): void {
    if (timestamp > this.timestamp || 
        (timestamp === this.timestamp && this.nodeId < this.nodeId)) {
      this.value = value;
      this.timestamp = timestamp;
    }
  }

  get(): T {
    return this.value;
  }

  merge(other: LWWRegister<T>): void {
    if (other.timestamp > this.timestamp ||
        (other.timestamp === this.timestamp && other.nodeId > this.nodeId)) {
      this.value = other.value;
      this.timestamp = other.timestamp;
      this.nodeId = other.nodeId;
    }
  }
}

export class GCounter {
  private counts: Map<string, number>;

  constructor() {
    this.counts = new Map();
  }

  increment(nodeId: string, amount = 1): void {
    const current = this.counts.get(nodeId) || 0;
    this.counts.set(nodeId, current + amount);
  }

  value(): number {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const count of this.counts.values()) {
      sum += count;
    }
    return sum;
  }

  merge(other: GCounter): void {
    for (const [nodeId, count] of other.counts.entries()) {
      const current = this.counts.get(nodeId) || 0;
      this.counts.set(nodeId, Math.max(current, count));
    }
  }

  toJSON(): any {
    return Object.fromEntries(this.counts);
  }

  static fromJSON(json: any): GCounter {
    const counter = new GCounter();
    counter.counts = new Map(Object.entries(json));
    return counter;
  }
}

export class ORSet<T> {
  private elements: Map<T, Set<string>>;
  private tombstones: Map<T, Set<string>>;

  constructor() {
    this.elements = new Map();
    this.tombstones = new Map();
  }

  add(element: T, uniqueId: string): void {
    if (!this.elements.has(element)) {
      this.elements.set(element, new Set());
    }
    this.elements.get(element)!.add(uniqueId);
  }

  remove(element: T): void {
    const ids = this.elements.get(element);
    if (ids) {
      if (!this.tombstones.has(element)) {
        this.tombstones.set(element, new Set());
      }
      for (const id of ids) {
        this.tombstones.get(element)!.add(id);
      }
    }
  }

  has(element: T): boolean {
    const elementIds = this.elements.get(element);
    const tombstoneIds = this.tombstones.get(element);

    if (!elementIds) return false;

    for (const id of elementIds) {
      if (!tombstoneIds || !tombstoneIds.has(id)) {
        return true;
      }
    }
    return false;
  }

  values(): T[] {
    const result: T[] = [];
    for (const element of this.elements.keys()) {
      if (this.has(element)) {
        result.push(element);
      }
    }
    return result;
  }

  merge(other: ORSet<T>): void {
    // Merge elements
    for (const [element, ids] of other.elements.entries()) {
      if (!this.elements.has(element)) {
        this.elements.set(element, new Set());
      }
      for (const id of ids) {
        this.elements.get(element)!.add(id);
      }
    }

    // Merge tombstones
    for (const [element, ids] of other.tombstones.entries()) {
      if (!this.tombstones.has(element)) {
        this.tombstones.set(element, new Set());
      }
      for (const id of ids) {
        this.tombstones.get(element)!.add(id);
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```typescript
      case 'custom':
        if (!this.config.resolver) {
          throw new Error('Custom resolver not provided');
        }
        return {
          ...local,
          data: this.config.resolver(local.data, remote.data, base?.data),
          timestamp: Date.now(),
          version: Math.max(local.version, remote.version) + 1
        };
      
      default:
        return this.lastWriteWins(local, remote);
    }
  }

  private lastWriteWins(local: Document, remote: Document): Document {
    if (remote.timestamp > local.timestamp) {
      return remote;
    } else if (local.timestamp > remote.timestamp) {
      return local;
    } else {
      // Tie-break using document ID
      return local.id > remote.id ? local : remote;
    }
  }

  private firstWriteWins(local: Document, remote: Document): Document {
    if (remote.timestamp < local.timestamp) {
      return remote;
    } else if (local.timestamp < remote.timestamp) {
      return local;
    } else {
      return local.id < remote.id ? local : remote;
    }
  }

  private merge(local: Document, remote: Document, base?: Document): Document {
    const merged = this.threeWayMerge(
      base?.data || {},
      local.data,
      remote.data
    );

    return {
      id: local.id,
      data: merged,
      version: Math.max(local.version, remote.version) + 1,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      vectorClock: this.mergeVectorClocks(local.vectorClock, remote.vectorClock)
    };
  }

  private threeWayMerge(base: any, local: any, remote: any): any {
    if (typeof local !== 'object' || typeof remote !== 'object') {
      return remote.timestamp > local.timestamp ? remote : local;
    }

    const result: any = { ...base };

    // Get all unique keys
    const allKeys = new Set([
      ...Object.keys(base || {}),
      ...Object.keys(local || {}),
      ...Object.keys(remote || {})
    ]);

    for (const key of allKeys) {
      const baseValue = base?.[key];
      const localValue = local?.[key];
      const remoteValue = remote?.[key];

      // Both modified differently
      if (localValue !== baseValue && remoteValue !== baseValue) {
        if (JSON.stringify(localValue) === JSON.stringify(remoteValue)) {
          result[key] = localValue;
        } else if (typeof localValue === 'object' && typeof remoteValue === 'object') {
          result[key] = this.threeWayMerge(baseValue, localValue, remoteValue);
        } else {
          // Conflict - prefer remote
          result[key] = remoteValue;
        }
      }
      // Only local modified
      else if (localValue !== baseValue) {
        result[key] = localValue;
      }
      // Only remote modified
      else if (remoteValue !== baseValue) {
        result[key] = remoteValue;
      }
      // No change
      else {
        result[key] = baseValue;
      }
    }

    return result;
  }

  private mergeVectorClocks(vc1: VectorClock, vc2: VectorClock): VectorClock {
    const result: VectorClock = { ...vc1 };

    for (const [nodeId, clock] of Object.entries(vc2)) {
      result[nodeId] = Math.max(result[nodeId] || 0, clock);
    }

    return result;
  }

  compareVectorClocks(vc1: VectorClock, vc2: VectorClock): 'before' | 'after' | 'concurrent' {
    let vc1Greater = false;
    let vc2Greater = false;

    const allNodes = new Set([...Object.keys(vc1), ...Object.keys(vc2)]);

    for (const node of allNodes) {
      const v1 = vc1[node] || 0;
      const v2 = vc2[node] || 0;

      if (v1 > v2) vc1Greater = true;
      if (v2 > v1) vc2Greater = true;
    }

    if (vc1Greater && !vc2Greater) return 'after';
    if (vc2Greater && !vc1Greater) return 'before';
    if (!vc1Greater && !vc2Greater) return 'before'; // Equal
    return 'concurrent';
  }
}
```
