## Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff

```typescript
// retry.ts
export class RetryManager {
  private baseDelay: number;
  private maxDelay: number;
  private maxRetries: number;

  constructor(
    baseDelay = 1000,
    maxDelay = 60000,
    maxRetries = 5
  ) {
    this.baseDelay = baseDelay;
    this.maxDelay = maxDelay;
    this.maxRetries = maxRetries;
  }

  async executeWithRetry<T>(
    operation: () => Promise<T>,
    onRetry?: (attempt: number, error: Error) => void
  ): Promise<T> {
    let lastError: Error;

    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < this.maxRetries; attempt++) {
      try {
        return await operation();
      } catch (error) {
        lastError = error as Error;

        if (attempt < this.maxRetries - 1) {
          const delay = this.calculateDelay(attempt);
          onRetry?.(attempt, lastError);
          await this.sleep(delay);
        }
      }
    }

    throw lastError!;
  }

  private calculateDelay(attempt: number): number {
    // Exponential backoff with jitter
    const exponentialDelay = Math.min(
      this.baseDelay * Math.pow(2, attempt),
      this.maxDelay
    );

    // Add jitter (±25%)
    const jitter = exponentialDelay * 0.25 * (Math.random() * 2 - 1);
    return Math.floor(exponentialDelay + jitter);
  }

  private sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
    return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
  }

  shouldRetry(error: Error): boolean {
    // Retry on network errors
    if (error.message.includes('network') || 
        error.message.includes('timeout') ||
        error.message.includes('fetch')) {
      return true;
    }

    // Don't retry on client errors (4xx)
    if (error.message.includes('400') ||
        error.message.includes('401') ||
        error.message.includes('403') ||
        error.message.includes('404')) {
      return false;
    }

    // Retry on server errors (5xx)
    if (error.message.includes('500') ||
        error.message.includes('502') ||
        error.message.includes('503')) {
      return true;
    }

    return false;
  }
}
```

```typescript
export interface TelemetryEvent {
  type: string;
  timestamp: number;
  data: any;
  level: 'debug' | 'info' | 'warning' | 'error';
}

export class Telemetry {
  private events: TelemetryEvent[] = [];
  private metrics: SyncMetrics;
  private listeners: Map<string, Function[]> = new Map();
  private maxEvents = 1000;

  constructor() {
    this.metrics = {
      operationsQueued: 0,
      operationsSynced: 0,
      operationsFailed: 0,
      conflictsResolved: 0,
      avgSyncTime: 0,
      lastSyncTime: 0,
      networkErrors: 0,
      retries: 0
    };
  }

  log(
    type: string,
    data: any,
    level: 'debug' | 'info' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'info'
  ): void {
    const event: TelemetryEvent = {
      type,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      data,
      level
    };

    this.events.push(event);

    // Trim events if needed
    if (this.events.length > this.maxEvents) {
      this.events.shift();
    }

    // Notify listeners
    const typeListeners = this.listeners.get(type) || [];
    const allListeners = this.listeners.get('*') || [];
    
    [...typeListeners, ...allListeners].forEach(callback => {
      callback(event);
    });

    // Console output
    if (level === 'error') {
      console.error(`[Sync] ${type}:`, data);
    } else if (level === 'warning') {
      console.warn(`[Sync] ${type}:`, data);
    } else if (level === 'debug') {
      console.debug(`[Sync] ${type}:`, data);
    } else {
      console.log(`[Sync] ${type}:`, data);
    }
  }

  updateMetric(key: keyof SyncMetrics, value: number): void {
    if (key === 'avgSyncTime') {
      // Calculate running average
      const count = this.metrics.operationsSynced || 1;
      this.metrics.avgSyncTime = 
        (this.metrics.avgSyncTime * (count - 1) + value) / count;
    } else {
      this.metrics[key] = value;
    }

    this.log('metric-updated', { key, value }, 'debug');
  }

  incrementMetric(key: keyof SyncMetrics, amount = 1): void {
    this.metrics[key] += amount;
    this.log('metric-incremented', { key, amount }, 'debug');
  }

  getMetrics(): SyncMetrics {
    return { ...this.metrics };
  }

  getEvents(filter?: {
    type?: string;
    level?: string;
    since?: number;
  }): TelemetryEvent[] {
    let filtered = [...this.events];

    if (filter?.type) {
      filtered = filtered.filter(e => e.type === filter.type);
    }

    if (filter?.level) {
      filtered = filtered.filter(e => e.level === filter.level);
    }

    if (filter?.since) {
      filtered = filtered.filter(e => e.timestamp >= filter.since);
    }

    return filtered;
  }

  on(eventType: string, callback: (event: TelemetryEvent) => void): void {
    if (!this.listeners.has(eventType)) {
      this.listeners.set(eventType, []);
    }
    this.listeners.get(eventType)!.push(callback);
  }

  off(eventType: string, callback: Function): void {
    const listeners = this.listeners.get(eventType);
    if (listeners) {
      const index = listeners.indexOf(callback);
      if (index > -1) {
        listeners.splice(index, 1);
      }
    }
  }

  clear(): void {
    this.events = [];
  }

  async exportMetrics(): Promise<string> {
    return JSON.stringify({
      metrics: this.metrics,
      events: this.events.slice(-100), // Last 100 events
      timestamp: Date.now()
    }, null, 2);
  }
}
```

```python
# slo_calculator.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List
import prometheus_client as prom

@dataclass
class SLO:
    name: str
    target: float  # 0.999 for 99.9%
    window_days: int
    query: str

class SLOTracker:
    def __init__(self, prometheus_url: str):
        self.prom = prom.Prometheus(prometheus_url)
        
    def calculate_error_budget(self, slo: SLO) -> Dict:
        """Calculate remaining error budget"""
        window_start = datetime.now() - timedelta(days=slo.window_days)
        
        # Query actual SLI value
        result = self.prom.query_range(
            query=slo.query,
            start=window_start,
            end=datetime.now(),
            step='5m'
        )
        
        current_sli = self._aggregate_sli(result)
        
        # Calculate budget
        allowed_error_rate = 1 - slo.target
        actual_error_rate = 1 - current_sli
        
        budget_remaining = (
            (allowed_error_rate - actual_error_rate) 
            / allowed_error_rate
        )
        
        return {
            'slo_name': slo.name,
            'target': slo.target,
            'current_sli': current_sli,
            'budget_remaining_pct': budget_remaining * 100,
            'budget_status': self._budget_status(budget_remaining),
            'estimated_depletion': self._estimate_depletion(
                budget_remaining, 
                actual_error_rate
            )
        }
    
    def _budget_status(self, remaining: float) -> str:
        if remaining > 0.75:
            return "healthy"
        elif remaining > 0.25:
            return "warning"
        else:
            return "critical"
```

**Indicators**: High DB connection pool usage, slow queries

```sql
-- Check long-running queries

WHERE state = 'active' 
ORDER BY duration DESC;
```

**Remediation**:
1. Identify slow queries (use pgbadger/explain analyze)
2. Add missing indexes
3. Scale read replicas if needed

### Path B: Memory Pressure
**Indicators**: High GC time, OOM warnings
```bash
# Check container memory

# Review GC logs

```

**Remediation**:
1. Increase memory limits
2. Analyze heap dumps
3. Scale horizontally

### Path C: Downstream Service Degradation
**Indicators**: Increased timeout errors, circuit breakers open
```bash
# Check circuit breaker status

```

**Remediation**:
1. Verify downstream service health
2. Adjust timeout/retry configurations

```yaml
kind: Runbook
metadata:
  name: high-api-latency
  
spec:
  triggers:
    - alert: APILatencyHigh
      severity: warning
  
  steps:
    - name: diagnose_scope
      type: prometheus_query
      query: |
        topk(5, 
          histogram_quantile(0.95, 
            sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) 
            by (le, service, endpoint)
          )
        )
      export_as: slow_endpoints
    
    - name: check_deployment_age
      type: kubernetes
      command: |
        kubectl rollout history deployment/{{.service}} 
        -n {{.namespace}} --revision=1
      export_as: last_deployment
    
    - name: auto_scale_decision
      type: decision
      condition: |
        {{.slow_endpoints.value}} > 2000 
        && {{.last_deployment.age}} < "1h"
      then:
        - action: scale_deployment
          replicas: +50%
      else:
        - action: create_incident
          assign_to: on_call_sre
    
    - name: notify
      type: webhook
      url: https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage

        channel: "#incidents"
```

## 1. Identity Verification Module

```python
# identity_verification.py
from typing import Optional, Dict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import secrets
import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum

class VerificationMethod(Enum):
    EMAIL_OTP = "email_otp"
    SMS_OTP = "sms_otp"
    DOCUMENT_UPLOAD = "document_upload"
    EXISTING_CREDENTIALS = "existing_credentials"
    TWO_FACTOR = "two_factor"

@dataclass
class VerificationRequest:
    request_id: str
    user_identifier: str
    method: VerificationMethod
    created_at: datetime
    expires_at: datetime
    attempts: int = 0
    verified: bool = False

class IdentityVerifier:
    def __init__(self, db_connection, notification_service):
        self.db = db_connection
        self.notification = notification_service
        self.max_attempts = 3
        self.otp_expiry_minutes = 15
        
    def initiate_verification(
        self, 
        user_identifier: str, 
        method: VerificationMethod,
        risk_level: str = "medium"
    ) -> VerificationRequest:
        """Start identity verification process"""
        request_id = self._generate_request_id()
        
        verification = VerificationRequest(
            request_id=request_id,
            user_identifier=user_identifier,
            method=method,
            created_at=datetime.utcnow(),
            expires_at=datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=self.otp_expiry_minutes)
        )
        
        # Store verification request
        self._store_verification(verification)
        
        # Send verification based on method
        if method == VerificationMethod.EMAIL_OTP:
            self._send_email_otp(verification)
        elif method == VerificationMethod.SMS_OTP:
            self._send_sms_otp(verification)
        elif method == VerificationMethod.DOCUMENT_UPLOAD:
            self._initiate_document_verification(verification)
        
        return verification
    
    def verify_otp(self, request_id: str, otp_code: str) -> bool:
        """Verify OTP code"""
        verification = self._get_verification(request_id)
        
        if not verification:
            return False
        
        # Check expiry
        if datetime.utcnow() > verification.expires_at:
            return False
        
        # Check attempts
        if verification.attempts >= self.max_attempts:
            return False
        
        # Verify OTP
        stored_otp = self._get_stored_otp(request_id)
        verification.attempts += 1
        
        if self._constant_time_compare(otp_code, stored_otp):
            verification.verified = True
            self._update_verification(verification)
            return True
        
        self._update_verification(verification)
        return False
    
    def _generate_request_id(self) -> str:
        """Generate unique verification request ID"""
        return f"VER-{secrets.token_urlsafe(16)}"
    
    def _generate_otp(self) -> str:
        """Generate 6-digit OTP"""
        return str(secrets.randbelow(1000000)).zfill(6)
    
    def _send_email_otp(self, verification: VerificationRequest):
        """Send OTP via email"""
        otp = self._generate_otp()
        self._store_otp(verification.request_id, otp)
        
        self.notification.send_email(
            to=verification.user_identifier,
            subject="Identity Verification Code",
            body=f"Your verification code is: {otp}\nValid for {self.otp_expiry_minutes} minutes."
        )
    
    def _constant_time_compare(self, a: str, b: str) -> bool:
        """Constant time string comparison to prevent timing attacks"""
        return secrets.compare_digest(a.encode(), b.encode())
    
    def _store_verification(self, verification: VerificationRequest):
        """Store verification request in database"""
        self.db.execute("""
            INSERT INTO verification_requests 
            (request_id, user_identifier, method, created_at, expires_at, verified)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
        """, (verification.request_id, verification.user_identifier, 
              verification.method.value, verification.created_at, 
              verification.expires_at, verification.verified))
    
    def _store_otp(self, request_id: str, otp: str):
        """Store hashed OTP"""
        hashed_otp = hashlib.sha256(otp.encode()).hexdigest()
        self.db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO otp_codes (request_id, hashed_otp) VALUES (?, ?)",
            (request_id, hashed_otp)
        )
    
    def _get_stored_otp(self, request_id: str) -> str:
        """Retrieve stored OTP hash"""
        result = self.db.execute(
            "SELECT hashed_otp FROM otp_codes WHERE request_id = ?",
            (request_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        return result[0] if result else None
    
    def _get_verification(self, request_id: str) -> Optional[VerificationRequest]:
        """Retrieve verification request"""
        # Implementation omitted for brevity
        pass
    
    def _update_verification(self, verification: VerificationRequest):
        """Update verification status"""
        self.db.execute("""
            UPDATE verification_requests 
            SET attempts = ?, verified = ?
            WHERE request_id = ?
        """, (verification.attempts, verification.verified, verification.request_id))
```

## 2. Scoped Data Extract

```python
# data_extractor.py
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Set
from dataclasses import dataclass
import json
from datetime import datetime
import asyncio

@dataclass
class DataSource:
    name: str
    type: str  # database, s3, api, logs
    connection_config: Dict[str, Any]
    tables: List[str] = None
    fields: List[str] = None

@dataclass
class ExtractionScope:
    data_sources: List[DataSource]
    user_identifier: str
    identifier_fields: List[str]  # email, user_id, etc.
    date_range: tuple = None
    categories: List[str] = None  # PII, financial, health, etc.

class DataExtractor:
    def __init__(self):
        self.extractors = {
            'database': DatabaseExtractor(),
            's3': S3Extractor(),
            'api': APIExtractor(),
            'logs': LogExtractor()
        }
    
    async def extract_user_data(
        self, 
        scope: ExtractionScope
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Extract all user data according to scope"""
        results = {
            'user_identifier': scope.user_identifier,
            'extraction_date': datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            'data_sources': {},
            'metadata': {
                'total_records': 0,
                'total_fields': 0
            }
        }
        
        # Extract from each data source concurrently
        tasks = []
        for source in scope.data_sources:
            extractor = self.extractors.get(source.type)
            if extractor:
                task = extractor.extract(source, scope)
                tasks.append(task)
        
        extractions = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
        
        # Compile results
        for i, source in enumerate(scope.data_sources):
            source_data = extractions[i]
            results['data_sources'][source.name] = source_data
            results['metadata']['total_records'] += len(source_data.get('records', []))
        
        return results

class DatabaseExtractor:
    """Extract data from relational databases"""
    
    async def extract(
        self, 
        source: DataSource, 
        scope: ExtractionScope
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Extract user data from database"""
        import asyncpg
        
        conn = await asyncpg.connect(**source.connection_config)
        results = {'records': [], 'schema': {}}
        
        try:
            # Find all tables with user data
            tables = source.tables or await self._discover_tables(
                conn, 
                scope.identifier_fields
            )
            
            for table in tables:
                # Build query based on identifier fields
                query = await self._build_extraction_query(
                    table, 
                    scope.identifier_fields,
                    scope.user_identifier
                )
                
                # Execute and collect results
                rows = await conn.fetch(query)
                
                if rows:
                    results['records'].extend([dict(row) for row in rows])
                    results['schema'][table] = [
                        {'name': k, 'type': str(type(v))} 
                        for k, v in rows[0].items()
                    ]
        
        finally:
            await conn.close()
        
        return results
    
    async def _discover_tables(
        self, 
        conn, 
        identifier_fields: List[str]
    ) -> List[str]:
        """Discover tables containing user identifier fields"""
        tables = []
        
        for field in identifier_fields:
            query = """
                SELECT DISTINCT table_name 
                FROM information_schema.columns 
                WHERE column_name = $1
                AND table_schema = 'public'
            """
            rows = await conn.fetch(query, field)
            tables.extend([row['table_name'] for row in rows])
        
        return list(set(tables))
    
    async def _build_extraction_query(
        self,
        table: str,
        identifier_fields: List[str],
        user_identifier: str
    ) -> str:
        """Build SQL query for data extraction"""
        conditions = " OR ".join([
            f"{field} = '{user_identifier}'" 
            for field in identifier_fields
        ])
        
        return f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE {conditions}"

class S3Extractor:
    """Extract data from S3/object storage"""
    
    async def extract(
        self, 
        source: DataSource, 
        scope: ExtractionScope
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Extract user data from S3"""
        import aioboto3
        
        results = {'files': [], 'total_size': 0}
        
        session = aioboto3.Session()
        async with session.client('s3', **source.connection_config) as s3:
            # List objects with user identifier in key or metadata
            bucket = source.connection_config['bucket']
            prefix = f"users/{scope.user_identifier}/"
            
            paginator = s3.get_paginator('list_objects_v2')
            async for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=bucket, Prefix=prefix):
                for obj in page.get('Contents', []):
                    # Get object metadata
                    metadata = await s3.head_object(
                        Bucket=bucket, 
                        Key=obj['Key']
                    )
                    
                    results['files'].append({
                        'key': obj['Key'],
                        'size': obj['Size'],
                        'last_modified': obj['LastModified'].isoformat(),
                        'metadata': metadata.get('Metadata', {})
                    })
                    
                    results['total_size'] += obj['Size']
        
        return results

class LogExtractor:
    """Extract user data from log systems"""
    
    async def extract(
        self, 
        source: DataSource, 
        scope: ExtractionScope
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Extract user logs from various log systems"""

    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
```

```python
        }
```

```python
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:

                    proof_hash=proof['hash']
                )
                
                deletion_report['records'].append(record.__dict__)
                deletion_report['summary']['successful'] += 1
                deletion_report['summary']['records_deleted'] += deletion_result['records_deleted']
                
                # Log to audit system
                self.audit_logger.log_deletion(record, proof)
                
            except Exception as e:
                record = DeletionRecord(
                    source=source.name,
                    table_or_location=str(source.tables),
                    identifier=scope.user_identifier,
                    record_count=0,
                    timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
                    status=DeletionStatus.FAILED,

                )
                deletion_report['records'].append(record.__dict__)

        deletion_report['completed_at'] = datetime.utcnow()
        deletion_report['summary']['total_sources'] = len(scope.data_sources)
        
        # Store deletion report
        await self._store_deletion_report(deletion_report)
        
        return deletion_report

    async def _delete_from_database(
        self,
        source: DataSource,
        scope: ExtractionScope,
        soft_delete: bool,
        retention_exceptions: List[str]
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Delete from database with transaction safety"""
        import asyncpg
        
        conn = await asyncpg.connect(**source.connection_config)
        total_deleted = 0
        
        try:
            async with conn.transaction():
                for table in source.tables:
                    # Skip retention exceptions
                    if retention_exceptions and table in retention_exceptions:
                        continue
                    
                    if soft_delete:
                        # Soft delete: mark as deleted
                        query = f"""
                            UPDATE {table} 
                            SET deleted_at = NOW(), 
                                deleted_by = 'dsar_automation'
                            WHERE {self._build_where_clause(scope.identifier_fields, scope.user_identifier)}
                        """
                    else:
                        # Hard delete
                        query = f"""
                            DELETE FROM {table}
                            WHERE {self._build_where_clause(scope.identifier_fields, scope.user_identifier)}
                        """
                    
                    result = await conn.execute(query)
                    # Parse "DELETE X" or "UPDATE Y" to get count
                    count = int(result.split()[-1])
                    total_deleted += count
        
        finally:
            await conn.close()
        
        return {'records_deleted': total_deleted}
    
    async def _delete_from_s3(
        self,
        source: DataSource,
        scope: ExtractionScope
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Delete from S3/object storage"""
        import aioboto3
        
        total_deleted = 0
        session = aioboto3.Session()
        
        async with session.client('s3', **source.connection_config) as s3:
            bucket = source.connection_config['bucket']
            prefix = f"users/{scope.user_identifier}/"
            
            # List and delete objects
            paginator = s3.get_paginator('list_objects_v2')
            async for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=bucket, Prefix=prefix):
                objects = page.get('Contents', [])
                
                if objects:
                    delete_keys = [{'Key': obj['Key']} for obj in objects]
                    await s3.delete_objects(
                        Bucket=bucket,
                        Delete={'Objects': delete_keys}
                    )
                    total_deleted += len(objects)
        
        return {'records_deleted': total_deleted}
    
    def _generate_deletion_proof(
        self,
        pre_state: Dict[str, Any],
        deletion_result: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Generate cryptographic proof of deletion"""
        
        proof_data = {
            'pre_deletion': pre_state,
            'deletion_result': deletion_result,
            'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
        }
        
        # Create hash of proof data
        proof_json = json.dumps(proof_data, sort_keys=True, default=str)
        proof_hash = hashlib.sha256(proof_json.encode()).hexdigest()
        
        return {
            'hash': proof_hash,
            'data': proof_data
        }
    
    def _build_where_clause(
        self, 
        identifier_fields: List[str],
        user_identifier: str
    ) -> str:
        """Build SQL WHERE clause"""
        conditions = [f"{field} = '{user_identifier}'" for field in identifier_fields]
        return " OR ".join(conditions)
```

```python
from enum import Enum
from queue import PriorityQueue
import threading
import time

class RetrievalTier(Enum):
    EXPEDITED = "expedited"    # 1-5 minutes, expensive
    STANDARD = "standard"      # 3-5 hours, moderate
    BULK = "bulk"             # 5-12 hours, cheapest

@dataclass
class RehydrationRequest:
    request_id: str
    object_key: str
    tier: RetrievalTier
    priority: int
    requested_at: datetime
    size_gb: float
    callback_url: Optional[str] = None
    
    def __lt__(self, other):
        return self.priority < other.priority

class RehydrationManager:
    def __init__(self, bucket_name: str, max_concurrent: int = 10):
        self.s3_client = boto3.client('s3')
        self.bucket_name = bucket_name
        self.request_queue = PriorityQueue()
        self.active_requests: Dict[str, RehydrationRequest] = {}
        self.max_concurrent = max_concurrent
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        
    def request_rehydration(self, request: RehydrationRequest) -> str:
        """Queue a rehydration request"""
        self.request_queue.put((request.priority, request))
        
        # Start processing thread if not running
        if len(self.active_requests) < self.max_concurrent:
            threading.Thread(target=self._process_queue, daemon=True).start()
            
        return request.request_id
    
    def _process_queue(self):
        """Process rehydration requests from queue"""
        while not self.request_queue.empty():
            with self.lock:
                if len(self.active_requests) >= self.max_concurrent:
                    break
                    
                _, request = self.request_queue.get()
                self.active_requests[request.request_id] = request
            
            try:
                self._restore_object(request)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error restoring {request.object_key}: {e}")
                with self.lock:
                    del self.active_requests[request.request_id]
    
    def _restore_object(self, request: RehydrationRequest):
        """Restore object from Glacier"""
        tier_map = {
            RetrievalTier.EXPEDITED: 'Expedited',
            RetrievalTier.STANDARD: 'Standard',
            RetrievalTier.BULK: 'Bulk'
        }
        
        # Check if already restored
        try:
            head_response = self.s3_client.head_object(
                Bucket=self.bucket_name,
                Key=request.object_key
            )
            
            if head_response.get('Restore'):
                restore_status = head_response['Restore']
                if 'ongoing-request="false"' in restore_status:
                    self._mark_completed(request)
                    return
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error checking restore status: {e}")
        
        # Initiate restore
        try:
            self.s3_client.restore_object(
                Bucket=self.bucket_name,
                Key=request.object_key,
                RestoreRequest={
                    'Days': 7,  # Days to keep in hot tier
                    'GlacierJobParameters': {
                        'Tier': tier_map[request.tier]
                    }
                }
            )
            
            # Poll for completion
            self._poll_restore_status(request)
            
        except self.s3_client.exceptions.RestoreAlreadyInProgress:
            self._poll_restore_status(request)
    
    def _poll_restore_status(self, request: RehydrationRequest):
        """Poll for restore completion"""
        max_polls = 1000
        poll_interval = 60  # seconds
        
        for _ in range(max_polls):
            time.sleep(poll_interval)
            
            response = self.s3_client.head_object(
                Bucket=self.bucket_name,
                Key=request.object_key
            )
            
            restore_status = response.get('Restore', '')
            if 'ongoing-request="false"' in restore_status:
                self._mark_completed(request)
                return
        
        raise TimeoutError(f"Restore timed out for {request.object_key}")
    
    def _mark_completed(self, request: RehydrationRequest):
        """Mark restoration as complete"""
        with self.lock:
            if request.request_id in self.active_requests:
                del self.active_requests[request.request_id]
        
        # Notify callback URL if provided
        if request.callback_url:
            self._notify_completion(request)
    
    def _notify_completion(self, request: RehydrationRequest):
        """Send completion notification"""
        import requests
        try:
            requests.post(request.callback_url, json={
                'request_id': request.request_id,
                'object_key': request.object_key,
                'status': 'completed',
                'completed_at': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
            })
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error notifying callback: {e}")
    
    def get_status(self, request_id: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        """Get status of rehydration request"""
        with self.lock:
            if request_id in self.active_requests:
                request = self.active_requests[request_id]
                return {
                    'status': 'in_progress',
                    'object_key': request.object_key,
                    'requested_at': request.requested_at.isoformat()
                }
        return None
```

## 3. Durability Checks

```python
import hashlib
from typing import Tuple
import concurrent.futures

class DurabilityChecker:
    def __init__(self, bucket_name: str):
        self.s3_client = boto3.client('s3')
        self.bucket_name = bucket_name
        
    def check_object_integrity(self, key: str) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Verify object integrity using ETag"""
        try:
            # Get object metadata
            response = self.s3_client.head_object(
                Bucket=self.bucket_name,
                Key=key
            )
            
            etag = response['ETag'].strip('"')
            
            # For objects <5GB, ETag is MD5
            # For multipart uploads, it's different
            if '-' not in etag:
                # Download and verify MD5
                obj = self.s3_client.get_object(
                    Bucket=self.bucket_name,
                    Key=key
                )
                
                md5 = hashlib.md5()
                for chunk in obj['Body'].iter_chunks(chunk_size=8192):
                    md5.update(chunk)
                
                calculated_etag = md5.hexdigest()
                
                if calculated_etag == etag:
                    return True, "Integrity verified"
                else:
                    return False, f"ETag mismatch: {etag} vs {calculated_etag}"
            else:
                # Multipart upload - use versioning or checksum
                return self._verify_multipart(key, etag)
                
        except Exception as e:
            return False, f"Error checking integrity: {e}"
    
    def _verify_multipart(self, key: str, etag: str) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Verify multipart upload using object lock or version"""
        # Use S3 Object Lock or versioning to verify
        try:
            response = self.s3_client.head_object(
                Bucket=self.bucket_name,
                Key=key
            )
            
            # Check if object has not been modified
            if response.get('ETag', '').strip('"') == etag:
                return True, "ETag matches"
            
            return False, "ETag changed"
        except Exception as e:
            return False, f"Verification error: {e}"
    
    def bulk_integrity_check(self, prefix: str = "", 
                            max_workers: int = 10) -> Dict:
        """Check integrity of all objects with prefix"""
        results = {
            'total': 0,
            'verified': 0,
            'failed': 0,
            'errors': []
        }
        
        # List all objects
        paginator = self.s3_client.get_paginator('list_objects_v2')
        pages = paginator.paginate(Bucket=self.bucket_name, Prefix=prefix)
        
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
            futures = []
            
            for page in pages:
                for obj in page.get('Contents', []):
                    key = obj['Key']
                    results['total'] += 1
                    
                    future = executor.submit(self.check_object_integrity, key)
                    futures.append((key, future))
            
            # Collect results
            for key, future in futures:
                try:
                    is_valid, message = future.result(timeout=300)
                    if is_valid:
                        results['verified'] += 1
                    else:
                        results['failed'] += 1
                        results['errors'].append({'key': key, 'error': message})
                except Exception as e:
                    results['failed'] += 1
                    results['errors'].append({'key': key, 'error': str(e)})
        
        return results
    
    def setup_continuous_monitoring(self, prefix: str = ""):
        """Set up continuous durability monitoring using S3 Storage Lens"""
        storage_lens_config = {
            'Id': 'durability-monitoring',
            'AccountLevel': {
                'BucketLevel': {
                    'PrefixLevel': {
                        'StorageMetrics': {
                            'IsEnabled': True,
                            'SelectionCriteria': {
                                'Delimiter': '/',
                                'MaxDepth': 5,
                                'MinStorageBytesPercentage': 1.0
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            },
            'Include': {
                'Buckets': [f'arn:aws:s3:::{self.bucket_name}'],
                'Regions': ['us-east-1']  # Adjust as needed
            },
            'IsEnabled': True,
            'DataExport': {
                'S3BucketDestination': {
                    'OutputSchemaVersion': 'V_1',
                    'Format': 'CSV',
                    'AccountId': '123456789012',  # Your account
                    'Arn': f'arn:aws:s3:::storage-lens-reports',
                    'Prefix': 'durability-reports/'
                }
            }
        }
        
        # Note: This requires S3 Control client
        return storage_lens_config
```

## 4. Cost Model

```python
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import List

@dataclass
class StorageCost:
    tier: StorageTier
    size_gb: float
    age_days: int
    access_count: int
    
    def calculate_monthly_cost(self) -> Decimal:
        """Calculate total monthly storage cost"""
        policy = TIER_POLICIES[self.tier]
        
        # Storage cost
        storage_cost = Decimal(str(self.size_gb * policy.cost_per_gb_month))
        
        # Retrieval cost
        retrieval_cost = Decimal(str(
            self.access_count * self.size_gb * policy.retrieval_cost_per_gb
        ))
        
        # Early deletion fee (if applicable)
        early_deletion_cost = Decimal('0')
        if self.age_days < policy.min_storage_days:
            remaining_days = policy.min_storage_days - self.age_days
            early_deletion_cost = Decimal(str(
                self.size_gb * policy.cost_per_gb_month * 
                (remaining_days / 30)
            ))
        
        return storage_cost + retrieval_cost + early_deletion_cost

class CostOptimizer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.policies = TIER_POLICIES
        
    def recommend_tier(self, age_days: int, size_gb: float,
                      monthly_access_count: int) -> Tuple[StorageTier, Decimal]:
        """Recommend optimal storage tier based on usage"""
        costs = {}
        
        for tier, policy in self.policies.items():
            # Skip if object is too young for tier
            if age_days < policy.min_age_days:
                continue
            
            cost = StorageCost(
                tier=tier,
                size_gb=size_gb,
                age_days=age_days,
                access_count=monthly_access_count
            ).calculate_monthly_cost()
            
            costs[tier] = cost
        
        # Return tier with lowest cost
        optimal_tier = min(costs.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])
        return optimal_tier
    
    def analyze_bucket_costs(self, objects: List[Dict]) -> Dict:
        """Analyze costs for all objects in bucket"""
        total_storage_gb = 0
        total_cost = Decimal('0')
        recommendations = []
        
        for obj in objects:
            current_tier = obj['tier']
            size_gb = obj['size_bytes'] / (1024**3)
            age_days = obj['age_days']
            access_count = obj.get('monthly_accesses', 0)
            
            total_storage_gb += size_gb
            
            # Current cost
            current_cost = StorageCost(
                tier=current_tier,
                size_gb=size_gb,
                age_days=age_days,
                access_count=access_count
            ).calculate_monthly_cost()
            
            total_cost += current_cost
            
            # Optimal tier
            optimal_tier, optimal_cost = self.recommend_tier(
                age_days, size_gb, access_count
            )
            
            if optimal_tier != current_tier:
                savings = current_cost - optimal_cost
                recommendations.append({
                    'key': obj['key'],
                    'current_tier': current_tier.value,
                    'recommended_tier': optimal_tier.value,
                    'monthly_savings': float(savings)
                })
        
        return {
            'total_storage_gb': total_storage_gb,
            'monthly_cost': float(total_cost),
            'recommendations': recommendations,
            'potential_savings': sum(r['monthly_savings'] 
                                   for r in recommendations)
        }
    
    def project_costs(self, growth_rate: float, months: int,
                     current_size_gb: float) -> List[Dict]:
        """Project costs over time with growth"""
        projections = []
        size_gb = current_size_gb
        
        for month in range(1, months + 1):
            # Age distribution (simplified)
            hot_pct = 0.3
            warm_pct = 0.3
            cold_pct = 0.2
            glacier_pct = 0.15
            deep_archive_pct = 0.05
            
            monthly_cost = Decimal('0')
            monthly_cost += Decimal(str(size_gb * hot_pct * 
                                      self.policies[StorageTier.HOT].cost_per_gb_month))
            monthly_cost += Decimal(str(size_gb * warm_pct * 
                                      self.policies[StorageTier.WARM].cost_per_gb_month))
            monthly_cost += Decimal(str(size_gb * cold_pct * 
                                      self.policies[StorageTier.COLD].cost_per_gb_month))
            monthly_cost += Decimal(str(size_gb * glacier_pct * 
                                      self.policies[StorageTier.GLACIER].cost_per_gb_month))
            monthly_cost += Decimal(str(size_gb * deep_archive_pct * 
                                      self.policies[StorageTier.DEEP_ARCHIVE].cost_per_gb_month))
            
            projections.append({
                'month': month,
                'total_size_gb': size_gb,
                'monthly_cost': float(monthly_cost)
            })
            
            size_gb *= (1 + growth_rate)
        
        return projections
```

## 5. Complete Archival System

```python
class ArchivalSystem:
    def __init__(self, bucket_name: str):
        self.bucket_name = bucket_name
        self.lifecycle_mgr = LifecycleManager(bucket_name)
        self.rehydration_mgr = RehydrationManager(bucket_name)
        self.durability_checker = DurabilityChecker(bucket_name)
        self.cost_optimizer = CostOptimizer()
        
    def setup(self, prefix: str = ""):
        """Initialize archival system"""
        # Set up lifecycle policies
        self.lifecycle_mgr.create_lifecycle_policy(prefix)
        
        # Enable versioning for durability
        s3 = boto3.client('s3')
        s3.put_bucket_versioning(
            Bucket=self.bucket_name,
            VersioningConfiguration={'Status': 'Enabled'}
        )
        
        print(f"Archival system initialized for {self.bucket_name}")
    
    def archive_data(self, key: str, data: bytes, 
                    metadata: Optional[Dict] = None):
        """Archive data with metadata"""
        s3 = boto3.client('s3')
        
        # Calculate checksum
        md5 = hashlib.md5(data).hexdigest()
        
        # Add archival metadata
        archive_metadata = {
            'archived-at': datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            'checksum-md5': md5,
            'original-size': str(len(data))
        }
        
        if metadata:
            archive_metadata.update(metadata)
        
        # Upload
        s3.put_object(
            Bucket=self.bucket_name,
            Key=key,
            Body=data,
            Metadata=archive_metadata,
            StorageClass='STANDARD'  # Will transition per lifecycle
        )
        
        return md5
    
    def retrieve_data(self, key: str, priority: int = 5,
                     tier: RetrievalTier = RetrievalTier.STANDARD) -> str:
        """Request data retrieval from archive"""
        # Get object info
        s3 = boto3.client('s3')
        response = s3.head_object(Bucket=self.bucket_name, Key=key)
        
        size_gb = response['ContentLength'] / (1024**3)
        
        request = RehydrationRequest(
            request_id=hashlib.md5(
                f"{key}{datetime.utcnow()}".encode()
            ).hexdigest(),
            object_key=key,
            tier=tier,
            priority=priority,
            requested_at=datetime.utcnow(),
            size_gb=size_gb
        )
        
        return self.rehydration_mgr.request_rehydration(request)
    
    def health_check(self, prefix: str = "") -> Dict:
        """Comprehensive health check"""
        return {
            'durability': self.durability_checker.bulk_integrity_check(prefix),
            'rehydration_queue': len(self.rehydration_mgr.active_requests),
            'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
        }
    
    def cost_report(self, objects: List[Dict]) -> Dict:
        """Generate cost analysis report"""
        return self.cost_optimizer.analyze_bucket_costs(objects)

# Usage example
if __name__ == "__main__":
    system = ArchivalSystem('my-archive-bucket')
    system.setup()
    
    # Archive data
    data = b"Important data to archive..." * 1000
    checksum = system.archive_data('documents/2024/report.pdf', data)
    print(f"Archived with checksum: {checksum}")
    
    # Later, retrieve
    request_id = system.retrieve_data('documents/2024/report.pdf')
    print(f"Rehydration requested: {request_id}")
    
    # Health check
    health = system.health_check('documents/')
    print(f"Health: {health}")
```

This comprehensive system handles all aspects of data archival with production-ready features!

```typescript
export class FeatureFlagEngine {
  private flags: Map<string, FeatureFlag> = new Map();
  private segments: Map<string, TargetingSegment> = new Map();
  private evaluationCache: Map<string, CacheEntry> = new Map();
  private metrics: MetricsCollector;
  private auditLogger: AuditLogger;
  private killSwitchMonitor: KillSwitchMonitor;

  constructor(
    metrics: MetricsCollector,
    auditLogger: AuditLogger,
    killSwitchMonitor: KillSwitchMonitor
  ) {
    this.metrics = metrics;
    this.auditLogger = auditLogger;
    this.killSwitchMonitor = killSwitchMonitor;
  }

  // Main evaluation method
  async evaluate(
    flagKey: string,
    context: EvaluationContext,
    defaultValue?: any
  ): Promise<FlagEvaluation> {
    const startTime = Date.now();
    
    try {
      // Get flag definition
      const flag = this.flags.get(flagKey);
      if (!flag) {
        this.metrics.increment('flag.not_found', { flag: flagKey });
        return this.createEvaluation(flagKey, defaultValue, 'flag_not_found');
      }

      // Check kill switch first
      if (flag.killSwitch.enabled) {
        this.metrics.increment('flag.kill_switch_active', { flag: flagKey });
        return this.createEvaluation(
          flagKey,
          flag.defaultValue,
          'kill_switch_active',
          { killSwitch: flag.killSwitch }
        );
      }

      // Check if flag is enabled
      if (!flag.enabled) {
        return this.createEvaluation(
          flagKey,
          flag.defaultValue,
          'flag_disabled'
        );
      }

      // Check environment restrictions
      if (!flag.blastRadius.allowedEnvironments.includes(context.environment)) {
        return this.createEvaluation(
          flagKey,
          flag.defaultValue,
          'environment_not_allowed'
        );
      }

      // Check cache
      const cacheKey = this.getCacheKey(flagKey, context);
      const cached = this.evaluationCache.get(cacheKey);
      if (cached && !this.isCacheExpired(cached)) {
        this.metrics.increment('flag.cache_hit', { flag: flagKey });
        return cached.evaluation;
      }

      // Check blast radius limits
      const blastRadiusCheck = await this.checkBlastRadius(flag, context);
      if (!blastRadiusCheck.allowed) {
        this.metrics.increment('flag.blast_radius_exceeded', { flag: flagKey });
        return this.createEvaluation(
          flagKey,
          flag.defaultValue,
          'blast_radius_exceeded',
          { reason: blastRadiusCheck.reason }
        );
      }

      // Evaluate targeting
      const evaluation = await this.evaluateTargeting(flag, context);

      // Cache result
      this.evaluationCache.set(cacheKey, {
        evaluation,
        timestamp: Date.now(),
        ttl: 60000, // 1 minute
      });

      // Audit logging (async)
      this.auditLogger.logEvaluation(flagKey, context, evaluation);

      // Metrics
      this.metrics.histogram('flag.evaluation_time', Date.now() - startTime, {
        flag: flagKey,
      });

      return evaluation;
    } catch (error) {
      this.metrics.increment('flag.evaluation_error', { flag: flagKey });
      console.error(`Error evaluating flag ${flagKey}:`, error);
      return this.createEvaluation(flagKey, defaultValue, 'error', { error });
    }
  }

  // Targeting evaluation
  private async evaluateTargeting(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): Promise<FlagEvaluation> {
    if (!context.user) {
      return this.createEvaluation(
        flag.key,
        flag.defaultValue,
        'no_user_context'
      );
    }

    // Check experiment first
    if (flag.experiment) {
      const experimentResult = this.evaluateExperiment(flag, context);
      if (experimentResult) {
        return experimentResult;
      }
    }

    // Evaluate segments
    const inTargetSegment = await this.evaluateSegments(
      flag.targeting.segments,
      context
    );

    if (!inTargetSegment) {
      return this.createEvaluation(
        flag.key,
        flag.defaultValue,
        'segment_not_matched'
      );
    }

    // Evaluate rollout strategy
    return this.evaluateRollout(flag, context);
  }

  // Segment evaluation
  private async evaluateSegments(
    segmentIds: string[],
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    if (segmentIds.length === 0) return true;

    for (const segmentId of segmentIds) {
      const segment = this.segments.get(segmentId);
      if (!segment) continue;

      const matches = this.evaluateSegment(segment, context);
      if (matches) return true;
    }

    return false;
  }

  private evaluateSegment(
    segment: TargetingSegment,
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): boolean {
    const results = segment.rules.map((rule) =>
      this.evaluateRule(rule, context)
    );

    return segment.combineWith === 'AND'
      ? results.every((r) => r)
      : results.some((r) => r);
  }

  private evaluateRule(rule: TargetingRule, context: EvaluationContext): boolean {
    const value = this.getAttributeValue(rule.attribute, context);
    
    switch (rule.operator) {
      case 'eq':
        return rule.values.includes(value);
      
      case 'neq':
        return !rule.values.includes(value);
      
      case 'in':
        return Array.isArray(value) && 
               value.some(v => rule.values.includes(v));
      
      case 'nin':
        return !Array.isArray(value) || 
               !value.some(v => rule.values.includes(v));
      
      case 'gt':
        return typeof value === 'number' && value > rule.values[0];
      
      case 'lt':
        return typeof value === 'number' && value < rule.values[0];
      
      case 'regex':
        const regex = new RegExp(rule.values[0]);
        return typeof value === 'string' && regex.test(value);
      
      case 'semver':
        return typeof value === 'string' && 
               satisfies(value, rule.values[0]);
      
      default:
        return false;
    }
  }

  private getAttributeValue(
    attribute: string,
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): any {
    // Check custom attributes first
    if (context.customAttributes?.[attribute] !== undefined) {
      return context.customAttributes[attribute];
    }

    // Check user attributes
    if (context.user) {
      const parts = attribute.split('.');
      let value: any = context.user;
      
      for (const part of parts) {
        value = value?.[part];
        if (value === undefined) break;
      }
      
      return value;
    }

    return undefined;
  }

  // Rollout evaluation
  private evaluateRollout(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): FlagEvaluation {
    const { rollout } = flag.targeting;

    switch (rollout.type) {
      case 'whitelist':
        return this.evaluateWhitelist(flag, context, rollout);
      
      case 'percentage':
        return this.evaluatePercentage(flag, context, rollout);
      
      case 'gradual':
        return this.evaluateGradual(flag, context, rollout);
      
      default:
        return this.createEvaluation(
          flag.key,
          flag.defaultValue,
          'unknown_rollout_type'
        );
    }
  }

  private evaluateWhitelist(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    context: EvaluationContext,
    rollout: RolloutStrategy
  ): FlagEvaluation {
    const userId = context.user?.id;
    const inWhitelist = rollout.userIds?.includes(userId!);

    return this.createEvaluation(
      flag.key,
      inWhitelist ? flag.defaultValue : this.getVariantValue(flag, false),
      inWhitelist ? 'whitelist_match' : 'whitelist_no_match'
    );
  }

  private evaluatePercentage(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    context: EvaluationContext,
    rollout: RolloutStrategy
  ): FlagEvaluation {
    const userId = context.user?.id!;
    const percentage = this.getUserPercentile(flag.key, userId);
    const enabled = percentage < (rollout.percentage || 0);

    return this.createEvaluation(
      flag.key,
      enabled ? this.getVariantValue(flag, true) : flag.defaultValue,
      'percentage_rollout',
      { percentage, threshold: rollout.percentage }
    );
  }

  private evaluateGradual(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    context: EvaluationContext,
    rollout: RolloutStrategy
  ): FlagEvaluation {
    const now = new Date();
    const activeStep = rollout.gradualSteps?.find(
      (step) => new Date(step.startDate) <= now
    );

    if (!activeStep) {
      return this.createEvaluation(
        flag.key,
        flag.defaultValue,
        'gradual_not_started'
      );
    }

    // Check segment if specified
    if (activeStep.segmentId) {
      const segment = this.segments.get(activeStep.segmentId);
      if (segment && !this.evaluateSegment(segment, context)) {
        return this.createEvaluation(
          flag.key,
          flag.defaultValue,
          'gradual_segment_no_match'
        );
      }
    }

    // Check percentage
    const userId = context.user?.id!;
    const percentage = this.getUserPercentile(flag.key, userId);
    const enabled = percentage < activeStep.percentage;

    return this.createEvaluation(
      flag.key,
      enabled ? this.getVariantValue(flag, true) : flag.defaultValue,
      'gradual_rollout',
      { percentage, threshold: activeStep.percentage }
    );
  }

  // Experiment evaluation
  private evaluateExperiment(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): FlagEvaluation | null {
    const { experiment } = flag;
    if (!experiment || !context.user) return null;

    // Check traffic allocation
    const userId = context.user.id;
    const bucket = this.getUserPercentile(`${flag.key}:experiment`, userId);
    
    if (bucket >= experiment.trafficAllocation) {
      return null; // Not in experiment
    }

    // Assign variant
    const variant = this.assignVariant(experiment.variants, userId, flag.key);

    return this.createEvaluation(
      flag.key,
      variant.value,
      'experiment',
      {
        experimentId: experiment.id,
        variant: variant.name,
      }
    );
  }

  private assignVariant(
    variants: ExperimentVariant[],
    userId: string,
    flagKey: string
  ): ExperimentVariant {
    const hash = this.getUserPercentile(`${flagKey}:variant`, userId);
    let cumulative = 0;

    for (const variant of variants) {
      cumulative += variant.weight;
      if (hash < cumulative) {
        return variant;
      }
    }

    return variants[variants.length - 1];
  }

  // Consistent hashing for user bucketing
  private getUserPercentile(salt: string, userId: string): number {
    const hash = createHash('sha256')
      .update(`${salt}:${userId}`)
      .digest('hex');
    
    const intValue = parseInt(hash.substring(0, 8), 16);
    return (intValue / 0xffffffff) * 100;
  }

  // Blast radius control
  private async checkBlastRadius(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    context: EvaluationContext
  ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; reason?: string }> {
    const { blastRadius } = flag;
    
    // Check rate limit
    const currentRate = await this.metrics.getRate(
      `flag.${flag.key}.evaluations`,
      1
    );
    
    if (currentRate > blastRadius.rateLimitPerSecond) {
      return { allowed: false, reason: 'rate_limit_exceeded' };
    }

    // Check max users (using approximate counting)
    const activeUsers = await this.metrics.getGauge(
      `flag.${flag.key}.active_users`
    );
    
    if (activeUsers >= blastRadius.maxUsers) {
      return { allowed: false, reason: 'max_users_exceeded' };
    }

    return { allowed: true };
  }

  // Helper methods
  private createEvaluation(
    flagKey: string,
    value: any,
    reason: string,
    metadata?: Record<string, any>
  ): FlagEvaluation {
    return {
      flagKey,
      value,
      reason,
      metadata,
      timestamp: new Date(),
    };
  }

  private getCacheKey(flagKey: string, context: EvaluationContext): string {
    return `${flagKey}:${context.user?.id}:${context.environment}`;
  }

  private isCacheExpired(entry: CacheEntry): boolean {
    return Date.now() - entry.timestamp > entry.ttl;
  }

  private getVariantValue(flag: FeatureFlag, enabled: boolean): any {
    // Return appropriate value based on flag type
    return enabled ? flag.defaultValue : this.getDisabledValue(flag.defaultValue);
  }

  private getDisabledValue(defaultValue: any): any {
    if (typeof defaultValue === 'boolean') return false;
    if (typeof defaultValue === 'number') return 0;
    if (typeof defaultValue === 'string') return '';
    if (Array.isArray(defaultValue)) return [];
    if (typeof defaultValue === 'object') return {};
    return null;
  }

  // Admin methods
  loadFlags(flags: FeatureFlag[]): void {
    flags.forEach(flag => this.flags.set(flag.key, flag));
  }

  loadSegments(segments: TargetingSegment[]): void {
    segments.forEach(segment => this.segments.set(segment.id, segment));
  }

  clearCache(): void {
    this.evaluationCache.clear();
  }
}

interface FlagEvaluation {
  flagKey: string;
  value: any;
  reason: string;
  metadata?: Record<string, any>;
  timestamp: Date;
}

interface CacheEntry {
  evaluation: FlagEvaluation;
  timestamp: number;
  ttl: number;
}
```

```typescript
// kill-switch/kill-switch-monitor.ts
export class KillSwitchMonitor {
  private flagEngine: FeatureFlagEngine;
  private alerting: AlertingService;
  private storage: FlagStorage;
  private metrics: MetricsCollector;

  // Automatic kill switch triggers
  private triggers: KillSwitchTrigger[] = [
    {
      name: 'error_rate',
      check: async (flag: FeatureFlag) => {
        const errorRate = await this.metrics.getRate(
          `flag.${flag.key}.errors`,
          60 // last minute
        );
        return errorRate > 0.1; // 10% error rate
      },
      severity: 'critical',
    },
    {
      name: 'latency_spike',
      check: async (flag: FeatureFlag) => {
        const p99 = await this.metrics.getPercentile(
          `flag.${flag.key}.latency`,
          99,
          60
        );
        return p99 > 1000; // 1 second
      },
      severity: 'high',
    },
    {
      name: 'traffic_anomaly',
      check: async (flag: FeatureFlag) => {
        const currentTraffic = await this.metrics.getRate(
          `flag.${flag.key}.evaluations`,
          60
        );
        const baselineTraffic = await this.metrics.getRate(
          `flag.${flag.key}.evaluations`,
          3600 // last hour average
        );
        return currentTraffic > baselineTraffic * 3; // 3x spike
      },
      severity: 'medium',
    },
  ];

  async startMonitoring(): Promise<void> {
    setInterval(() => this.monitorFlags(), 10000); // Every 10 seconds
  }

  private async monitorFlags(): Promise<void> {
    const flags = await this.storage.getAllFlags();

    for (const flag of flags) {
      if (flag.killSwitch.enabled) continue; // Already killed

      for (const trigger of this.triggers) {
        try {
          const shouldKill = await trigger.check(flag);

          if (shouldKill) {
            await this.activateKillSwitch(flag, trigger);
            break; // Stop checking other triggers
          }
        } catch (error) {
          console.error(
            `Error checking kill switch trigger ${trigger.name}:`,
            error
          );
        }
      }
    }
  }

  async activateKillSwitch(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    trigger?: KillSwitchTrigger,
    userId?: string,
    reason?: string
  ): Promise<void> {
    console.warn(
      `🚨 Activating kill switch for flag: ${flag.key}`,
      { trigger: trigger?.name, reason }
    );

    // Update flag
    flag.killSwitch = {
      enabled: true,
      triggeredAt: new Date(),
      triggeredBy: userId || 'system',
      reason: reason || trigger?.name || 'manual',
    };

    await this.storage.updateFlag(flag);

    // Clear caches immediately
    this.flagEngine.clearCache();

    // Alert
    await this.alerting.sendAlert({
      severity: trigger?.severity || 'critical',
      title: `Kill Switch Activated: ${flag.key}`,
      message: `Kill switch activated for flag ${flag.key}. Reason: ${reason || trigger?.name}`,
      flag: flag.key,
      metadata: { trigger: trigger?.name, reason },
    });

    // Metrics
    this.metrics.increment('killswitch.activated', {
      flag: flag.key,
      trigger: trigger?.name || 'manual',
    });
  }

  async deactivateKillSwitch(
    flagKey: string,
    userId: string,
    reason: string
  ): Promise<void> {
    const flag = await this.storage.getFlag(flagKey);
    if (!flag) throw new Error(`Flag not found: ${flagKey}`);

    console.log(`Deactivating kill switch for flag: ${flagKey}`, { reason });

    flag.killSwitch.enabled = false;
    await this.storage.updateFlag(flag);

    this.flagEngine.clearCache();

    await this.alerting.sendAlert({
      severity: 'info',
      title: `Kill Switch Deactivated: ${flagKey}`,
      message: `Kill switch deactivated for flag ${flagKey} by ${userId}. Reason: ${reason}`,
      flag: flagKey,
    });

    this.metrics.increment('killswitch.deactivated', { flag: flagKey });
  }
}

interface KillSwitchTrigger {
  name: string;
  check: (flag: FeatureFlag) => Promise<boolean>;
  severity: 'critical' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'low';
}
```

// migration/flag-lifecycle-manager.ts
export class FlagLifecycleManager {
  private storage: FlagStorage;
  private metrics: MetricsCollector;
  private alerting: AlertingService;

  async analyzeFlagUsage(flagKey: string): Promise<FlagUsageReport> {
    const flag = await this.storage.getFlag(flagKey);
    if (!flag) throw new Error(`Flag not found: ${flagKey}`);

    const last30Days = Date.now() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

    return {
      flag: flagKey,
      evaluations: await this.metrics.sum(
        `flag.${flagKey}.evaluations`,
        last30Days
      ),
      uniqueUsers: await this.metrics.cardinality(
        `flag.${flagKey}.users`,
        last30Days
      ),
      variants: await this.getVariantDistribution(flagKey, last30Days),
      codeReferences: await this.findCodeReferences(flagKey),
      dependencies: flag.dependencies,
      ageInDays: this.getAgeInDays(flag.lifecycle.createdAt),
      recommendation: this.getRecommendation(flag),
    };
  }

  private getRecommendation(flag: FeatureFlag): string {
    const ageInDays = this.getAgeInDays(flag.lifecycle.createdAt);

    // Flag is in stable state and old
    if (flag.lifecycle.stage === 'stable' && ageInDays > 90) {
      // Check if rollout is at 100%
      if (this.isFullRollout(flag)) {
        return 'REMOVE_FLAG - Flag has been at 100% rollout for 90+ days';
      }
    }

    // Flag is deprecated
    if (flag.lifecycle.stage === 'deprecated') {
      if (flag.lifecycle.removalDate && new Date(flag.lifecycle.removalDate) < new Date()) {
        return 'REMOVE_NOW - Removal date has passed';
      }
      return 'PREPARE_REMOVAL - Flag is deprecated';
    }

    // Flag has no recent evaluations
    const hasRecentActivity = true; // Check metrics
    if (!hasRecentActivity && ageInDays > 30) {
      return 'CONSIDER_DEPRECATION - No recent activity';
    }

    return 'KEEP - Flag is actively used';
  }

  private isFullRollout(flag: FeatureFlag): boolean {
    const { rollout } = flag.targeting;
    
    if (rollout.type === 'percentage') {
      return rollout.percentage === 100;
    }
    
    if (rollout.type === 'gradual' && rollout.gradualSteps) {
      const lastStep = rollout.gradualSteps[rollout.gradualSteps.length - 1];
      return lastStep.percentage === 100 &&
             new Date(lastStep.startDate) < new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    }
    
    return false;
  }

  async deprecateFlag(
    flagKey: string,
    userId: string,
    removalDate: Date
  ): Promise<void> {
    const flag = await this.storage.getFlag(flagKey);
    if (!flag) throw new Error(`Flag not found: ${flagKey}`);

    flag.lifecycle.stage = 'deprecated';
    flag.lifecycle.deprecationDate = new Date();
    flag.lifecycle.removalDate = removalDate;
    flag.lifecycle.lastModifiedBy = userId;
    flag.lifecycle.lastModifiedAt = new Date();

    await this.storage.updateFlag(flag);

    // Alert team
    await this.alerting.sendAlert({
      severity: 'info',
      title: `Flag Deprecated: ${flagKey}`,
      message: `Flag ${flagKey} has been deprecated. Scheduled for removal on ${removalDate.toISOString()}`,
      flag: flagKey,
    });

    this.metrics.increment('flag.deprecated', { flag: flagKey });
  }

  async removeFlag(flagKey: string, userId: string): Promise<FlagRemovalPlan> {
    const flag = await this.storage.getFlag(flagKey);
    if (!flag) throw new Error(`Flag not found: ${flagKey}`);

    // Pre-removal checks
    const checks: RemovalCheck[] = [
      {
        name: 'deprecation_status',
        passed: flag.lifecycle.stage === 'deprecated',
        message: flag.lifecycle.stage === 'deprecated'
          ? 'Flag is properly deprecated'
          : 'Flag must be deprecated before removal',
      },
      {
        name: 'removal_date',
        passed: flag.lifecycle.removalDate 
          ? new Date(flag.lifecycle.removalDate) <= new Date()
          : false,
        message: 'Removal date has been reached',
      },
      {
        name: 'dependencies',
        passed: flag.dependencies.length === 0,
        message: flag.dependencies.length === 0
          ? 'No dependencies found'
          : `Dependencies exist: ${flag.dependencies.join(', ')}`,
      },
      {
        name: 'code_references',
        passed: false, // Will be checked
        message: 'Checking code references...',
      },
    ];

    // Check code references
    const references = await this.findCodeReferences(flagKey);
    checks[3].passed = references.length === 0;
    checks[3].message = references.length === 0
      ? 'No code references found'
      : `Found ${references.length} code references`;

    const canRemove = checks.every((check) => check.passed);

    return {
      flagKey,
      canRemove,
      checks,
      codeReferences: references,
      steps: this.getRemovalSteps(flag, references),
    };
  }

  private getRemovalSteps(
    flag: FeatureFlag,
    references: CodeReference[]
  ): RemovalStep[] {
    const steps: RemovalStep[] = [];

    if (references.length > 0) {
      steps.push({
        order: 1,
        description: 'Remove code references',
        details: references.map((ref) => `${ref.file}:${ref.line}`),
      });
    }

    if (flag.dependencies.length > 0) {
      steps.push({
        order: 2,
        description: 'Update dependent flags',
        details: flag.dependencies,
      });
    }

    steps.push({
      order: steps.length + 1,
      description: 'Archive flag configuration',
      details: ['Export flag data for audit trail'],
    });

    steps.push({
      order: steps.length + 1,
      description: 'Delete flag from system',
      details: ['Remove from database and caches'],
    });

    return steps;
  }

  // Code scanning
  private async findCodeReferences(flagKey: string): Promise<CodeReference[]> {
    // This would integrate with your code scanning tool
    // For example: grep, GitHub Code Search, etc.
    return [];
  }

  private getAgeInDays(createdAt: Date): number {
    return Math.floor((Date.now() - createdAt.getTime()) / (24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
  }

  private async getVariantDistribution(
    flagKey: string,
    since: number
  ): Promise<Record<string, number>> {
    // Query metrics to get variant distribution

  }
}

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Set
import networkx as nx

@dataclass
class DomainCandidate:
    name: str
    business_value: int
    complexity: int
    team_ownership: str
    change_frequency: float
    coupling_score: int
    data_tables: List[str]
    dependencies: Set[str]

class DomainDecomposer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.dependency_graph = nx.DiGraph()
    
    def analyze_coupling(self, domains: List[DomainCandidate]) -> dict:
        """Analyze coupling between domain candidates"""
        for domain in domains:
            self.dependency_graph.add_node(domain.name)
            for dep in domain.dependencies:
                self.dependency_graph.add_edge(domain.name, dep)
        
        return {
            'cycles': list(nx.simple_cycles(self.dependency_graph)),
            'strongly_connected': list(nx.strongly_connected_components(self.dependency_graph)),
            'coupling_scores': self._calculate_coupling_scores()
        }
    
    def _calculate_coupling_scores(self) -> dict:
        """Calculate afferent and efferent coupling"""
        scores = {}
        for node in self.dependency_graph.nodes():
            afferent = self.dependency_graph.in_degree(node)  # Dependencies on this
            efferent = self.dependency_graph.out_degree(node)  # This depends on others
            instability = efferent / (afferent + efferent) if (afferent + efferent) > 0 else 0
            scores[node] = {
                'afferent': afferent,
                'efferent': efferent,
                'instability': instability
            }
        return scores
    
    def recommend_migration_order(self, domains: List[DomainCandidate]) -> List[str]:
        """Recommend migration order based on multiple factors"""
        scored_domains = []
        
        for domain in domains:
            # Lower coupling, higher business value = migrate first
            score = (
                domain.business_value * 2 +  # Business value weight
                (10 - domain.coupling_score) +  # Lower coupling is better
                domain.change_frequency * 1.5 -  # High change frequency benefits from isolation
                domain.complexity * 0.5  # Lower complexity is easier
            )
            scored_domains.append((score, domain.name))
        
        scored_domains.sort(reverse=True)
        return [name for _, name in scored_domains]

# Example usage
domains = [
    DomainCandidate(
        name="notifications",
        business_value=6,
        complexity=3,
        team_ownership="platform",
        change_frequency=0.3,
        coupling_score=2,
        data_tables=["notifications", "templates"],
        dependencies=set()
    ),
    DomainCandidate(
        name="orders",

]
```

```sql
WITH table_relationships AS (
    SELECT 
        tc.table_name as source_table,
        ccu.table_name AS referenced_table,
        COUNT(*) as reference_count
    FROM information_schema.table_constraints AS tc 
    JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage AS kcu
        ON tc.constraint_name = kcu.constraint_name
    JOIN information_schema.constraint_column_usage AS ccu
        ON ccu.constraint_name = tc.constraint_name
    WHERE tc.constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY'
    GROUP BY tc.table_name, ccu.table_name
),
table_domains AS (
    SELECT 
        'orders' as table_name, 'order_service' as target_service
    UNION ALL SELECT 'order_items', 'order_service'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'inventory', 'inventory_service'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'products', 'product_service'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'customers', 'customer_service'
)
SELECT 
    tr.source_table,
    td_source.target_service as source_service,
    tr.referenced_table,
    td_ref.target_service as referenced_service,
    tr.reference_count,
    CASE 
        WHEN td_source.target_service = td_ref.target_service 
        THEN 'INTERNAL' 
        ELSE 'CROSS_SERVICE' 
    END as relationship_type
FROM table_relationships tr
JOIN table_domains td_source ON tr.source_table = td_source.table_name
JOIN table_domains td_ref ON tr.referenced_table = td_ref.table_name
ORDER BY source_table;
```

```python
# data_migration/data_ownership_splitter.py
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime

class MigrationStrategy(Enum):
    SNAPSHOT_AND_SYNC = "snapshot_and_sync"
    EVENT_SOURCING_REPLAY = "event_sourcing_replay"
    DUAL_WRITE = "dual_write"
    CDC_STREAMING = "cdc_streaming"

class DataOwnershipSplitter:
    """Orchestrate data migration from monolith to microservices"""
    
    def __init__(self, source_db, target_services: Dict):
        self.source_db = source_db
        self.target_services = target_services
        self.migration_log = []
    
    async def migrate_table(
        self, 
        table_name: str, 
        target_service: str,
        strategy: MigrationStrategy,
        batch_size: int = 1000
    ):
        """Migrate a table to new service ownership"""
        
        if strategy == MigrationStrategy.SNAPSHOT_AND_SYNC:
            await self._snapshot_and_sync(table_name, target_service, batch_size)
        elif strategy == MigrationStrategy.CDC_STREAMING:
            await self._cdc_stream(table_name, target_service)
        elif strategy == MigrationStrategy.DUAL_WRITE:
            await self._enable_dual_write(table_name, target_service)
    
    async def _snapshot_and_sync(self, table_name: str, target_service: str, batch_size: int):
        """
        Phase 1: Take snapshot of current data
        Phase 2: Stream changes via CDC
        Phase 3: Cutover when caught up
        """
        print(f"[{datetime.now()}] Starting snapshot for {table_name}")
        
        # Phase 1: Snapshot
        offset = 0
        total_rows = await self._get_row_count(table_name)
        
        while offset < total_rows:
            batch = await self.source_db.fetch(
                f"SELECT * FROM {table_name} LIMIT {batch_size} OFFSET {offset}"
            )
            
            await self._write_to_target_service(target_service, table_name, batch)
            
            offset += batch_size
            progress = (offset / total_rows) * 100
            print(f"Migration progress: {progress:.2f}%")
            
            self.migration_log.append({
                'timestamp': datetime.now(),
                'table': table_name,
                'rows_migrated': len(batch),
                'total_progress': progress
            })
        
        # Phase 2: Enable CDC for ongoing sync
        await self._enable_cdc(table_name, target_service)
        
        print(f"[{datetime.now()}] Snapshot complete for {table_name}")
    
    async def _enable_cdc(self, table_name: str, target_service: str):
        """Enable Change Data Capture streaming"""
        # Implementation would use Debezium, AWS DMS, or similar
        print(f"Enabling CDC for {table_name} -> {target_service}")
    
    async def _enable_dual_write(self, table_name: str, target_service: str):
        """
        Enable writing to both old and new locations
        Used during transition period
        """
        dual_write_config = {
            'table': table_name,
            'primary': 'monolith_db',
            'secondary': target_service,
            'consistency_check': True,
            'rollback_on_failure': True
        }
        # Configure application to dual-write
        return dual_write_config
    
    async def verify_data_consistency(self, table_name: str, target_service: str):
        """Verify data matches between source and target"""
        source_checksum = await self._calculate_checksum(self.source_db, table_name)
        target_checksum = await self._get_target_checksum(target_service, table_name)
        
        if source_checksum == target_checksum:
            print(f"✓ Data consistency verified for {table_name}")
            return True
        else:
            print(f"✗ Data mismatch detected for {table_name}")
            await self._log_inconsistency(table_name, source_checksum, target_checksum)
            return False
    
    async def _get_row_count(self, table_name: str) -> int:
        result = await self.source_db.fetch_one(f"SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM {table_name}")
        return result['count']
    
    async def _write_to_target_service(self, service: str, table: str, data: List[Dict]):
        # Write to target service's database via API or direct DB access
        target_db = self.target_services[service]
        await target_db.bulk_insert(table, data)
    
    async def _calculate_checksum(self, db, table_name: str) -> str:
        # Calculate checksum for verification
        return "checksum_value"
    
    async def _get_target_checksum(self, service: str, table: str) -> str:
        # Get checksum from target service
        return "checksum_value"
    
    async def _log_inconsistency(self, table: str, source_sum: str, target_sum: str):
        print(f"Inconsistency in {table}: source={source_sum}, target={target_sum}")

# Example migration plan
async def execute_migration_plan():
    splitter = DataOwnershipSplitter(
        source_db=MonolithDB(),
        target_services={
            'order_service': OrderServiceDB(),
```

```typescript
// services/order-service/src/data-access/customer-reference.ts

/**
 * Pattern: Reference Data via ID (not foreign key)
 * Each service owns its data, references others by ID only
 */

interface CustomerReference {
  customerId: string;  // Reference only, no FK constraint
  // Cached denormalized data for performance
  customerName?: string;
  customerEmail?: string;
  cacheTimestamp?: Date;
}

class CustomerReferenceService {
  constructor(
    private eventBus: EventBus,
    private cache: RedisCache
  ) {
    // Subscribe to customer update events
    this.eventBus.subscribe('customer.updated', this.handleCustomerUpdated.bind(this));
  }
  
  async getCustomerData(customerId: string): Promise<CustomerReference> {
    // Try cache first
    const cached = await this.cache.get(`customer:${customerId}`);
    if (cached && this.isCacheValid(cached.cacheTimestamp)) {
      return cached;
    }
    
    // Cache miss - fetch from Customer Service API
    const customer = await this.fetchFromCustomerService(customerId);
    
    // Cache for future requests
    await this.cache.set(`customer:${customerId}`, {
      customerId: customer.id,
      customerName: customer.name,
      customerEmail: customer.email,
      cacheTimestamp: new Date()
    }, { ttl: 3600 }); // 1 hour TTL
    
    return customer;
  }
  
  private async handleCustomerUpdated(event: CustomerUpdatedEvent) {
    // Invalidate cache when customer data changes
    await this.cache.delete(`customer:${event.customerId}`);
  }
  
  private async fetchFromCustomerService(customerId: string) {
    // Call Customer Service API with circuit breaker
    return await this.httpClient.get(`/customers/${customerId}`);
  }
  
  private isCacheValid(timestamp: Date): boolean {
    const age = Date.now() - timestamp.getTime();
    return age < 3600000; // 1 hour
  }
}
```
