```javascript
// server/utils/webauthn.js
const crypto = require('crypto');
const base64url = require('base64url');
const cbor = require('cbor');

const RP_NAME = 'Your App Name';
const RP_ID = process.env.RP_ID || 'localhost';
const ORIGIN = process.env.ORIGIN || 'http://localhost:3000';
const CHALLENGE_TIMEOUT = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes

class WebAuthnService {
    /**
     * Generate registration options
     */
    generateRegistrationOptions(user, existingCredentials = []) {
        const challenge = this.generateChallenge();
        
        return {
            challenge: base64url.encode(challenge),
            rp: {
                name: RP_NAME,
                id: RP_ID
            },
            user: {
                id: base64url.encode(Buffer.from(user.id)),
                name: user.email,
                displayName: user.username
            },
            pubKeyCredParams: [
                { alg: -7, type: 'public-key' },  // ES256
                { alg: -257, type: 'public-key' } // RS256
            ],
            timeout: 60000,
            attestation: 'none',
            excludeCredentials: existingCredentials.map(cred => ({
                id: cred.credential_id,
                type: 'public-key',
                transports: cred.transports || ['internal', 'usb', 'nfc', 'ble']
            })),
            authenticatorSelection: {
                authenticatorAttachment: 'platform', // Prefer platform authenticators
                requireResidentKey: true,
                residentKey: 'required',
                userVerification: 'required'
            },
            extensions: {
                credProps: true
            }
        };
    }

    /**
     * Generate authentication options
     */
    generateAuthenticationOptions(credentials = []) {
        const challenge = this.generateChallenge();
        
        return {
            challenge: base64url.encode(challenge),
            rpId: RP_ID,
            timeout: 60000,
            userVerification: 'required',
            allowCredentials: credentials.length > 0 
                ? credentials.map(cred => ({
                    id: cred.credential_id,
                    type: 'public-key',
                    transports: cred.transports || ['internal', 'usb', 'ble', 'nfc']
                }))
                : undefined // Allow discoverable credentials
        };
    }

    /**
     * Verify registration response
     */
    async verifyRegistrationResponse(response, expectedChallenge, expectedOrigin = ORIGIN) {
        const { id, rawId, response: attestationResponse, type, authenticatorAttachment } = response;

        // Verify type
        if (type !== 'public-key') {
            throw new Error('Invalid credential type');
        }

        // Decode client data
        const clientDataJSON = base64url.decode(attestationResponse.clientDataJSON);
        const clientData = JSON.parse(clientDataJSON);

        // Verify challenge
        if (clientData.challenge !== expectedChallenge) {
            throw new Error('Challenge mismatch');
        }

        // Verify origin
        if (clientData.origin !== expectedOrigin) {
            throw new Error('Origin mismatch');
        }

        // Verify type
        if (clientData.type !== 'webauthn.create') {
            throw new Error('Invalid ceremony type');
        }

        // Parse authenticator data
        const attestationObject = cbor.decodeFirstSync(
            base64url.toBuffer(attestationResponse.attestationObject)
        );
        
        const authData = this.parseAuthenticatorData(attestationObject.authData);

        // Verify RP ID hash
        const rpIdHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(RP_ID).digest();
        if (!authData.rpIdHash.equals(rpIdHash)) {
            throw new Error('RP ID hash mismatch');
        }

        // Verify flags
        if (!authData.flags.up) {
            throw new Error('User not present');
        }
        if (!authData.flags.uv) {
            throw new Error('User not verified');
        }

        // Extract credential data
        const credentialId = base64url.encode(authData.credentialId);
        const publicKey = this.convertCOSEtoRaw(authData.publicKey);

        return {
            credentialId,
            publicKey: publicKey.toString('base64'),
            counter: authData.counter,
            aaguid: authData.aaguid.toString('hex'),
            backupEligible: authData.flags.be || false,
            backupState: authData.flags.bs || false,
            authenticatorAttachment,
            transports: attestationResponse.getTransports?.() || []
        };
    }

    /**
     * Verify authentication response
     */
    async verifyAuthenticationResponse(response, credential, expectedChallenge, expectedOrigin = ORIGIN) {
        const { id, rawId, response: assertionResponse, type } = response;

        // Verify type
        if (type !== 'public-key') {
            throw new Error('Invalid credential type');
        }

        // Decode client data
        const clientDataJSON = base64url.decode(assertionResponse.clientDataJSON);
        const clientData = JSON.parse(clientDataJSON);

        // Verify challenge
        if (clientData.challenge !== expectedChallenge) {
            throw new Error('Challenge mismatch');
        }

        // Verify origin
        if (clientData.origin !== expectedOrigin) {
            throw new Error('Origin mismatch');
        }

        // Verify type
        if (clientData.type !== 'webauthn.get') {
            throw new Error('Invalid ceremony type');
        }

        // Parse authenticator data
        const authDataBuffer = base64url.toBuffer(assertionResponse.authenticatorData);
        const authData = this.parseAuthenticatorData(authDataBuffer);

        // Verify RP ID hash
        const rpIdHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(RP_ID).digest();
        if (!authData.rpIdHash.equals(rpIdHash)) {
            throw new Error('RP ID hash mismatch');
        }

        // Verify flags
        if (!authData.flags.up) {
            throw new Error('User not present');
        }
        if (!authData.flags.uv) {
            throw new Error('User not verified');
        }

        // Verify counter (replay protection)
        if (authData.counter > 0 && authData.counter <= credential.counter) {
            throw new Error('Invalid counter: possible cloned authenticator');
        }

        // Verify signature
        const clientDataHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(clientDataJSON).digest();
        const signatureBase = Buffer.concat([authDataBuffer, clientDataHash]);
        
        const publicKey = crypto.createPublicKey({
            key: Buffer.from(credential.public_key, 'base64'),
            format: 'der',
            type: 'spki'
        });

        const signature = base64url.toBuffer(assertionResponse.signature);
        const verified = crypto.verify(
            null,
            signatureBase,
            publicKey,
            signature
        );

        if (!verified) {
            throw new Error('Invalid signature');
        }

        return {
            counter: authData.counter,
            backupState: authData.flags.bs || false
        };
    }

    /**
     * Generate random challenge
     */
    generateChallenge() {
        return crypto.randomBytes(32);
    }

    /**
     * Parse authenticator data
     */
    parseAuthenticatorData(buffer) {
        let offset = 0;

        // RP ID Hash (32 bytes)
        const rpIdHash = buffer.slice(offset, offset + 32);
        offset += 32;

        // Flags (1 byte)
        const flagsByte = buffer[offset];
        offset += 1;

        const flags = {
            up: !!(flagsByte & 0x01), // User Present
            uv: !!(flagsByte & 0x04), // User Verified
            be: !!(flagsByte & 0x08), // Backup Eligible
            bs: !!(flagsByte & 0x10), // Backup State
            at: !!(flagsByte & 0x40), // Attested Credential Data
            ed: !!(flagsByte & 0x80)  // Extension Data
        };

        // Counter (4 bytes)
        const counter = buffer.readUInt32BE(offset);
        offset += 4;

        let credentialId = null;
        let publicKey = null;
        let aaguid = null;

        // Attested credential data (only in registration)
        if (flags.at) {
            // AAGUID (16 bytes)
            aaguid = buffer.slice(offset, offset + 16);
            offset += 16;

            // Credential ID Length (2 bytes)
            const credIdLen = buffer.readUInt16BE(offset);
            offset += 2;

            // Credential ID
            credentialId = buffer.slice(offset, offset + credIdLen);
            offset += credIdLen;

            // Public Key (COSE format)
            const publicKeyCOSE = cbor.decodeFirstSync(buffer.slice(offset));
            publicKey = publicKeyCOSE;
            offset += cbor.encode(publicKeyCOSE).length;
        }

        return {
            rpIdHash,
            flags,
            counter,
            aaguid,
            credentialId,
            publicKey
        };
    }

    /**
     * Convert COSE public key to raw format
     */
    convertCOSEtoRaw(coseKey) {
        const kty = coseKey.get(1); // Key type
        const alg = coseKey.get(3); // Algorithm

        if (kty === 2) { // EC2 (Elliptic Curve)
            const crv = coseKey.get(-1); // Curve
            const x = coseKey.get(-2);   // X coordinate
            const y = coseKey.get(-3);   // Y coordinate

            // Create DER-encoded public key
            const publicKey = Buffer.concat([
                Buffer.from([0x04]), // Uncompressed point
                x,
                y
            ]);

            // Wrap in DER format for Node.js crypto
            return this.wrapInDER(publicKey, 'EC');
        } else if (kty === 3) { // RSA
            const n = coseKey.get(-1); // Modulus
            const e = coseKey.get(-2); // Exponent

            return this.wrapInDER({ n, e }, 'RSA');
        }

        throw new Error('Unsupported key type');
    }

    /**
     * Wrap key in DER format
     */
    wrapInDER(key, type) {
        if (type === 'EC') {
            // P-256 curve OID: 1.2.840.10045.3.1.7
            const oid = Buffer.from([0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0xce, 0x3d, 0x03, 0x01, 0x07]);
            
            return Buffer.concat([
                Buffer.from([0x30, 0x59]), // SEQUENCE
                Buffer.from([0x30, 0x13]), // SEQUENCE
                Buffer.from([0x06, 0x07]), // OID
                Buffer.from([0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0xce, 0x3d, 0x02, 0x01]), // ecPublicKey
                Buffer.from([0x06, 0x08]), // OID
                oid,
                Buffer.from([0x03, 0x42, 0x00]), // BIT STRING
                key
            ]);
        }
        
        throw new Error('Unsupported DER wrapping');
    }
}

module.exports = new WebAuthnService();

        );

        const tempUserData = await client.query(
            'SELECT * FROM challenges WHERE user_id = $1 LIMIT 1',
            [userId]
        );

        // Create user

             VALUES ($1,

                     (SELECT username FROM (VALUES ($3::text)) AS t(username)))
             ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET updated_at = NOW()
             RETURNING *`,
            [userId, req.body.email, req.body.username]
        );

        // Ensure user was created or handle registration context
        if (!userResult.rows[0] && !req.body.email) {

            ]
        );

        // Clean up challenge
        await client.query(
            'DELETE FROM challenges WHERE user_id = $1 AND type = $2',
            [userId, 'registration']
        );

        // Log action
        await this.logAudit(client, userId, 'passkey_registered', req);

        await client.query('COMMIT');

        // Create session

        );

        // Update credential counter and last used
        await client.query(
            `UPDATE credentials 
             SET counter = $1, backup_state = $2, last_used_at = NOW()
             WHERE credential_id = $3`,

            [storedCredential.user_id, 'authentication']

        await this.logAudit(client, storedCredential.user_id, 'passkey_login', req);

        await client.query('COMMIT');

        // Create session

# Task Queue Exactly-Once Semantics

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           At-Least-Once Queue               │
│  (Redelivery on timeout/failure)            │
└─────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
              │
              ▼

│         Deduplication Layer                 │

│  - Store processed task_ids with timestamp  │

              │
              ▼

│  - Remove old dedup records                 │

```python
import time
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional, Callable, Any
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import threading
import json

@dataclass
class Task:
    id: str
    payload: dict
    attempts: int = 0
    enqueued_at: float = None
    visibility_timeout: float = None
    
    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.enqueued_at is None:
            self.enqueued_at = time.time()

class DeduplicationStore:
    """Tracks processed task IDs with timestamps"""
    
    def __init__(self, retention_period: int = 7 * 24 * 3600):
        self.processed = {}  # task_id -> timestamp
        self.retention_period = retention_period
        self.lock = threading.RLock()
    
    def is_processed(self, task_id: str) -> bool:
        """Check if task was already processed"""
        with self.lock:
            return task_id in self.processed
    
    def mark_processed(self, task_id: str) -> bool:
        """Mark task as processed. Returns False if already processed."""
        with self.lock:
            if task_id in self.processed:
                return False
            self.processed[task_id] = time.time()
            return True
    
    def compact(self) -> int:
        """Remove old entries. Returns count of removed entries."""
        cutoff = time.time() - self.retention_period
        with self.lock:
            old_size = len(self.processed)
            self.processed = {
                tid: ts for tid, ts in self.processed.items()
                if ts > cutoff
            }
            removed = old_size - len(self.processed)
            return removed
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get dedup store statistics"""
        with self.lock:
            now = time.time()
            age_buckets = {'1h': 0, '1d': 0, '7d': 0, 'older': 0}
            
            for ts in self.processed.values():
                age = now - ts
                if age < 3600:
                    age_buckets['1h'] += 1
                elif age < 86400:
                    age_buckets['1d'] += 1
                elif age < 7 * 86400:
                    age_buckets['7d'] += 1
                else:
                    age_buckets['older'] += 1
            
            return {
                'total_entries': len(self.processed),
                'age_distribution': age_buckets,
                'memory_estimate_mb': len(self.processed) * 100 / 1024 / 1024
            }

class ExactlyOnceQueue:
    """At-least-once queue with deduplication for exactly-once semantics"""
    
    def __init__(self, 
                 visibility_timeout: int = 30,
                 max_attempts: int = 3,
                 dedup_retention: int = 7 * 24 * 3600,
                 auto_compact: bool = True,
                 compact_interval: int = 3600):
        
        self.queue = []  # Main task queue
        self.in_flight = {}  # task_id -> Task (being processed)
        self.dedup = DeduplicationStore(dedup_retention)
        
        self.visibility_timeout = visibility_timeout
        self.max_attempts = max_attempts
        self.lock = threading.RLock()
        
        # Auto-compaction
        if auto_compact:
            self._start_compaction_thread(compact_interval)
    
    def enqueue(self, task_id: Optional[str] = None, payload: dict = None) -> str:
        """Add task to queue. Returns task_id."""
        if task_id is None:
            task_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        
        with self.lock:
            # Check if already processed (even if not in queue)
            if self.dedup.is_processed(task_id):
                return task_id  # Silent dedup
            
            # Check if already in queue
            if any(t.id == task_id for t in self.queue):
                return task_id
            
            task = Task(id=task_id, payload=payload or {})
            self.queue.append(task)
        
        return task_id
    
    def dequeue(self) -> Optional[Task]:
        """Get next task with deduplication check"""
        with self.lock:
            # Return in-flight tasks that timed out
            self._recover_timed_out_tasks()
            
            while self.queue:
                task = self.queue.pop(0)
                
                # Deduplication check
                if self.dedup.is_processed(task.id):
                    continue  # Skip already processed
                
                # Check max attempts
                if task.attempts >= self.max_attempts:
                    self._move_to_dlq(task)
                    continue
                
                # Mark as in-flight
                task.attempts += 1
                task.visibility_timeout = time.time() + self.visibility_timeout
                self.in_flight[task.id] = task
                
                return task
            
            return None
    
    def ack(self, task_id: str) -> bool:
        """Acknowledge successful processing"""
        with self.lock:
            if task_id not in self.in_flight:
                return False
            
            # Mark as processed in dedup store
            self.dedup.mark_processed(task_id)
            
            # Remove from in-flight
            del self.in_flight[task_id]
            return True
    
    def nack(self, task_id: str, requeue: bool = True) -> bool:
        """Negative acknowledgment - task failed"""
        with self.lock:
            if task_id not in self.in_flight:
                return False
            
            task = self.in_flight[task_id]
            del self.in_flight[task_id]
            
            if requeue and task.attempts < self.max_attempts:
                # Requeue for retry (at-least-once behavior)
                self.queue.append(task)
            else:
                self._move_to_dlq(task)
            
            return True
    
    def _recover_timed_out_tasks(self):
        """Move timed-out in-flight tasks back to queue"""
        now = time.time()
        timed_out = [
            task for task in self.in_flight.values()
            if task.visibility_timeout and task.visibility_timeout < now
        ]
        
        for task in timed_out:
            del self.in_flight[task.id]
            if task.attempts < self.max_attempts:
                task.visibility_timeout = None
                self.queue.append(task)
    
    def _move_to_dlq(self, task: Task):
        """Move failed task to dead letter queue"""
        # In production, this would write to persistent DLQ
        print(f"Moving to DLQ: {task.id} (attempts: {task.attempts})")
    
    def compact_dedup_store(self) -> dict:
        """Manually trigger compaction"""
        removed = self.dedup.compact()
        stats = self.dedup.get_stats()
        return {
            'removed_entries': removed,
            'remaining_entries': stats['total_entries']
        }
    
    def _start_compaction_thread(self, interval: int):
        """Background thread for periodic compaction"""
        def compact_loop():
            while True:
                time.sleep(interval)
                result = self.compact_dedup_store()
                print(f"Auto-compaction: removed {result['removed_entries']} entries")
        
        thread = threading.Thread(target=compact_loop, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get comprehensive queue statistics"""
        with self.lock:
            return {
                'queue_length': len(self.queue),
                'in_flight': len(self.in_flight),
                'dedup_store': self.dedup.get_stats()
            }

# Example usage
def process_task(task: Task) -> bool:
    """Simulated task processor"""
    print(f"Processing task {task.id}: {task.payload}")
    # Simulate work
    time.sleep(0.1)

def worker(queue: ExactlyOnceQueue):
    """Worker that processes tasks with exactly-once semantics"""
    while True:
        task = queue.dequeue()
        if task is None:
            time.sleep(0.1)
            continue
        
        try:
            success = process_task(task)

            queue.nack(task.id, requeue=True)

### 2. Redis-Based Implementation

```python
import redis
import time
import json
from typing import Optional

class RedisExactlyOnceQueue:
    """Production-ready implementation using Redis"""
    
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis, queue_name: str,
                 visibility_timeout: int = 30,
                 dedup_retention: int = 7 * 24 * 3600):
        
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.queue_key = f"queue:{queue_name}"
        self.processing_key = f"queue:{queue_name}:processing"
        self.dedup_key = f"queue:{queue_name}:dedup"
        self.dlq_key = f"queue:{queue_name}:dlq"
        
        self.visibility_timeout = visibility_timeout
        self.dedup_retention = dedup_retention
    
    def enqueue(self, task_id: str, payload: dict, priority: int = 0) -> bool:
        """Enqueue with deduplication check"""
        
        # Check if already processed
        if self.redis.exists(f"{self.dedup_key}:{task_id}"):
            return False  # Already processed
        
        task_data = {
            'id': task_id,
            'payload': payload,
            'enqueued_at': time.time(),
            'attempts': 0
        }
        
        # Use ZADD for priority queue (score = priority + timestamp)
        score = priority * 1e10 + time.time()
        self.redis.zadd(self.queue_key, {json.dumps(task_data): score})
        
        return True
    
    def dequeue(self) -> Optional[dict]:
        """Atomic dequeue with deduplication"""
        
        # Lua script for atomic dequeue with dedup check
        lua_script = """
        local queue_key = KEYS[1]
        local processing_key = KEYS[2]
        local dedup_key = KEYS[3]
        local visibility_timeout = tonumber(ARGV[1])
        local now = tonumber(ARGV[2])
        
        -- Get lowest score item
        local items = redis.call('ZRANGE', queue_key, 0, 0)
        if #items == 0 then
            return nil
        end
        
        local task_json = items[1]
        local task = cjson.decode(task_json)
        
        -- Check deduplication
        if redis.call('EXISTS', dedup_key .. ':' .. task.id) == 1 then
            redis.call('ZREM', queue_key, task_json)
            return nil
        end
        
        -- Move to processing
        redis.call('ZREM', queue_key, task_json)
        task.visibility_timeout = now + visibility_timeout
        task.attempts = task.attempts + 1
        redis.call('ZADD', processing_key, now + visibility_timeout, cjson.encode(task))
        
        return task_json
        """
        
        result = self.redis.eval(
            lua_script, 3,
            self.queue_key, self.processing_key, self.dedup_key,
            self.visibility_timeout, time.time()
        )
        
        return json.loads(result) if result else None
    
    def ack(self, task_id: str) -> bool:
        """Mark task as successfully processed"""
        
        # Find and remove from processing
        processing_items = self.redis.zrange(self.processing_key, 0, -1)
        for item in processing_items:
            task = json.loads(item)
            if task['id'] == task_id:
                # Remove from processing
                self.redis.zrem(self.processing_key, item)
                
                # Add to dedup store with expiry
                self.redis.setex(
                    f"{self.dedup_key}:{task_id}",
                    self.dedup_retention,
                    time.time()
                )
                
                return True
        
        return False
    
    def nack(self, task_id: str, requeue: bool = True) -> bool:
        """Handle failed task processing"""
        
        processing_items = self.redis.zrange(self.processing_key, 0, -1)
        for item in processing_items:
            task = json.loads(item)
            if task['id'] == task_id:
                self.redis.zrem(self.processing_key, item)
                
                if requeue and task['attempts'] < 3:
                    # Requeue
                    score = time.time()
                    self.redis.zadd(self.queue_key, {item: score})
                else:
                    # Move to DLQ
                    self.redis.rpush(self.dlq_key, item)
                
                return True
        
        return False
    
    def recover_timed_out(self) -> int:
        """Recover timed-out tasks back to main queue"""
        
        lua_script = """
        local processing_key = KEYS[1]
        local queue_key = KEYS[2]
        local now = tonumber(ARGV[1])
        
        local timed_out = redis.call('ZRANGEBYSCORE', processing_key, 0, now)
        local count = 0
        
        for _, task_json in ipairs(timed_out) do
            redis.call('ZREM', processing_key, task_json)
            redis.call('ZADD', queue_key, now, task_json)
            count = count + 1
        end
        
        return count
        """
        
        return self.redis.eval(
            lua_script, 2,
            self.processing_key, self.queue_key,
            time.time()
        )
    
    def compact_dedup_store(self) -> int:
        """
        Clean up old dedup entries.
        Note: With SETEX, entries auto-expire, but this scans for manual cleanup.
        """
        cursor = 0
        removed = 0
        
        pattern = f"{self.dedup_key}:*"
        while True:
            cursor, keys = self.redis.scan(cursor, match=pattern, count=100)
            
            # Redis SETEX handles expiry automatically, just count
            removed += len(keys)
            
            if cursor == 0:
                break
        
        return removed
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get queue statistics"""
        return {
            'queue_length': self.redis.zcard(self.queue_key),
            'processing': self.redis.zcard(self.processing_key),
            'dlq': self.redis.llen(self.dlq_key),
            'dedup_entries': self.redis.dbsize()  # Approximate
        }

class TelemetryValidator:
    def __init__(self, contract: Dict, pii_map: Dict):
        self.contract = contract
        self.pii_map = pii_map
        
    def validate_and_minimize(self, event: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate event against contract and apply minimization"""
        validated_event = {}
        errors = []
        
        for field_spec in self.contract['fields']:
            field_name = field_spec['name']
            
            # Check prohibited fields
            if field_name in self.contract.get('prohibited', []):
                errors.append(f"Prohibited field: {field_name}")
                continue
            
            if field_name in event:
                value = event[field_name]
                
                # Apply minimization
                minimized_value = self._minimize_field(
                    value, 
                    field_spec.get('minimization'),
                    field_spec['piiType']
                )
                
                # Validate type
                if self._validate_type(minimized_value, field_spec['type']):
                    validated_event[field_name] = minimized_value
                else:
                    errors.append(f"Type mismatch: {field_name}")
        
        if errors:
            raise ValueError(f"Validation errors: {errors}")
            
        # Add metadata
        validated_event['_meta'] = {
            'contract_version': self.contract['version'],
            'purpose': self.contract['purpose'],
            'collected_at': self._now()
        }
        
        return validated_event
    
    def _minimize_field(self, value: Any, technique: str, pii_type: str) -> Any:
        """Apply data minimization techniques"""
        if not technique or pii_type == 'none':
            return value
            
        if technique == 'hashed':
            return self._hash_value(value)
        elif technique == 'subnet_only':
            return self._subnet_mask(value)
        elif technique == 'browser_family_only':
            return self._browser_family(value)
        elif technique == 'domain_only':
            return self._email_domain(value)
        else:
            return value
    
    def _hash_value(self, value: str, salt: str = "app_salt") -> str:
        """One-way hash with salt"""
        return hashlib.sha256(f"{value}{salt}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    
    def _subnet_mask(self, ip: str) -> str:
        """Mask IP to subnet level"""
        try:
            addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
            if addr.version == 4:
                # Keep /24 (255.255.255.0)
                network = ipaddress.ip_network(f"{ip}/24", strict=False)
                return str(network.network_address)
            else:
                # Keep /48 for IPv6
                network = ipaddress.ip_network(f"{ip}/48", strict=False)
                return str(network.network_address)
        except ValueError:
            return "invalid"
    
    def _browser_family(self, user_agent: str) -> str:
        """Extract only browser family"""
        ua = parse(user_agent)
        return f"{ua.browser.family}/{ua.browser.version_string.split('.')[0]}"
    
    def _email_domain(self, email: str) -> str:
        """Keep only email domain"""
        return email.split('@')[1] if '@' in email else "invalid"
    
    def _validate_type(self, value: Any, expected_type: str) -> bool:
        """Validate field type"""
        type_map = {
            'string': str,
            'boolean': bool,
            'datetime': (str, int),  # ISO string or timestamp
            'enum': str
        }
        expected = type_map.get(expected_type, str)
        return isinstance(value, expected)
    
    def _now(self):
        from datetime import datetime
        return datetime.utcnow().isoformat()

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List
import json

class RetentionManager:
    """Manage data lifecycle based on retention tiers"""
    
    def __init__(self, contract: Dict):
        self.contract = contract
        self.retention_map = self._build_retention_map()
    
    def _build_retention_map(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Build field -> retention days map"""
        retention = {}
        for field in self.contract['fields']:
            days = self._parse_retention(field.get('retention', '90d'))
            retention[field['name']] = days
        return retention
    
    def _parse_retention(self, retention_str: str) -> int:
        """Parse retention string to days"""
        if retention_str.endswith('d'):
            return int(retention_str[:-1])
        elif retention_str.endswith('m'):
            return int(retention_str[:-1]) * 30
        elif retention_str.endswith('y'):
            return int(retention_str[:-1]) * 365
        return 90
    
    def apply_retention_policy(self, event: Dict, event_date: datetime) -> Dict:
        """Remove expired fields from event"""
        now = datetime.utcnow()
        filtered_event = {}
        
        for field_name, value in event.items():
            if field_name.startswith('_'):
                filtered_event[field_name] = value
                continue
                
            retention_days = self.retention_map.get(field_name, 90)
            expiry_date = event_date + timedelta(days=retention_days)
            
            if now < expiry_date:
                filtered_event[field_name] = value
            else:
                # Field expired, redact
                filtered_event[field_name] = "[REDACTED]"
        
        return filtered_event
    
    def generate_deletion_query(self, table: str, days_old: int) -> str:
        """Generate SQL for field-level deletion"""
        updates = []
        
        for field, retention_days in self.retention_map.items():
            if retention_days <= days_old:
                updates.append(f"{field} = NULL")
        
        if not updates:
            return None
            
        return f"""
        UPDATE {table}
        SET {', '.join(updates)}
        WHERE timestamp < NOW() - INTERVAL '{days_old} days'
        AND ({' OR '.join([f'{f} IS NOT NULL' for f in self.retention_map.keys()])})
        """

# Automated retention job
class RetentionJob:
    """Scheduled job to enforce retention policies"""
    
    def __init__(self, contracts: List[Dict], db_connection):
        self.contracts = contracts
        self.db = db_connection
    
    def run_daily(self):
        """Daily retention enforcement"""
        for contract in self.contracts:
            manager = RetentionManager(contract)
            
            # Hot tier (7 days)
            query = manager.generate_deletion_query(
                table=f"events_{contract['eventName']}",
                days_old=7
            )
            if query:
                self.db.execute(query)
                print(f"Hot tier cleanup: {contract['eventName']}")
            
            # Warm tier (30 days)
            query = manager.generate_deletion_query(
                table=f"events_{contract['eventName']}",
                days_old=30
            )
            if query:
                self.db.execute(query)
                print(f"Warm tier cleanup: {contract['eventName']}")

    def __init__(self, contract: Dict):
        self.contract = contract
        self.allowed_purposes = set(contract.get('purpose', []))
        self.field_purposes = self._build_field_purpose_map()
    
    def _build_field_purpose_map(self) -> Dict[str, Set[str]]:
        """Map fields to allowed purposes"""
        field_map = {}
        for field in self.contract['fields']:
            purposes = field.get('purpose', self.contract.get('purpose', []))
            field_map[field['name']] = set(purposes)
        return field_map
    
    def filter_for_purpose(self, event: Dict, purpose: str) -> Dict:
        """Filter event to only include fields allowed for purpose"""
        if purpose not in self.allowed_purposes:
            raise ValueError(f"Purpose '{purpose}' not allowed for this event")
        
        filtered = {}
        for field_name, value in event.items():
            # Keep metadata
            if field_name.startswith('_'):
                filtered[field_name] = value
                continue
            
            # Check if field allowed for this purpose
            field_purposes = self.field_purposes.get(field_name, set())
            if purpose in field_purposes or not field_purposes:
                filtered[field_name] = value
        
        # Add purpose attestation
        filtered['_meta'] = filtered.get('_meta', {})
        filtered['_meta']['accessed_for_purpose'] = purpose
        
        return filtered
    
    def validate_query(self, fields: List[str], purpose: str) -> bool:
        """Validate that query fields are allowed for purpose"""
        for field in fields:

### Advanced Multi-Level Scoping

```python
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List

class CacheScope(Enum):
    TENANT = "tenant"
    USER = "user"
    ORGANIZATION = "org"
    GLOBAL = "global"

class HierarchicalCacheKey:
    """Hierarchical key structure for complex scenarios"""
    
    def __init__(self, scope: CacheScope, identifiers: Dict[str, str], 
                 resource: str, **attributes):
        self.scope = scope
        self.identifiers = identifiers
        self.resource = resource
        self.attributes = attributes
    
    def to_key(self) -> str:
        """Convert to cache key string"""
        parts = [self.scope.value]
        
        # Add identifiers in consistent order
        for key in sorted(self.identifiers.keys()):
            parts.append(f"{key}:{self.identifiers[key]}")
        
        parts.append(self.resource)
        
        # Add attributes
        if self.attributes:
            attr_str = ",".join(f"{k}={v}" 
                               for k, v in sorted(self.attributes.items()))
            parts.append(attr_str)
        
        return "::".join(parts)
    
    def get_invalidation_patterns(self) -> List[str]:
        """Get patterns to invalidate related keys"""
        patterns = []
        key_parts = [self.scope.value]
        
        for key in sorted(self.identifiers.keys()):
            key_parts.append(f"{key}:{self.identifiers[key]}")
        
        # Progressive patterns for hierarchical invalidation
        for i in range(len(key_parts)):
            pattern = "::".join(key_parts[:i+1]) + "::*"
            patterns.append(pattern)
        
        return patterns

# Usage
key = HierarchicalCacheKey(
    scope=CacheScope.USER,
    identifiers={"tenant": "t123", "user": "u456"},
    resource="preferences",
    lang="en"
)

import redis
from typing import List, Set, Pattern
import re

class TenantCacheInvalidator:
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis):
        self.redis = redis_client
    
    def invalidate_tenant(self, tenant_id: str) -> int:
        """Invalidate all cache entries for a tenant"""
        pattern = f"tenant:{tenant_id}::*"
        return self._delete_by_pattern(pattern)
    
    def invalidate_resource(self, tenant_id: str, resource: str) -> int:
        """Invalidate specific resource for tenant"""
        pattern = TenantCacheKey.build_pattern(tenant_id, resource)
        return self._delete_by_pattern(pattern)
    
    def invalidate_user(self, tenant_id: str, user_id: str) -> int:
        """Invalidate all user-specific cache"""
        pattern = f"tenant:{tenant_id}::user::{user_id}::*"
        return self._delete_by_pattern(pattern)
    
    def _delete_by_pattern(self, pattern: str) -> int:
        """Delete keys matching pattern (use with caution)"""
        deleted = 0
        cursor = 0
        
        while True:
            cursor, keys = self.redis.scan(
                cursor=cursor,
                match=pattern,
                count=100
            )
            
            if keys:
                deleted += self.redis.delete(*keys)
            
            if cursor == 0:
                break
        
        return deleted

# Better: Use Redis Sets for tracking
class TrackedTenantCache:
    """Track cache keys per tenant for efficient invalidation"""
    
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis):
        self.redis = redis_client
    
    def _tracker_key(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
        return f"cache:tracker:{tenant_id}"
    
    def set(self, tenant_id: str, key: str, value: Any, ttl: int = 3600):
        """Set value and track the key"""
        cache_key = TenantCacheKey.build(tenant_id, key)
        
        pipe = self.redis.pipeline()
        pipe.setex(cache_key, ttl, value)
        pipe.sadd(self._tracker_key(tenant_id), cache_key)
        pipe.expire(self._tracker_key(tenant_id), ttl + 300)  # Tracker lives longer
        pipe.execute()
    
    def invalidate_tenant(self, tenant_id: str) -> int:
        """Efficiently invalidate using tracked keys"""
        tracker_key = self._tracker_key(tenant_id)
        
        keys = self.redis.smembers(tracker_key)
        if not keys:
            return 0
        
        pipe = self.redis.pipeline()
        pipe.delete(*keys)
        pipe.delete(tracker_key)
        results = pipe.execute()
        
        return sum(results[:-1])

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Callable, Dict, List
from datetime import datetime

class CacheInvalidationEvent:
    def __init__(self, tenant_id: str, resource: str, 
                 action: str, metadata: Dict = None):
        self.tenant_id = tenant_id
        self.resource = resource
        self.action = action
        self.metadata = metadata or {}
        self.timestamp = datetime.utcnow()

class InvalidationStrategy(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def should_invalidate(self, event: CacheInvalidationEvent) -> bool:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_keys_to_invalidate(self, event: CacheInvalidationEvent) -> List[str]:
        pass

class ResourceUpdateStrategy(InvalidationStrategy):
    """Invalidate when resource is updated"""
    
    def __init__(self, resource_type: str):
        self.resource_type = resource_type
    
    def should_invalidate(self, event: CacheInvalidationEvent) -> bool:
        return (event.resource == self.resource_type and 
                event.action in ['create', 'update', 'delete'])
    
    def get_keys_to_invalidate(self, event: CacheInvalidationEvent) -> List[str]:
        patterns = [
            TenantCacheKey.build_pattern(event.tenant_id, self.resource_type),
            TenantCacheKey.build_pattern(event.tenant_id, f"{self.resource_type}_list"),
        ]
        
        # If specific ID, also invalidate detail cache
        if 'id' in event.metadata:
            patterns.append(
                TenantCacheKey.build(event.tenant_id, self.resource_type, 
                                   event.metadata['id'])
            )
        
        return patterns

class CacheInvalidationManager:
    def __init__(self, cache: TrackedTenantCache):
        self.cache = cache
        self.strategies: List[InvalidationStrategy] = []
    
    def register_strategy(self, strategy: InvalidationStrategy):
        self.strategies.append(strategy)
    
    def handle_event(self, event: CacheInvalidationEvent):
        """Process invalidation event"""
        for strategy in self.strategies:
            if strategy.should_invalidate(event):
                patterns = strategy.get_keys_to_invalidate(event)
                
                for pattern in patterns:
                    if pattern.endswith('*'):
                        # Handle pattern
                        self.cache._delete_by_pattern(pattern)
                    else:
                        # Direct key delete
                        self.cache.redis.delete(pattern)

### Quota-Based Fairness

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import threading

class TenantCacheQuota:
    """Enforce per-tenant cache quotas"""
    
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis, 
                 default_max_entries: int = 1000,
                 default_max_memory_mb: int = 100):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.default_max_entries = default_max_entries
        self.default_max_memory_mb = default_max_memory_mb
        self.quotas: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
    
    def set_quota(self, tenant_id: str, max_entries: int, max_memory_mb: int):
        """Set custom quota for tenant"""
        self.quotas[tenant_id] = {
            'max_entries': max_entries,
            'max_memory_mb': max_memory_mb
        }
    
    def _get_quota(self, tenant_id: str) -> Dict:
        return self.quotas.get(tenant_id, {
            'max_entries': self.default_max_entries,
            'max_memory_mb': self.default_max_memory_mb
        })
    
    def _get_stats_key(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
        return f"cache:stats:{tenant_id}"
    
    def can_cache(self, tenant_id: str, estimated_size_bytes: int = 1024) -> bool:
        """Check if tenant can add more cache entries"""
        quota = self._get_quota(tenant_id)
        stats_key = self._get_stats_key(tenant_id)
        
        # Get current stats
        stats = self.redis.hgetall(stats_key)
        current_entries = int(stats.get(b'entries', 0))
        current_memory = int(stats.get(b'memory_bytes', 0))
        
        # Check limits
        if current_entries >= quota['max_entries']:
            return False
        
        max_memory_bytes = quota['max_memory_mb'] * 1024 * 1024
        if current_memory + estimated_size_bytes > max_memory_bytes:
            return False
        
        return True
    
    def record_cache_set(self, tenant_id: str, size_bytes: int):
        """Record cache entry creation"""
        stats_key = self._get_stats_key(tenant_id)
        
        pipe = self.redis.pipeline()
        pipe.hincrby(stats_key, 'entries', 1)
        pipe.hincrby(stats_key, 'memory_bytes', size_bytes)
        pipe.expire(stats_key, 86400)  # Stats TTL
        pipe.execute()
    
    def record_cache_delete(self, tenant_id: str, size_bytes: int):
        """Record cache entry deletion"""
        stats_key = self._get_stats_key(tenant_id)
        
        pipe = self.redis.pipeline()
        pipe.hincrby(stats_key, 'entries', -1)
        pipe.hincrby(stats_key, 'memory_bytes', -size_bytes)
        pipe.execute()

class FairTenantCache:
    """Cache with fairness guarantees"""
    
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis, quota_manager: TenantCacheQuota):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.quota_manager = quota_manager
    
    def set(self, tenant_id: str, key: str, value: str, ttl: int = 3600) -> bool:
        """Set with quota enforcement"""
        size_bytes = len(value.encode('utf-8'))
        
        if not self.quota_manager.can_cache(tenant_id, size_bytes):
            # Quota exceeded - evict oldest entries
            self._evict_oldest(tenant_id, size_bytes)
            
            # Check again
            if not self.quota_manager.can_cache(tenant_id, size_bytes):
                return False  # Still can't cache
        
        cache_key = TenantCacheKey.build(tenant_id, key)
        
        # Store with metadata
        pipe = self.redis.pipeline()
        pipe.setex(cache_key, ttl, value)
        pipe.zadd(
            f"cache:access:{tenant_id}",
            {cache_key: datetime.utcnow().timestamp()}
        )
        pipe.execute()
        
        self.quota_manager.record_cache_set(tenant_id, size_bytes)
        return True
    
    def _evict_oldest(self, tenant_id: str, needed_bytes: int):
        """Evict oldest cache entries"""
        access_key = f"cache:access:{tenant_id}"
        
        # Get oldest entries
        oldest = self.redis.zrange(access_key, 0, 9)  # Remove up to 10 oldest
        
        for cache_key in oldest:
            # Get size before deleting
            value = self.redis.get(cache_key)
            if value:
                size = len(value)
                self.redis.delete(cache_key)
                self.quota_manager.record_cache_delete(tenant_id, size)
            
            self.redis.zrem(access_key, cache_key)
```

### Rate-Limited Caching

```python
import time
from typing import Optional

class TenantCacheRateLimiter:
    """Prevent cache stampede per tenant"""
    
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis,
                 max_requests_per_second: int = 100):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.max_rps = max_requests_per_second
    
    def _rate_key(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
        current_second = int(time.time())
        return f"cache:rate:{tenant_id}:{current_second}"
    
    def can_proceed(self, tenant_id: str) -> bool:
        """Check if tenant can make cache request"""
        rate_key = self._rate_key(tenant_id)
        
        pipe = self.redis.pipeline()
        pipe.incr(rate_key)
        pipe.expire(rate_key, 2)  # Keep for 2 seconds
        results = pipe.execute()
        
        current_count = results[0]
        return current_count <= self.max_rps
    
    def wait_if_needed(self, tenant_id: str, timeout: float = 1.0) -> bool:
        """Wait until request can proceed"""
        start = time.time()
        
        while time.time() - start < timeout:
            if self.can_proceed(tenant_id):
                return True
            time.sleep(0.01)
        
        return False

class RateLimitedCache:
    """Complete tenant-aware cache with all features"""
    
    def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.quota_manager = TenantCacheQuota(redis_client)
        self.rate_limiter = TenantCacheRateLimiter(redis_client)
        self.fair_cache = FairTenantCache(redis_client, self.quota_manager)
    
    def get(self, tenant_id: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Get with rate limiting"""
        if not self.rate_limiter.can_proceed(tenant_id):
            raise Exception(f"Rate limit exceeded for tenant {tenant_id}")
        
        cache_key = TenantCacheKey.build(tenant_id, key)
        return self.redis.get(cache_key)
    
    def set(self, tenant_id: str, key: str, value: str, ttl: int = 3600) -> bool:
        """Set with rate limiting and quotas"""
        if not self.rate_limiter.can_proceed(tenant_id):
            raise Exception(f"Rate limit exceeded for tenant {tenant_id}")
        
        return self.fair_cache.set(tenant_id, key, value, ttl)
```

## Complete Usage Example

```python
# Initialize
redis_client = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379, decode_responses=True)
cache = RateLimitedCache(redis_client)

# Set tenant-specific quotas
cache.quota_manager.set_quota(
    tenant_id="premium-tenant",
    max_entries=10000,
    max_memory_mb=500
)

cache.quota_manager.set_quota(
    tenant_id="free-tenant",
    max_entries=100,

# Use cache with automatic fairness
try:

    profile = cache.get("premium-tenant", "user:123:profile")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Cache operation failed: {e}")

# Invalidation

```

This comprehensive solution ensures proper tenant isolation, efficient invalidation, and fair resource usage across all tenants.

# Key Management Strategy

## Envelope Encryption Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  KMS/HSM                        │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │   Master Key (never leaves KMS)          │  │
│  └──────────────┬───────────────────────────┘  │
│                 │ encrypts/decrypts             │
│  ┌──────────────▼───────────────────────────┐  │
│  │   KEK (Key Encryption Key)               │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                  │ encrypts/decrypts
    ┌─────────────▼────────────────┐
    │  DEK (Data Encryption Key)   │  ← Stored encrypted
    │  (per file/object/record)    │     with data
    └─────────────┬────────────────┘
                  │ encrypts
    ┌─────────────▼────────────────┐
    │     Plaintext Data           │
    └──────────────────────────────┘
```

## Implementation Example

### 1. **Envelope Encryption Service**

```python
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.pbkdf2 import PBKDF2
import boto3
import os
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Tuple, Optional
import base64

class EnvelopeEncryption:
    def __init__(self, kms_client=None, key_id=None):
        """
        Initialize with KMS (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault)
        """
        self.kms = kms_client or boto3.client('kms')
        self.master_key_id = key_id
        
    def generate_dek(self, key_spec='AES_256') -> Tuple[bytes, bytes]:
        """
        Generate a new Data Encryption Key via KMS
        Returns: (plaintext_dek, encrypted_dek)
        """
        response = self.kms.generate_data_key(
            KeyId=self.master_key_id,
            KeySpec=key_spec
        )
        
        return (
            response['Plaintext'],
            response['CiphertextBlob']
        )
    
    def encrypt_data(self, plaintext: bytes) -> dict:
        """
        Encrypt data using envelope encryption
        """
        # Generate DEK
        dek_plaintext, dek_encrypted = self.generate_dek()
        
        # Encrypt data with DEK
        aesgcm = AESGCM(dek_plaintext)
        nonce = os.urandom(12)
        ciphertext = aesgcm.encrypt(nonce, plaintext, None)
        
        # Clear plaintext DEK from memory
        del dek_plaintext
        
        return {
            'ciphertext': base64.b64encode(ciphertext).decode(),
            'nonce': base64.b64encode(nonce).decode(),
            'encrypted_dek': base64.b64encode(dek_encrypted).decode(),
            'encryption_timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            'key_id': self.master_key_id
        }
    
    def decrypt_data(self, envelope: dict) -> bytes:
        """
        Decrypt data using envelope encryption
        """
        # Decrypt DEK using KMS
        encrypted_dek = base64.b64decode(envelope['encrypted_dek'])
        response = self.kms.decrypt(
            CiphertextBlob=encrypted_dek,
            KeyId=envelope.get('key_id')
        )
        dek_plaintext = response['Plaintext']
        
        # Decrypt data with plaintext DEK
        aesgcm = AESGCM(dek_plaintext)
        nonce = base64.b64decode(envelope['nonce'])
        ciphertext = base64.b64decode(envelope['ciphertext'])
        plaintext = aesgcm.decrypt(nonce, ciphertext, None)
        
        # Clear DEK from memory
        del dek_plaintext
        
        return plaintext
    
    def reencrypt_dek(self, encrypted_dek: bytes, 
                      new_key_id: str) -> bytes:
        """
        Re-encrypt DEK with new KEK (for KEK rotation)
        """
        response = self.kms.re_encrypt(
            CiphertextBlob=encrypted_dek,
            SourceKeyId=self.master_key_id,
            DestinationKeyId=new_key_id
        )
        return response['CiphertextBlob']
```

### 3. **Key Recovery System**

```python
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa, padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from typing import Dict, List

class KeyRecoverySystem:
    """
    Implements Shamir's Secret Sharing for key recovery
    Requires M-of-N key holders to recover
    """
    
    def __init__(self, threshold: int, total_shares: int):
        self.threshold = threshold  # M
        self.total_shares = total_shares  # N
        self.recovery_keys: Dict[str, rsa.RSAPrivateKey] = {}
    
    def create_recovery_shares(self, master_key: bytes) -> List[dict]:
        """
        Split master key into N shares, requiring M to recover
        """
        from secretsharing import PlaintextToHexSecretSharer
        
        # Convert key to hex
        key_hex = master_key.hex()
        
        # Create shares
        shares = PlaintextToHexSecretSharer.split_secret(
            key_hex,
            self.threshold,
            self.total_shares
        )
        
        recovery_shares = []
        for i, share in enumerate(shares):
            # Encrypt each share with recovery key holder's public key
            recovery_key = rsa.generate_private_key(
                public_exponent=65537,
                key_size=2048
            )
            
            public_key = recovery_key.public_key()
            encrypted_share = public_key.encrypt(
                share.encode(),
                padding.OAEP(
                    mgf=padding.MGF1(algorithm=hashes.SHA256()),
                    algorithm=hashes.SHA256(),
                    label=None
                )
            )
            
            recovery_shares.append({
                'share_id': i + 1,
                'encrypted_share': base64.b64encode(encrypted_share).decode(),
                'recovery_public_key': public_key.public_bytes(
                    encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
                    format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo
                ).decode()
            })
            
            # Store private key securely (in practice: HSM or secure vault)
            self.recovery_keys[f"holder_{i+1}"] = recovery_key
        
        return recovery_shares
    
    def recover_key(self, encrypted_shares: List[dict], 
                    private_keys: List[rsa.RSAPrivateKey]) -> bytes:
        """
        Recover master key from M shares
        """
        from secretsharing import PlaintextToHexSecretSharer
        
        if len(encrypted_shares) < self.threshold:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Need at least {self.threshold} shares, got {len(encrypted_shares)}"
            )
        
        # Decrypt shares
        decrypted_shares = []
        for encrypted_share, private_key in zip(encrypted_shares, private_keys):
            encrypted_data = base64.b64decode(encrypted_share['encrypted_share'])
            decrypted_share = private_key.decrypt(
                encrypted_data,
                padding.OAEP(
                    mgf=padding.MGF1(algorithm=hashes.SHA256()),
                    algorithm=hashes.SHA256(),
                    label=None
                )
            ).decode()
            decrypted_shares.append(decrypted_share)
        
        # Recover secret
        key_hex = PlaintextToHexSecretSharer.recover_secret(
            decrypted_shares[:self.threshold]

        return bytes.fromhex(key_hex)

                 envelope_crypto: EnvelopeEncryption):

        thread.start()

# Circuit Breaker with Hedging

A production-ready implementation combining circuit breaker pattern with request hedging for resilient distributed systems.

## Complete Implementation

```python
import asyncio
import time
import random
from enum import Enum
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Any, Optional, List
from collections import deque
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class CircuitState(Enum):
    CLOSED = "closed"      # Normal operation
    OPEN = "open"          # Failing, reject requests
    HALF_OPEN = "half_open"  # Testing recovery


@dataclass
class CircuitBreakerConfig:
    # Failure thresholds
    failure_threshold: int = 5  # Failures before opening
    failure_rate_threshold: float = 0.5  # 50% failure rate
    min_calls: int = 10  # Min calls before calculating rate
    
    # Timing
    timeout: float = 5.0  # Request timeout
    open_duration: float = 60.0  # Time before trying half-open
    half_open_max_calls: int = 3  # Test calls in half-open
    
    # Hedging
    hedge_delay: float = 1.0  # Delay before hedged request
    max_hedged_requests: int = 2  # Max concurrent hedges
    
    # Backoff
    base_backoff: float = 1.0
    max_backoff: float = 60.0
    jitter_factor: float = 0.3  # 30% jitter
    
    # Success sampling
    success_threshold: int = 5  # Successes to close from half-open
    sample_size: int = 100  # Rolling window size


@dataclass
class CallStats:
    successes: int = 0
    failures: int = 0
    timeouts: int = 0
    hedged_wins: int = 0  # Times hedged request finished first
    consecutive_successes: int = 0
    consecutive_failures: int = 0
    
    # Rolling window for success rate calculation
    recent_calls: deque = field(default_factory=lambda: deque(maxlen=100))
    
    def record_success(self):
        self.successes += 1
        self.consecutive_successes += 1
        self.consecutive_failures = 0
        self.recent_calls.append(True)
    
    def record_failure(self):
        self.failures += 1
        self.consecutive_failures += 1
        self.consecutive_successes = 0
        self.recent_calls.append(False)
    
    def record_timeout(self):
        self.timeouts += 1
        self.record_failure()
    
    def record_hedged_win(self):
        self.hedged_wins += 1
    
    @property
    def total_calls(self) -> int:
        return len(self.recent_calls)
    
    @property
    def failure_rate(self) -> float:
        if not self.recent_calls:
            return 0.0
        failures = sum(1 for success in self.recent_calls if not success)
        return failures / len(self.recent_calls)


class CircuitBreakerError(Exception):
    pass


class CircuitBreakerOpen(CircuitBreakerError):
    pass


class HedgedCircuitBreaker:
    def __init__(self, config: Optional[CircuitBreakerConfig] = None):
        self.config = config or CircuitBreakerConfig()
        self.state = CircuitState.CLOSED
        self.stats = CallStats()
        self.opened_at: Optional[float] = None
        self.half_open_calls = 0
        self.backoff_multiplier = 1
        
    def _calculate_backoff(self) -> float:
        """Calculate backoff with exponential increase and jitter."""
        backoff = min(
            self.config.base_backoff * (2 ** self.backoff_multiplier),
            self.config.max_backoff
        )
        
        # Add jitter: random value between (1-jitter) and (1+jitter)
        jitter_range = backoff * self.config.jitter_factor
        jitter = random.uniform(-jitter_range, jitter_range)
        
        return max(0.1, backoff + jitter)
    
    def _should_open(self) -> bool:
        """Check if circuit should open based on thresholds."""
        # Check consecutive failures
        if self.stats.consecutive_failures >= self.config.failure_threshold:
            return True
        
        # Check failure rate
        if self.stats.total_calls >= self.config.min_calls:
            if self.stats.failure_rate >= self.config.failure_rate_threshold:
                return True
        
        return False
    
    def _should_attempt_reset(self) -> bool:
        """Check if enough time has passed to try half-open state."""
        if self.opened_at is None:
            return False
        
        backoff = self._calculate_backoff()
        return (time.time() - self.opened_at) >= backoff
    
    def _transition_to_half_open(self):
        """Transition from OPEN to HALF_OPEN state."""
        logger.info("Circuit transitioning to HALF_OPEN")
        self.state = CircuitState.HALF_OPEN
        self.half_open_calls = 0
    
    def _open_circuit(self):
        """Open the circuit breaker."""
        if self.state != CircuitState.OPEN:
            logger.warning(
                f"Circuit OPENED after {self.stats.consecutive_failures} "
                f"consecutive failures (failure rate: {self.stats.failure_rate:.2%})"
            )
            self.state = CircuitState.OPEN
            self.opened_at = time.time()
            self.backoff_multiplier += 1
    
    def _close_circuit(self):
        """Close the circuit breaker."""
        logger.info(
            f"Circuit CLOSED after {self.stats.consecutive_successes} "
            "consecutive successes"
        )
        self.state = CircuitState.CLOSED
        self.opened_at = None
        self.backoff_multiplier = 1  # Reset backoff
        self.half_open_calls = 0
    
    async def _execute_with_timeout(
        self,
        func: Callable,
        *args,
        **kwargs
    ) -> Any:
        """Execute function with timeout."""
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(
                func(*args, **kwargs),
                timeout=self.config.timeout
            )
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            self.stats.record_timeout()
            raise
    
    async def _hedged_call(
        self,
        func: Callable,
        *args,
        **kwargs
    ) -> Any:
        """Execute call with hedging strategy."""
        tasks = []
        primary_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self._execute_with_timeout(func, *args, **kwargs)
        )
        tasks.append(('primary', primary_task))
        
        # Schedule hedged requests
        for i in range(self.config.max_hedged_requests):
            await asyncio.sleep(self.config.hedge_delay)
            
            # Check if primary already completed
            if primary_task.done():
                break
            
            hedged_task = asyncio.create_task(
                self._execute_with_timeout(func, *args, **kwargs)
            )
            tasks.append((f'hedge_{i+1}', hedged_task))
            logger.debug(f"Launched hedged request #{i+1}")
        
        # Wait for first successful completion
        try:
            while tasks:
                done, pending = await asyncio.wait(
                    [task for _, task in tasks],
                    return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
                )
                
                for completed_task in done:
                    # Find which task completed
                    task_name = next(
                        name for name, task in tasks 
                        if task == completed_task
                    )
                    
                    try:
                        result = await completed_task
                        
                        # Cancel remaining tasks
                        for _, pending_task in tasks:
                            if not pending_task.done():
                                pending_task.cancel()
                        
                        if task_name != 'primary':
                            self.stats.record_hedged_win()
                            logger.info(f"Hedged request won ({task_name})")
                        
                        return result
                    
                    except Exception as e:
                        # Remove failed task and continue
                        tasks = [(n, t) for n, t in tasks if t != completed_task]
                        
                        # If no tasks left, raise the last exception
                        if not tasks:
                            raise
            
        finally:
            # Cleanup: cancel any remaining tasks
            for _, task in tasks:
                if not task.done():
                    task.cancel()
                    try:
                        await task
                    except asyncio.CancelledError:
                        pass
    
    async def call(self, func: Callable, *args, **kwargs) -> Any:
        """
        Execute a call through the circuit breaker with hedging.
        
        Args:
            func: Async function to execute
            *args, **kwargs: Arguments to pass to func
            
        Returns:
            Result from the function call
            
        Raises:
            CircuitBreakerOpen: If circuit is open
            Any exception from the underlying function
        """
        # Check if circuit should transition from OPEN to HALF_OPEN
        if self.state == CircuitState.OPEN:
            if self._should_attempt_reset():
                self._transition_to_half_open()
            else:
                raise CircuitBreakerOpen(
                    f"Circuit breaker is OPEN. "
                    f"Retry after {self._calculate_backoff():.1f}s"
                )
        
        # In HALF_OPEN, limit number of test calls
        if self.state == CircuitState.HALF_OPEN:
            if self.half_open_calls >= self.config.half_open_max_calls:
                raise CircuitBreakerOpen(
                    "Circuit breaker is HALF_OPEN and test limit reached"
                )
            self.half_open_calls += 1
        
        try:
            # Execute with hedging
            result = await self._hedged_call(func, *args, **kwargs)
            
            # Record success
            self.stats.record_success()
            
            # Check if we should close the circuit
            if self.state == CircuitState.HALF_OPEN:
                if self.stats.consecutive_successes >= self.config.success_threshold:
                    self._close_circuit()
            
            return result
        
        except Exception as e:
            # Record failure
            self.stats.record_failure()
            
            # Check if we should open the circuit
            if self.state == CircuitState.CLOSED:
                if self._should_open():
                    self._open_circuit()
            
            # If in HALF_OPEN and failed, go back to OPEN
            elif self.state == CircuitState.HALF_OPEN:
                self._open_circuit()
            
            raise
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get current statistics."""
        return {
            'state': self.state.value,
            'successes': self.stats.successes,
            'failures': self.stats.failures,
            'timeouts': self.stats.timeouts,
            'hedged_wins': self.stats.hedged_wins,
            'consecutive_successes': self.stats.consecutive_successes,
            'consecutive_failures': self.stats.consecutive_failures,
            'failure_rate': f"{self.stats.failure_rate:.2%}",
            'total_calls': self.stats.total_calls,
            'backoff_multiplier': self.backoff_multiplier,
        }
    
    def reset(self):
        """Reset the circuit breaker to initial state."""
        self.state = CircuitState.CLOSED
        self.stats = CallStats()
        self.opened_at = None
        self.half_open_calls = 0
        self.backoff_multiplier = 1
        logger.info("Circuit breaker reset")


# Demo and testing
async def unreliable_service(
    call_id: int,
    fail_rate: float = 0.3,
    delay: float = 0.1
) -> str:
    """Simulate an unreliable service."""
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    
    if random.random() < fail_rate:
        raise Exception(f"Service failed for call {call_id}")
    
    return f"Success: {call_id}"


async def demo_basic_usage():
    """Demonstrate basic circuit breaker usage."""
    print("\n=== Basic Circuit Breaker Demo ===\n")
    
    config = CircuitBreakerConfig(
        failure_threshold=3,
        timeout=2.0,
        hedge_delay=0.5,
        max_hedged_requests=1,
    )
    
    breaker = HedgedCircuitBreaker(config)
    
    for i in range(20):
        try:
            # Adjust fail rate to simulate service degradation
            fail_rate = 0.7 if 5 <= i < 12 else 0.1
            
            result = await breaker.call(
                unreliable_service,
                call_id=i,
                fail_rate=fail_rate,
                delay=0.2
            )
            
            print(f"Call {i}: {result}")
        
        except CircuitBreakerOpen as e:
            print(f"Call {i}: Circuit breaker prevented call - {e}")
        
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Call {i}: Failed - {e}")
        
        # Show stats every 5 calls
        if (i + 1) % 5 == 0:
            print(f"\nStats: {breaker.get_stats()}\n")
        
        await asyncio.sleep(0.3)


async def demo_hedging():
    """Demonstrate hedging behavior."""
    print("\n=== Hedging Demo ===\n")
    
    async def slow_service(call_id: int) -> str:
        """Service with variable latency."""
        delay = random.uniform(0.5, 2.0)
        await asyncio.sleep(delay)
        return f"Completed {call_id} after {delay:.2f}s"
    
    config = CircuitBreakerConfig(
        hedge_delay=0.3,
        max_hedged_requests=2,
        timeout=3.0,
        failure_threshold=5,
    )
    
    breaker = HedgedCircuitBreaker(config)
    
    for i in range(5):
        start = time.time()
        try:
            result = await breaker.call(slow_service, call_id=i)
            elapsed = time.time() - start
            print(f"Call {i}: {result} (took {elapsed:.2f}s)")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Call {i}: Failed - {e}")
    
    print(f"\nHedged wins: {breaker.stats.hedged_wins}")


async def demo_recovery():
    """Demonstrate circuit recovery with jittered backoff."""
    print("\n=== Recovery Demo ===\n")
    
    # Simulate service that fails then recovers
    failure_window = set(range(5, 10))
    
    async def recovering_service(call_id: int) -> str:
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        if call_id in failure_window:
            raise Exception("Service degraded")
        return f"Success: {call_id}"
    
    config = CircuitBreakerConfig(
        failure_threshold=2,
        base_backoff=2.0,
        max_backoff=10.0,
        jitter_factor=0.3,
        success_threshold=3,
        open_duration=1.0,
    )
    
    breaker = HedgedCircuitBreaker(config)
    
    for i in range(20):
        try:
            result = await breaker.call(recovering_service, call_id=i)
            print(f"✓ Call {i}: {result}")
        
        except CircuitBreakerOpen:
            print(f"✗ Call {i}: Circuit OPEN")
        
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"✗ Call {i}: {e}")
        
        print(f"  State: {breaker.state.value}, "
              f"Consecutive failures: {breaker.stats.consecutive_failures}")
        
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    
    print(f"\nFinal stats: {breaker.get_stats()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(demo_basic_usage())
    asyncio.run(demo_hedging())
    asyncio.run(demo_recovery())
```

## Key Features

### 1. **State Management**
- CLOSED → OPEN → HALF_OPEN → CLOSED cycle
- Configurable thresholds for transitions

### 2. **Hedging Strategy**
- Launches backup requests after delay
- Cancels slower requests
- Tracks hedge win rate

### 3. **Jittered Backoff**
- Exponential backoff with randomization
- Prevents thundering herd
- Configurable min/max bounds

### 4. **Success Sampling**
- Rolling window for failure rate
- Tracks consecutive successes/failures
- Configurable sample sizes

## Configuration Options

```python
config = CircuitBreakerConfig(
    # When to open
    failure_threshold=5,        # Consecutive failures
    failure_rate_threshold=0.5, # 50% failure rate
    min_calls=10,               # Min sample size
    
    # Hedging
    hedge_delay=1.0,           # Delay before hedge
    max_hedged_requests=2,     # Max concurrent hedges

```python
# Flink/Spark Structured Streaming Example
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

class CDCOrderingProcessor:
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("CDC-Ordering") \
            .config("spark.sql.streaming.statefulOperator.checkCorrectness.enabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
    
    def process_stream(self, kafka_stream):
        """
        Process CDC events with ordering guarantees
        """
        # Parse CDC events
        parsed_df = kafka_stream.select(
            col("key").cast("string").alias("record_key"),
            from_json(col("value").cast("string"), self.get_schema()).alias("data"),
            col("partition"),
            col("offset"),
            col("timestamp")
        )
        
        # Extract ordering fields
        ordered_df = parsed_df.select(
            col("data.payload.after.*"),
            col("data.payload.source.table").alias("table_name"),
            col("data.payload.source.ts_ms").alias("source_ts"),
            col("data.payload.source.lsn").alias("lsn"),  # PostgreSQL
            col("data.payload.source.pos").alias("binlog_pos"),  # MySQL
            col("data.payload.source.txId").alias("tx_id"),
            col("data.payload.transaction.total_order").alias("tx_order"),
            col("data.payload.op").alias("operation"),
            col("partition"),
            col("offset"),
            col("timestamp").alias("kafka_ts")
        )
        
        # Deduplicate within micro-batch using window functions
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("table_name", "id") \
            .orderBy(
                col("source_ts").desc(),
                col("lsn").desc_nulls_last(),
                col("binlog_pos").desc_nulls_last(),
                col("tx_order").desc_nulls_last(),
                col("kafka_ts").desc()
            )
        
        deduped_df = ordered_df \
            .withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
            .filter(col("row_num") == 1) \
            .drop("row_num")
        
        return deduped_df

    def stateful_deduplication(self, df):
        """
        Stateful deduplication across batches using watermarks
        """
        return df \
            .withWatermark("kafka_ts", "10 minutes") \
            .dropDuplicates([
                "table_name", "id", "source_ts", "lsn", "tx_id"
            ])
```
